````rust
  1: //! Assembly-derived Red Room encounter planning.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room is not a macro-lattice shape. It inherits a real assembly's
  4: //! footprint and entrance, then adds stable semantic crossing planes.
  5: 
  6: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  7:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, AxisDirection, OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, QuarterTurn,
  8:     TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
  9: };
 10: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::AssemblyInstance;
 11: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 12: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{SNAP, mix64, stable_id};
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: 
 15: const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
 16: const THRESHOLD_DEPTH: f32 = 2.8;
 17: const LOOP_GATE_DEPTH: f32 = 6.0;
 18: 
 19: fn clamp_inward(desired: f32, far_inner_plane: f32, direction: AxisDirection) -> f32 {
 20:     match direction {
 21:         AxisDirection::Positive => desired.min(far_inner_plane),
 22:         AxisDirection::Negative => desired.max(far_inner_plane),
 23:     }
 24: }
 25: 
 26: fn red_room_instance(
 27:     seed: u32,
 28:     region_origin: Position,
 29:     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
 30: ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
 31:     let entrance = *assembly.entrances.first()?;
 32:     let bounds = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 33:     let center = Position::new((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
 34:     let region_x = (region_origin.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 35:     let region_z = (region_origin.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 36:     let id = mix64(
 37:         stable_id(seed, AnomalyKind::RedRoom, region_x, region_z)
 38:             ^ (assembly.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
 39:     );
 40:     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
 41:         center,
 42:         half_x: (bounds.2 - bounds.0) * 0.5,
 43:         half_z: (bounds.3 - bounds.1) * 0.5,
 44:         basis: OrthoBasis {
 45:             turn: QuarterTurn::Zero,
 46:         },
 47:     };
 48:     let axis = if entrance.through_x_wall {
 49:         Axis2::Z
 50:     } else {
 51:         Axis2::X
 52:     };
 53:     let (edge_coordinate, center_coordinate, half_depth) = match axis {
 54:         Axis2::X => (entrance.center.x, center.x, footprint.half_x),
 55:         Axis2::Z => (entrance.center.z, center.z, footprint.half_z),
 56:     };
 57:     let forward = if center_coordinate >= edge_coordinate {
 58:         AxisDirection::Positive
 59:     } else {
 60:         AxisDirection::Negative
 61:     };
 62: 
 63:     // Commitment happens inside the room, beyond the externally readable
 64:     // doorway. Entrance placement guarantees enough depth for this vestibule.
 65:     let threshold_plane = edge_coordinate + forward.sign() * THRESHOLD_DEPTH;
 66:     let (span_min, span_max) = if axis == Axis2::Z {
 67:         (
 68:             entrance.center.x - entrance.width * 0.5,
 69:             entrance.center.x + entrance.width * 0.5,
 70:         )
 71:     } else {
 72:         (
 73:             entrance.center.z - entrance.width * 0.5,
 74:             entrance.center.z + entrance.width * 0.5,
 75:         )
 76:     };
 77:     let affected_bounds = footprint.bounds();
 78:     let threshold_gate = TraversalGate {
 79:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x6A7E_0ED0),
 80:         instance_id: id,
 81:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
 82:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
 83:         axis,
 84:         plane: threshold_plane,
 85:         span_min,
 86:         span_max,
 87:         forward,
 88:         affected_bounds,
 89:     };
 90: 
 91:     // The loop checkpoint is six units beyond commitment when the room has
 92:     // that depth. Shallow rooms clamp it one plan voxel inside the far wall,
 93:     // keeping the semantic crossing on geometry owned by this encounter.
 94:     let far_inner_plane = center_coordinate + forward.sign() * (half_depth - SNAP).max(0.0);
 95:     let loop_plane = clamp_inward(
 96:         threshold_plane + forward.sign() * LOOP_GATE_DEPTH,
 97:         far_inner_plane,
 98:         forward,
 99:     );
100:     let loop_gate = TraversalGate {
101:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x9B4C_1A2F),
102:         instance_id: id,
103:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
104:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
105:         axis,
106:         plane: loop_plane,
107:         span_min,
108:         span_max,
109:         // `forward` records the authored inward direction. Runtime state owns
110:         // the separate policy for which traversal directions advance a loop.
111:         forward,
112:         affected_bounds,
113:     };
114: 
115:     Some(AnomalyInstance {
116:         id,
117:         kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
118:         footprint,
119:         basis: footprint.basis,
120:         macro_anchor: (region_x, region_z),
121:         pillar_lattice: None,
122:         pit_lattice: None,
123:         arch: None,
124:         gates: vec![threshold_gate, loop_gate],
125:         skeleton_half_width: 1.0,
126:         entry_band: THRESHOLD_DEPTH,
127:     })
128: }
129: 
130: pub(crate) fn plan_red_rooms(
131:     seed: u32,
132:     region_origin: Position,
133:     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
134:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
135: ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
136:     let forced = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
137:     let organic_enabled = config.anomalies.frequency > 0.0 && config.anomalies.red_rooms > 0.0;
138:     if !forced && !organic_enabled {
139:         return Vec::new();
140:     }
141: 
142:     assemblies
143:         .iter()
144:         .filter(|assembly| assembly.corruption.red_room)
145:         .filter_map(|assembly| red_room_instance(seed, region_origin, assembly))
146:         .collect()
147: }
148: 
149: #[cfg(test)]
150: mod tests {
151:     use super::*;
152:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
153:         CorruptionProfile, Opening, Polygon2, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystem,
154:         StructuralSystemInstance,
155:     };
156: 
157:     fn red_assembly(entrance_z: f32) -> AssemblyInstance {
158:         AssemblyInstance {
159:             id: 7,
160:             program: SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
161:             footprint: Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 12.0, 8.0),
162:             entrances: vec![Opening {
163:                 center: Position::new(6.0, entrance_z),
164:                 width: 1.2,
165:                 through_x_wall: true,
166:                 lintel_units: Some(2.2),
167:             }],
168:             spaces: Vec::new(),
169:             structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
170:                 system: StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
171:                 bay_x: 4.0,
172:                 bay_z: 4.0,
173:                 phase: (0.0, 0.0),
174:                 column_side: 0.4,
175:             },
176:             ceiling_zones: Vec::new(),
177:             fixtures: Vec::new(),
178:             service_voids: Vec::new(),
179:             corruption: CorruptionProfile {
180:                 red_room: true,
181:                 ..CorruptionProfile::default()
182:             },
183:         }
184:     }
185: 
186:     #[test]
187:     fn forced_red_room_survives_zero_frequency_and_zero_family_weight() {
188:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
189:         config.anomalies.frequency = 0.0;
190:         config.anomalies.red_rooms = 0.0;
191:         config.anomalies.forced_kind = Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
192:         let rooms = plan_red_rooms(42, Position::new(0.0, 0.0), &[red_assembly(0.0)], &config);
193:         assert_eq!(rooms.len(), 1);
194:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].kind, AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
195:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].gates.len(), 2);
196:     }
197: 
198:     #[test]
199:     fn loop_gate_is_inside_both_entrance_orientations() {
200:         let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
201:         for entrance_z in [0.0, 8.0] {
202:             let room = plan_red_rooms(
203:                 42,
204:                 Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
205:                 &[red_assembly(entrance_z)],
206:                 &config,
207:             )
208:             .pop()
209:             .unwrap();
210:             let loop_gate = room
211:                 .gates
212:                 .iter()
213:                 .find(|gate| gate.kind == TraversalGateKind::RedLoop)
214:                 .unwrap();
215:             let bounds = room.footprint.bounds();
216:             assert!(loop_gate.plane >= bounds.min_z + SNAP - f32::EPSILON);
217:             assert!(loop_gate.plane <= bounds.max_z - SNAP + f32::EPSILON);
218:         }
219:     }
220: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/recursive_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Addressing for the Level 0 world reached through a committed Red Room.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room does not invent a second procedural grammar.  It addresses a
  4: //! distant, deterministic copy of Level 0 and changes its presentation.  The
  5: //! address must therefore be stable across chunk order and worker boundaries,
  6: //! while retaining all 64 bits of anomaly identity until hashing is complete.
  7: //! Converting an `AnomalyId` directly to `f32` loses most of those bits and can
  8: //! make distinct rooms share a world; this module derives integer region
  9: //! coordinates first and converts only the small final translation.
 10: 
 11: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
 12:     AnomalyId, AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, PitHazard, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase, TraversalGate,
 13:     WorldBounds,
 14: };
 15: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
 19: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
 20: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 21: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 22: 
 23: const ADDRESS_DOMAIN: u64 = 0x5245_4452_4F4F_4D00; // "REDROOM\0"
 24: // Keep translated coordinates near enough to the origin that f32 retains
 25: // sub-centimetre detail for future fine voxel requests. Branch uniqueness is
 26: // carried by the derived seed, so the translation itself need not be huge.
 27: const MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS: i64 = 64;
 28: const TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN: u64 = 192;
 29: 
 30: /// Stable procedural address of the recursive Level 0 associated with one
 31: /// Red Room instance.
 32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
 33: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelAddress {
 34:     instance_id: AnomalyId,
 35:     derived_seed: u32,
 36:     translation_regions: (i64, i64),
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// The finite planning window needed to render one request into a recursive
 40: /// Level 0 branch.  The branch remains infinite; this value is only its local
 41: /// query cache, just like an ordinary chunk's region window.
 42: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelWindow {
 43:     address: RecursiveLevelAddress,
 44:     seed: u32,
 45:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 46:     regions: InfiniteRegionWindow,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: impl RecursiveLevelWindow {
 50:     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 51:         source_origin: Position,
 52:         chunk_size: f32,
 53:         halo: f32,
 54:         world_seed: u32,
 55:         base_config: GeneratorConfig,
 56:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 57:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 58:     ) -> Option<Self> {
 59:         let (address, _) = RecursiveLevelAddress::from_reality(world_seed, reality)?;
 60:         let seed = address.derived_seed();
 61:         let config = address.recursive_config(base_config);
 62:         let recursive_origin = address.to_recursive_world(source_origin);
 63:         let regions = InfiniteRegionWindow::around_chunk(
 64:             recursive_origin,
 65:             chunk_size,
 66:             halo,
 67:             seed,
 68:             &config,
 69:             noise,
 70:         );
 71:         Some(Self {
 72:             address,
 73:             seed,
 74:             config,
 75:             regions,
 76:         })
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     pub(crate) fn seed(&self) -> u32 {
 80:         self.seed
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     pub(crate) fn instance_id(&self) -> AnomalyId {
 84:         self.address.instance_id
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     pub(crate) fn config(&self) -> &GeneratorConfig {
 88:         &self.config
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /// Returns both the recursive coordinate and the plan that owns it.
 92:     /// Keeping them paired prevents the old failure where a recursive plan
 93:     /// was sampled with the base world's seed and coordinates.
 94:     pub(crate) fn plan_at(&self, source: Position) -> Option<(Position, &RegionPlan)> {
 95:         let recursive = self.address.to_recursive_world(source);
 96:         self.regions
 97:             .plan_at(recursive)
 98:             .map(|plan| (recursive, plan))
 99:     }
100: 
101:     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
102:         self.regions.iter()
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// Project a semantic gate authored in the recursive branch back into
106:     /// the player's visible coordinate frame.
107:     pub(crate) fn project_gate(&self, mut gate: TraversalGate) -> TraversalGate {
108:         let offset = self.address.translation_world();
109:         match gate.axis {
110:             Axis2::X => {
111:                 gate.plane -= offset.x;
112:                 gate.span_min -= offset.z;
113:                 gate.span_max -= offset.z;
114:             }
115:             Axis2::Z => {
116:                 gate.plane -= offset.z;
117:                 gate.span_min -= offset.x;
118:                 gate.span_max -= offset.x;
119:             }
120:         }
121:         gate.affected_bounds = self.project_bounds(gate.affected_bounds);
122:         gate
123:     }
124: 
125:     pub(crate) fn project_hazard(&self, mut hazard: PitHazard) -> PitHazard {
126:         hazard.center = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.center);
127:         hazard.recovery = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.recovery);
128:         hazard
129:     }
130: 
131:     pub(crate) fn project_position(&self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
132:         self.address.to_source_world(recursive)
133:     }
134: 
135:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
136:         let min = self
137:             .address
138:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
139:         let max = self
140:             .address
141:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
142:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
143:     }
144: 
145:     fn project_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
146:         let min = self
147:             .address
148:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
149:         let max = self
150:             .address
151:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
152:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
153:     }
154: }
155: 
156: impl RecursiveLevelAddress {
157:     /// Derives an address using integer avalanche hashes only.  Both halves of
158:     /// the 64-bit instance id participate in the seed and in each axis.
159:     pub(crate) fn derive(world_seed: u32, instance_id: AnomalyId) -> Self {
160:         let root = mix64(
161:             ADDRESS_DOMAIN ^ instance_id ^ (world_seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15),
162:         );
163:         let seed_hash = mix64(root ^ 0x5EED_5EED_A11C_0DE5);
164:         let derived_seed = (seed_hash as u32) ^ ((seed_hash >> 32) as u32);
165:         let translation_regions = (
166:             translation_component(root, 0x5841_5849_5300_0001),
167:             translation_component(root, 0x5A41_5849_5300_0002),
168:         );
169: 
170:         Self {
171:             instance_id,
172:             derived_seed,
173:             translation_regions,
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// Selects the committed Red Room represented by a canonical reality
178:     /// snapshot, then derives its recursive address.
179:     pub(crate) fn from_reality(
180:         world_seed: u32,
181:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
182:     ) -> Option<(Self, &AnomalyStateStamp)> {
183:         let state = active_red_room(reality)?;
184:         Some((Self::derive(world_seed, state.instance_id), state))
185:     }
186: 
187:     pub(crate) fn derived_seed(self) -> u32 {
188:         self.derived_seed
189:     }
190: 
191:     pub(crate) fn translation_regions(self) -> (i64, i64) {
192:         self.translation_regions
193:     }
194: 
195:     /// Exact transform for region keys.  Planning should prefer this form so
196:     /// large-world floating-point precision never participates in identity.
197:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_region(self, source_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
198:         (
199:             source_region.0.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.0),
200:             source_region.1.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.1),
201:         )
202:     }
203: 
204:     pub(crate) fn to_source_region(self, recursive_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
205:         (
206:             recursive_region
207:                 .0
208:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.0),
209:             recursive_region
210:                 .1
211:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.1),
212:         )
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// World-space form used by column sampling.  The translation is an exact
216:     /// multiple of the 80u region lattice, preserving portals and 0.4u plan
217:     /// geometry across every chunk and LOD.
218:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_world(self, source: Position) -> Position {
219:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(source);
220:         let recursive = self.to_recursive_region(region);
221:         join_world_position(recursive, local)
222:     }
223: 
224:     pub(crate) fn to_source_world(self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
225:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(recursive);
226:         let source = self.to_source_region(region);
227:         join_world_position(source, local)
228:     }
229: 
230:     pub(crate) fn translation_world(self) -> Position {
231:         let translation = self.translation_regions();
232:         Position::new(
233:             translation.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
234:             translation.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
235:         )
236:     }
237: 
238:     /// Produces a Level 0 config for the addressed world.  Organic anomaly
239:     /// tuning is preserved, allowing recursive Level 0 to remain the complete
240:     /// generator; only the one-shot debug override is cleared so it cannot be
241:     /// cloned into every recursive address.
242:     pub(crate) fn recursive_config(self, mut base: GeneratorConfig) -> GeneratorConfig {
243:         base.level = LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
244:         base.anomalies.forced_kind = None;
245:         base
246:     }
247: }
248: 
249: /// Chooses one committed Red Room without depending on snapshot insertion
250: /// order.  Under the current state machine, only red thresholds can produce a
251: /// non-`Outside` phase.  Progress is compared explicitly because `epoch` is
252: /// the best available recency signal; stable identity is the final tie-break.
253: pub(crate) fn active_red_room(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Option<&AnomalyStateStamp> {
254:     reality
255:         .stamps()
256:         .iter()
257:         .filter(|state| state.phase != RedRoomPhase::Outside)
258:         .max_by_key(|state| {
259:             (
260:                 state.epoch,
261:                 state.phase,
262:                 state.loop_count,
263:                 state.last_gate_id,
264:                 state.instance_id,
265:             )
266:         })
267: }
268: 
269: fn translation_component(root: u64, axis_domain: u64) -> i64 {
270:     let hash = mix64(root ^ axis_domain);
271:     let magnitude = MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS + (hash % TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN) as i64;
272:     if hash & (1 << 63) == 0 {
273:         magnitude
274:     } else {
275:         -magnitude
276:     }
277: }
278: 
279: fn split_world_position(position: Position) -> ((i64, i64), (f32, f32)) {
280:     let region = (
281:         (position.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
282:         (position.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
283:     );
284:     let local = (
285:         position.x - region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
286:         position.z - region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
287:     );
288:     (region, local)
289: }
290: 
291: fn join_world_position(region: (i64, i64), local: (f32, f32)) -> Position {
292:     Position::new(
293:         region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.0,
294:         region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.1,
295:     )
296: }
297: 
298: fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
299:     value ^= value >> 30;
300:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
301:     value ^= value >> 27;
302:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
303:     value ^ (value >> 31)
304: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Deterministic access to the finite window of an infinite planned level.
  2: //!
  3: //! Chunk generation is local, but Level 0 architecture is not: a chunk may
  4: //! sample corridors, assemblies, or anomaly footprints planned by any region
  5: //! that overlaps its voxel halo.  This module makes that query explicit.  The
  6: //! window owns a stable, row-major set of region plans and is otherwise just a
  7: //! world-point-to-plan lookup; callers do not need to reproduce region-range
  8: //! arithmetic or fall back to an unrelated plan when a lookup misses.
  9: 
 10: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::WorldBounds;
 11: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 12: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 15: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan, region_index};
 16: 
 17: /// The region plans needed to sample one bounded area of an infinite level.
 18: ///
 19: /// Plans are stored in `(z, x)` row-major order.  That order is deliberately
 20: /// independent of hash maps and request timing, so planning the same area is
 21: /// replayable on the main thread, in a worker, or during a test.
 22: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
 23: pub(crate) struct InfiniteRegionWindow {
 24:     min_region_x: i64,
 25:     min_region_z: i64,
 26:     max_region_x: i64,
 27:     max_region_z: i64,
 28:     plans: Vec<RegionPlan>,
 29: }
 30: 
 31: impl InfiniteRegionWindow {
 32:     /// Plans every region touched by `area` after expanding it by `halo` world
 33:     /// units.  Boundary-touching regions are included intentionally: a voxel
 34:     /// sampler may ask about the exact far edge while constructing skirts,
 35:     /// meshes, or collision data.
 36:     pub(crate) fn covering(
 37:         area: WorldBounds,
 38:         halo: f32,
 39:         seed: u32,
 40:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 41:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 42:     ) -> Self {
 43:         assert!(
 44:             halo.is_finite() && halo >= 0.0,
 45:             "region-window halo must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
 46:         );
 47:         let area = area.expanded(halo);
 48:         assert!(
 49:             [area.min_x, area.min_z, area.max_x, area.max_z]
 50:                 .into_iter()
 51:                 .all(f32::is_finite),
 52:             "an infinite-region window requires finite world bounds"
 53:         );
 54: 
 55:         let min_region_x = region_index(area.min_x);
 56:         let min_region_z = region_index(area.min_z);
 57:         let max_region_x = region_index(area.max_x);
 58:         let max_region_z = region_index(area.max_z);
 59:         let width = region_count(min_region_x, max_region_x);
 60:         let height = region_count(min_region_z, max_region_z);
 61:         let capacity = width
 62:             .checked_mul(height)
 63:             .expect("requested region window is too large to address");
 64:         let mut plans = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);
 65: 
 66:         for region_z in min_region_z..=max_region_z {
 67:             for region_x in min_region_x..=max_region_x {
 68:                 plans.push(generate_region_plan(
 69:                     seed,
 70:                     region_origin(region_x, region_z),
 71:                     REGION_SIZE,
 72:                     config,
 73:                     noise,
 74:                 ));
 75:             }
 76:         }
 77: 
 78:         Self {
 79:             min_region_x,
 80:             min_region_z,
 81:             max_region_x,
 82:             max_region_z,
 83:             plans,
 84:         }
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     /// Convenience constructor for the common chunk-plus-voxel-halo query.
 88:     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 89:         chunk_origin: Position,
 90:         chunk_size: f32,
 91:         halo: f32,
 92:         seed: u32,
 93:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 94:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 95:     ) -> Self {
 96:         assert!(
 97:             chunk_size.is_finite() && chunk_size >= 0.0,
 98:             "chunk size must be a finite, non-negative world distance"
 99:         );
100:         Self::covering(
101:             WorldBounds::new(
102:                 chunk_origin.x,
103:                 chunk_origin.z,
104:                 chunk_origin.x + chunk_size,
105:                 chunk_origin.z + chunk_size,
106:             ),
107:             halo,
108:             seed,
109:             config,
110:             noise,
111:         )
112:     }
113: 
114:     /// Returns the authoritative plan for a world point, or `None` when the
115:     /// caller sampled beyond the area/halo declared at construction time.
116:     pub(crate) fn plan_at(&self, world: Position) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
117:         self.plan_for_region(region_index(world.x), region_index(world.z))
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub(crate) fn plan_for_region(&self, region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
121:         if region_x < self.min_region_x
122:             || region_x > self.max_region_x
123:             || region_z < self.min_region_z
124:             || region_z > self.max_region_z
125:         {
126:             return None;
127:         }
128: 
129:         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
130:         let local_x = usize::try_from(region_x - self.min_region_x).ok()?;
131:         let local_z = usize::try_from(region_z - self.min_region_z).ok()?;
132:         self.plans
133:             .get(local_z.saturating_mul(width).saturating_add(local_x))
134:     }
135: 
136:     #[cfg(test)]
137:     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
138:         self.plans.len()
139:     }
140: 
141:     #[cfg(test)]
142:     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
143:         self.plans.is_empty()
144:     }
145: 
146:     /// Stable row-major iteration for semantic export and deterministic tests.
147:     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
148:         let width = region_count(self.min_region_x, self.max_region_x);
149:         self.plans.iter().enumerate().map(move |(index, plan)| {
150:             let local_z = index / width;
151:             let local_x = index % width;
152:             (
153:                 (
154:                     self.min_region_x + local_x as i64,
155:                     self.min_region_z + local_z as i64,
156:                 ),
157:                 plan,
158:             )
159:         })
160:     }
161: }
162: 
163: fn region_count(first: i64, last: i64) -> usize {
164:     let count = last
165:         .checked_sub(first)
166:         .and_then(|distance| distance.checked_add(1))
167:         .expect("requested region window exceeds integer address space");
168:     usize::try_from(count).expect("requested region window exceeds platform address space")
169: }
170: 
171: fn region_origin(region_x: i64, region_z: i64) -> Position {
172:     Position::new(region_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE, region_z as f32 * REGION_SIZE)
173: }
174:
````

````typescript
 27: async function renderedImageStats(page: import('@playwright/test').Page) {
 28:   const png = await page.locator('#view').screenshot();
 29:   const dataUrl = `data:image/png;base64,${png.toString('base64')}`;
 30: 
 31:   return page.evaluate(async encodedImage => {
 32:     const response = await fetch(encodedImage);
 33:     const bitmap = await createImageBitmap(await response.blob());
 34:     const sample = document.createElement('canvas');
 35:     sample.width = 64;
 36:     sample.height = 48;
 37:     const context = sample.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true });
 38:     if (!context) throw new Error('2D screenshot probe is unavailable');
 39:     context.drawImage(bitmap, 0, 0, sample.width, sample.height);
 40: 
 41:     const pixels = context.getImageData(0, 0, sample.width, sample.height).data;
 42:     const colors = new Set<number>();
 43:     let darkest = 255;
 44:     let brightest = 0;
 45:     for (let i = 0; i < pixels.length; i += 4) {
 46:       const red = pixels[i];
 47:       const green = pixels[i + 1];
 48:       const blue = pixels[i + 2];
 49:       const luminance = Math.round(red * 0.2126 + green * 0.7152 + blue * 0.0722);
 50:       darkest = Math.min(darkest, luminance);
 51:       brightest = Math.max(brightest, luminance);
 52:       colors.add(((red >> 4) << 8) | ((green >> 4) << 4) | (blue >> 4));
 53:     }
 54:     bitmap.close();
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/target.rs
````rust
  1: //! Framebuffer, depth buffer, and conservative hierarchical-Z storage.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module knows only pixels. Traversal decides *what* to draw and owns
  4: //! frame policy; the target clips a square splat, performs fine depth tests,
  5: //! enforces the caller's remaining write budget exactly, and maintains the
  6: //! coarse occlusion summary when requested.
  7: 
  8: /// Coarse hierarchical-Z tile edge in pixels.
  9: const COARSE_TILE: usize = 8;
 10: 
 11: /// One depth-tested square request in target coordinates.
 12: pub(super) struct SquareSplat {
 13:     center: [f32; 2],
 14:     half: f32,
 15:     depth: f32,
 16:     color: [u8; 3],
 17: }
 18: 
 19: impl SquareSplat {
 20:     pub(super) fn new(cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, depth: f32, color: [u8; 3]) -> Self {
 21:         Self {
 22:             center: [cx, cy],
 23:             half,
 24:             depth,
 25:             color,
 26:         }
 27:     }
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// Result of one square-splat write.
 31: pub(super) struct SplatWrite {
 32:     /// Fine-depth-tested pixels whose color and depth changed.
 33:     pub(super) pixel_writes: usize,
 34:     /// A further depth-passing pixel existed after the write budget ran out.
 35:     pub(super) budget_exhausted: bool,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: /// Reusable CPU render target. Infinity in `depth` means an uncovered pixel;
 39: /// infinity in `coarse_depth` therefore means the tile is not fully covered.
 40: pub(super) struct RenderTarget {
 41:     width: usize,
 42:     height: usize,
 43:     rgba: Vec<u8>,
 44:     depth: Vec<f32>,
 45:     /// Farthest fine depth in each fully covered tile.
 46:     coarse_depth: Vec<f32>,
 47:     /// Number of pixels that have transitioned from uncovered to covered.
 48:     coarse_filled: Vec<usize>,
 49:     coarse_width: usize,
 50:     coarse_height: usize,
 51: }
 52: 
 53: impl RenderTarget {
 54:     pub(super) fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {
 55:         let mut target = Self {
 56:             width: 0,
 57:             height: 0,
 58:             rgba: Vec::new(),
 59:             depth: Vec::new(),
 60:             coarse_depth: Vec::new(),
 61:             coarse_filled: Vec::new(),
 62:             coarse_width: 0,
 63:             coarse_height: 0,
 64:         };
 65:         target.resize(width, height);
 66:         target
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     pub(super) fn resize(&mut self, width: usize, height: usize) {
 70:         self.width = width.max(1);
 71:         self.height = height.max(1);
 72:         self.rgba = vec![0; self.width * self.height * 4];
 73:         self.depth = vec![f32::INFINITY; self.width * self.height];
 74:         self.coarse_width = self.width.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);
 75:         self.coarse_height = self.height.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);
 76:         self.coarse_depth = vec![f32::INFINITY; self.coarse_width * self.coarse_height];
 77:         self.coarse_filled = vec![0; self.coarse_width * self.coarse_height];
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     pub(super) fn width(&self) -> usize {
 81:         self.width
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     pub(super) fn height(&self) -> usize {
 85:         self.height
 86:     }
 87: 
 88:     pub(super) fn rgba(&self) -> &[u8] {
 89:         &self.rgba
 90:     }
 91: 
 92:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self, background: [u8; 3]) {
 93:         for pixel in self.rgba.chunks_exact_mut(4) {
 94:             pixel[0] = background[0];
 95:             pixel[1] = background[1];
 96:             pixel[2] = background[2];
 97:             pixel[3] = 255;
 98:         }
 99:         self.depth.fill(f32::INFINITY);
100:         self.coarse_depth.fill(f32::INFINITY);
101:         self.coarse_filled.fill(0);
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// Fills a depth-tested square. `half` is its half-extent in pixels.
105:     ///
106:     /// The budget check lives inside the depth-passing branch: rejected
107:     /// pixels cost no writes, while the first additional visible pixel after
108:     /// the budget is exhausted stops the splat and reports exhaustion.
109:     pub(super) fn write_splat(
110:         &mut self,
111:         splat: SquareSplat,
112:         write_budget: usize,
113:         maintain_coarse: bool,
114:     ) -> SplatWrite {
115:         // Anything larger should have been subdivided; the cap also prevents
116:         // malformed input from filling an unbounded target area in one call.
117:         let half = splat.half.min(32.0);
118:         let x0 = (splat.center[0] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize;
119:         let x1 = ((splat.center[0] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.width);
120:         let y0 = (splat.center[1] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize;
121:         let y1 = ((splat.center[1] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.height);
122: 
123:         let mut pixel_writes = 0;
124:         let mut budget_exhausted = false;
125:         'pixels: for y in y0..y1 {
126:             let row = y * self.width;
127:             for x in x0..x1 {
128:                 let idx = row + x;
129:                 if splat.depth < self.depth[idx] {
130:                     if pixel_writes >= write_budget {
131:                         budget_exhausted = true;
132:                         break 'pixels;
133:                     }
134:                     let was_uncovered = self.depth[idx] == f32::INFINITY;
135:                     self.depth[idx] = splat.depth;
136:                     let rgba_index = idx * 4;
137:                     self.rgba[rgba_index] = splat.color[0];
138:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 1] = splat.color[1];
139:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 2] = splat.color[2];
140:                     pixel_writes += 1;
141:                     if maintain_coarse && was_uncovered {
142:                         self.record_first_coverage(x, y);
143:                     }
144:                 }
145:             }
146:         }
147: 
148:         SplatWrite {
149:             pixel_writes,
150:             budget_exhausted,
151:         }
152:     }
153: 
154:     /// True only when every coarse tile under the screen rect is fully
155:     /// covered and its farthest stored pixel is nearer than `z_near`.
156:     pub(super) fn coarse_occludes(&self, px: f32, py: f32, proj_radius: f32, z_near: f32) -> bool {
157:         let clamp_tile = |value: f32, tiles: usize| {
158:             ((value.max(0.0) as usize) / COARSE_TILE).min(tiles.saturating_sub(1))
159:         };
160:         let x0 = clamp_tile((px - proj_radius).floor(), self.coarse_width);
161:         let x1 = clamp_tile((px + proj_radius).ceil(), self.coarse_width);
162:         let y0 = clamp_tile((py - proj_radius).floor(), self.coarse_height);
163:         let y1 = clamp_tile((py + proj_radius).ceil(), self.coarse_height);
164: 
165:         for tile_y in y0..=y1 {
166:             for tile_x in x0..=x1 {
167:                 if z_near <= self.coarse_depth[tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x] {
168:                     return false;
169:                 }
170:             }
171:         }
172:         true
173:     }
174: 
175:     /// Records an infinity-to-finite transition. A tile is scanned exactly
176:     /// once, when its final uncovered pixel becomes covered. Later depth
177:     /// writes only decrease values, so the stored maximum becomes a stale
178:     /// upper bound: conservative for rejection and free to maintain.
179:     fn record_first_coverage(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize) {
180:         let tile_x = x / COARSE_TILE;
181:         let tile_y = y / COARSE_TILE;
182:         let tile_index = tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x;
183:         self.coarse_filled[tile_index] += 1;
184:         if self.coarse_filled[tile_index] == self.tile_pixel_count(tile_x, tile_y) {
185:             self.coarse_depth[tile_index] = self.scan_tile_farthest(tile_x, tile_y);
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:     fn tile_pixel_count(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> usize {
190:         let width = ((tile_x + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.width) - tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
191:         let height = ((tile_y + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.height) - tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
192:         width * height
193:     }
194: 
195:     fn scan_tile_farthest(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> f32 {
196:         let x0 = tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
197:         let x1 = (x0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.width);
198:         let y0 = tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
199:         let y1 = (y0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.height);
200:         let mut farthest = 0.0f32;
201:         for y in y0..y1 {
202:             for x in x0..x1 {
203:                 farthest = farthest.max(self.depth[y * self.width + x]);
204:             }
205:         }
206:         farthest
207:     }
208: }
209: 
210: #[cfg(test)]
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/traversal.rs
````rust
  1: //! Primary SVO traversal, projection, LOD selection, and virtual subdivision.
  2: //!
  3: //! `render_node` is deliberately a short dispatcher. Projection, atlas
  4: //! decoding, budget fallback, leaf handling, interior handling, MIP drawing,
  5: //! and child ordering each live in a small helper with an explicit data type.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
  8: 
  9: use super::super::atlas::{VOXEL_AIR, decode_node, is_emissive};
 10: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 11: use super::{MAX_VISITED_NODES, SoftwareRasterizer};
 12: 
 13: /// Attributes carried by a real atlas leaf or a virtually subdivided leaf.
 14: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 15: struct LeafPayload {
 16:     voxel_type: u32,
 17:     color: [f32; 3],
 18:     light: f32,
 19: }
 20: 
 21: /// Everything needed to visit one real or virtual node.
 22: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 23: struct NodeVisit {
 24:     node_idx: usize,
 25:     min: [f32; 3],
 26:     size: f32,
 27:     crowded_siblings: u32,
 28:     virtual_leaf: Option<LeafPayload>,
 29:     virtual_depth: usize,
 30: }
 31: 
 32: impl NodeVisit {
 33:     fn root(chunk: &ChunkDraw) -> Self {
 34:         Self {
 35:             node_idx: chunk.root_index as usize,
 36:             min: chunk.origin,
 37:             size: chunk.world_size,
 38:             crowded_siblings: 1,
 39:             virtual_leaf: None,
 40:             virtual_depth: 0,
 41:         }
 42:     }
 43: }
 44: 
 45: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 46: enum NodeKind {
 47:     Leaf(LeafPayload),
 48:     Interior { child_base: usize, child_mask: u32 },
 49: }
 50: 
 51: /// Conservative screen projection of a node's bounding sphere and splat.
 52: struct ProjectedNode {
 53:     center: [f32; 3],
 54:     relative_to_camera: [f32; 3],
 55:     camera_depth: f32,
 56:     pixel_x: f32,
 57:     pixel_y: f32,
 58:     splat_half: f32,
 59:     projected_radius: f32,
 60:     camera_inside: bool,
 61: }
 62: 
 63: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 64: enum Children {
 65:     Atlas { base: usize, mask: u32 },
 66:     Virtual(LeafPayload),
 67: }
 68: 
 69: impl Children {
 70:     fn mask(self) -> u32 {
 71:         match self {
 72:             Self::Atlas { mask, .. } => mask,
 73:             Self::Virtual(_) => 0xFF,
 74:         }
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     fn child(
 78:         self,
 79:         octant: u32,
 80:         parent_virtual_depth: usize,
 81:     ) -> (usize, Option<LeafPayload>, usize) {
 82:         match self {
 83:             Self::Atlas { base, .. } => (base + octant as usize, None, 0),
 84:             Self::Virtual(payload) => (usize::MAX, Some(payload), parent_virtual_depth + 1),
 85:         }
 86:     }
 87: }
 88: 
 89: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 90:     /// Traversal entry point kept narrow for the frame orchestrator.
 91:     pub(super) fn render_chunk(&mut self, cam: &Camera, chunks: &[ChunkDraw], chunk: &ChunkDraw) {
 92:         self.render_node(cam, chunks, NodeVisit::root(chunk));
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     /// Projects, resolves, and dispatches one node. All branch-specific work
 96:     /// is delegated so the recursive control flow remains readable.
 97:     fn render_node(&mut self, cam: &Camera, chunks: &[ChunkDraw], visit: NodeVisit) {
 98:         let Some(projected) = self.project_node(cam, visit) else {
 99:             return;
100:         };
101: 
102:         // Preserve telemetry semantics: a projected malformed atlas node is
103:         // counted before its failed decode, just as the original traversal.
104:         self.visited_nodes += 1;
105:         let Some(kind) = self.resolve_node(visit) else {
106:             return;
107:         };
108: 
109:         if self.visited_nodes >= MAX_VISITED_NODES && !budget_exempt(cam, &projected) {
110:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
111:             self.render_budget_fallback(cam, chunks, visit, &projected, kind);
112:             return;
113:         }
114: 
115:         match kind {
116:             NodeKind::Leaf(payload) => self.render_leaf(cam, chunks, visit, &projected, payload),
117:             NodeKind::Interior {
118:                 child_base,
119:                 child_mask,
120:             } => {
121:                 self.render_interior(cam, chunks, visit, &projected, child_base, child_mask);
122:             }
123:         }
124:     }
125: 
126:     /// Projects a node and applies correctness clipping plus optional HZ
127:     /// rejection. `None` means the node cannot contribute a visible pixel.
128:     fn project_node(&self, cam: &Camera, visit: NodeVisit) -> Option<ProjectedNode> {
129:         let half_size = visit.size * 0.5;
130:         let center = [
131:             visit.min[0] + half_size,
132:             visit.min[1] + half_size,
133:             visit.min[2] + half_size,
134:         ];
135:         let radius = visit.size * 0.866;
136:         let relative_to_camera = [
137:             center[0] - cam.pos[0],
138:             center[1] - cam.pos[1],
139:             center[2] - cam.pos[2],
140:         ];
141:         let camera_depth = dot(relative_to_camera, cam.forward);
142:         if camera_depth + radius <= 0.01 {
143:             return None;
144:         }
145: 
146:         let camera_inside = camera_depth - radius <= 0.0;
147:         if camera_inside {
148:             return Some(project_inside_node(
149:                 cam,
150:                 center,
151:                 relative_to_camera,
152:                 camera_depth,
153:                 half_size,
154:                 radius,
155:             ));
156:         }
157: 
158:         let inverse_depth = 1.0 / camera_depth;
159:         let pixel_x =
160:             cam.half_w + dot(relative_to_camera, cam.right) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px;
161:         let pixel_y = cam.half_h - dot(relative_to_camera, cam.up) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px;
162:         let projected_radius = radius * cam.focal_px / (camera_depth - radius).max(0.001);
163: 
164:         if outside_target(
165:             pixel_x,
166:             pixel_y,
167:             projected_radius,
168:             self.target.width(),
169:             self.target.height(),
170:         ) {
171:             return None;
172:         }
173: 
174:         // OPTIMIZATION (hierarchical z): the target summary is conservative:
175:         // every overlapping tile must be fully covered and its farthest pixel
176:         // must still be nearer than this node's nearest possible depth.
177:         if self.settings.toggles.hierarchical_z
178:             && self.target.coarse_occludes(
179:                 pixel_x,
180:                 pixel_y,
181:                 projected_radius,
182:                 (camera_depth - radius).max(0.0),
183:             )
184:         {
185:             return None;
186:         }
187: 
188:         Some(ProjectedNode {
189:             center,
190:             relative_to_camera,
191:             camera_depth,
192:             pixel_x,
193:             pixel_y,
194:             splat_half: half_size * cam.focal_px * inverse_depth,
195:             projected_radius,
196:             camera_inside: false,
197:         })
198:     }
199: 
200:     fn resolve_node(&self, visit: NodeVisit) -> Option<NodeKind> {
201:         if let Some(payload) = visit.virtual_leaf {
202:             return Some(NodeKind::Leaf(payload));
203:         }
204: 
205:         let node = decode_node(&self.atlas, visit.node_idx)?;
206:         if node.is_leaf {
207:             Some(NodeKind::Leaf(LeafPayload {
208:                 voxel_type: node.voxel_type,
209:                 color: node.color,
210:                 light: node.light,
211:             }))
212:         } else {
213:             Some(NodeKind::Interior {
214:                 child_base: node.child_base,
215:                 child_mask: node.child_mask,
216:             })
217:         }
218:     }
219: 
220:     /// Safety-cap behavior: retain the current fidelity and stop descending.
221:     fn render_budget_fallback(
222:         &mut self,
223:         cam: &Camera,
224:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
225:         visit: NodeVisit,
226:         projected: &ProjectedNode,
227:         kind: NodeKind,
228:     ) {
229:         match kind {
230:             NodeKind::Leaf(payload) if payload.voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR => {
231:                 self.draw_leaf_splat(cam, chunks, visit, projected, payload);
232:             }
233:             NodeKind::Leaf(_) => {}
234:             NodeKind::Interior { .. } => self.draw_mip_splat(cam, chunks, visit, projected),
235:         }
236:     }
237: 
238:     fn render_leaf(
239:         &mut self,
240:         cam: &Camera,
241:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
242:         visit: NodeVisit,
243:         projected: &ProjectedNode,
244:         payload: LeafPayload,
245:     ) {
246:         if payload.voxel_type == VOXEL_AIR {
247:             return;
248:         }
249:         self.max_virtual_depth_reached = self.max_virtual_depth_reached.max(visit.virtual_depth);
250: 
251:         let should_subdivide = projected.splat_half > self.settings.max_splat_half_px
252:             && visit.size > self.settings.min_split_size
253:             && visit.virtual_depth < self.settings.max_virtual_depth as usize
254:             && !projected.camera_inside;
255:         if should_subdivide {
256:             self.visit_children(
257:                 cam,
258:                 chunks,
259:                 visit,
260:                 Children::Virtual(payload),
261:                 visit.crowded_siblings,
262:             );
263:         } else {
264:             self.draw_leaf_splat(cam, chunks, visit, projected, payload);
265:         }
266:     }
267: 
268:     fn draw_leaf_splat(
269:         &mut self,
270:         cam: &Camera,
271:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
272:         visit: NodeVisit,
273:         projected: &ProjectedNode,
274:         payload: LeafPayload,
275:     ) {
276:         let emissive = is_emissive(payload.voxel_type);
277:         let shadow = self.shadow_factor(chunks, projected.center, emissive, projected.camera_depth);
278:         self.shade_and_splat(
279:             cam,
280:             chunks,
281:             projected.center,
282:             visit.size,
283:             projected.pixel_x,
284:             projected.pixel_y,
285:             (projected.splat_half * 1.15).max(0.85),
286:             projected.camera_depth,
287:             payload.color,
288:             payload.light,
289:             emissive,
290:             visit.crowded_siblings,
291:             shadow,
292:         );
293:     }
294: 
295:     fn render_interior(
296:         &mut self,
297:         cam: &Camera,
298:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
299:         visit: NodeVisit,
300:         projected: &ProjectedNode,
301:         child_base: usize,
302:         child_mask: u32,
303:     ) {
304:         // OPTIMIZATION (LOD): a subtree fitting in roughly a pixel becomes
305:         // one prefiltered MIP splat instead of a full descendant walk.
306:         if self.settings.toggles.mip_lod && projected.projected_radius < self.settings.lod_cutoff_px
307:         {
308:             self.draw_mip_splat(cam, chunks, visit, projected);
309:             return;
310:         }
311: 
312:         self.visit_children(
313:             cam,
314:             chunks,
315:             visit,
316:             Children::Atlas {
317:                 base: child_base,
318:                 mask: child_mask,
319:             },
320:             child_mask.count_ones(),
321:         );
322:     }
323: 
324:     fn draw_mip_splat(
325:         &mut self,
326:         cam: &Camera,
327:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
328:         visit: NodeVisit,
329:         projected: &ProjectedNode,
330:     ) {
331:         let mip = self.mips.get(visit.node_idx).copied().unwrap_or_default();
332:         if mip.occupancy < self.settings.min_mip_occupancy {
333:             return;
334:         }
335:         let shadow = self.shadow_factor(chunks, projected.center, false, projected.camera_depth);
336:         self.shade_and_splat(
337:             cam,
338:             chunks,
339:             projected.center,
340:             visit.size,
341:             projected.pixel_x,
342:             projected.pixel_y,
343:             1.0,
344:             projected.camera_depth,
345:             mip.color,
346:             mip.light,
347:             false,
348:             visit.crowded_siblings,
349:             shadow,
350:         );
351:     }
352: 
353:     /// Visits occupied octants either near-to-far or in reference index
354:     /// order. Virtual subdivision reuses one leaf payload at the next depth.
355:     fn visit_children(
356:         &mut self,
357:         cam: &Camera,
358:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
359:         parent: NodeVisit,
360:         children: Children,
361:         crowding: u32,
362:     ) {
363:         let half_size = parent.size * 0.5;
364:         let parent_center = [
365:             parent.min[0] + half_size,
366:             parent.min[1] + half_size,
367:             parent.min[2] + half_size,
368:         ];
369:         let near_octant = (cam.pos[0] >= parent_center[0]) as u32
370:             | (((cam.pos[1] >= parent_center[1]) as u32) << 1)
371:             | (((cam.pos[2] >= parent_center[2]) as u32) << 2);
372: 
373:         // XOR distances grouped by popcount: camera octant first, opposite
374:         // octant last. Plain octant order is the toggle-off reference path.
375:         const FRONT_TO_BACK_ORDER: [u32; 8] = [0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7];
376:         let mask = children.mask();
377:         for (index, relative_octant) in FRONT_TO_BACK_ORDER.into_iter().enumerate() {
378:             let octant = if self.settings.toggles.front_to_back {
379:                 near_octant ^ relative_octant
380:             } else {
381:                 index as u32
382:             };
383:             if mask & (1 << octant) == 0 {
384:                 continue;
385:             }
386: 
387:             let min = [
388:                 parent.min[0] + (octant & 1) as f32 * half_size,
389:                 parent.min[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) as f32 * half_size,
390:                 parent.min[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) as f32 * half_size,
391:             ];
392:             let (node_idx, virtual_leaf, virtual_depth) =
393:                 children.child(octant, parent.virtual_depth);
394:             self.render_node(
395:                 cam,
396:                 chunks,
397:                 NodeVisit {
398:                     node_idx,
399:                     min,
400:                     size: half_size,
401:                     crowded_siblings: crowding,
402:                     virtual_leaf,
403:                     virtual_depth,
404:                 },
405:             );
406:         }
407:     }
408: }
409: 
410: fn project_inside_node(
411:     cam: &Camera,
412:     center: [f32; 3],
413:     relative_to_camera: [f32; 3],
414:     camera_depth: f32,
415:     half_size: f32,
416:     radius: f32,
417: ) -> ProjectedNode {
418:     let safe_depth = camera_depth.max(half_size * 0.5).max(0.05);
419:     let inverse_depth = 1.0 / safe_depth;
420:     ProjectedNode {
421:         center,
422:         relative_to_camera,
423:         camera_depth,
424:         pixel_x: cam.half_w + dot(relative_to_camera, cam.right) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px,
425:         pixel_y: cam.half_h - dot(relative_to_camera, cam.up) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px,
426:         splat_half: half_size * cam.focal_px * inverse_depth,
427:         projected_radius: radius * cam.focal_px * inverse_depth,
428:         camera_inside: true,
429:     }
430: }
431: 
432: fn outside_target(px: f32, py: f32, radius: f32, width: usize, height: usize) -> bool {
433:     px + radius < 0.0
434:         || px - radius >= width as f32
435:         || py + radius < 0.0
436:         || py - radius >= height as f32
437: }
438: 
439: /// The spotlight area is exempt from the node cap so the player's focus does
440: /// not visibly degrade when unrelated geometry exhausts the frame budget.
441: fn budget_exempt(cam: &Camera, projected: &ProjectedNode) -> bool {
442:     if !cam.flashlight {
443:         return false;
444:     }
445:     let distance = projected.camera_depth.max(0.001);
446:     if distance >= 15.0 {
447:         return false;
448:     }
449:     let direction = projected
450:         .relative_to_camera
451:         .map(|component| component / distance);
452:     dot(direction, cam.forward) > 0.88
453: }
454: 
455: /// Chunk-level visibility: distance cap plus the same conservative screen
456: /// bounds used for individual nodes.
457: pub(super) fn chunk_visible(
458:     chunk: &ChunkDraw,
459:     cam: &Camera,
460:     width: usize,
461:     height: usize,
462:     max_draw_distance: f32,
463: ) -> bool {
464:     let half_size = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
465:     let center = [
466:         chunk.origin[0] + half_size,
467:         chunk.origin[1] + half_size,
468:         chunk.origin[2] + half_size,
469:     ];
470:     let radius = chunk.world_size * 0.866;
471:     let relative_to_camera = [
472:         center[0] - cam.pos[0],
473:         center[1] - cam.pos[1],
474:         center[2] - cam.pos[2],
475:     ];
476: 
477:     if dot(relative_to_camera, relative_to_camera).sqrt() - radius > max_draw_distance {
478:         return false;
479:     }
480:     let camera_depth = dot(relative_to_camera, cam.forward);
481:     if camera_depth + radius <= 0.01 {
482:         return false;
483:     }
484:     if camera_depth - radius <= 0.0 {
485:         return true;
486:     }
487: 
488:     let inverse_depth = 1.0 / camera_depth;
489:     let pixel_x = cam.half_w + dot(relative_to_camera, cam.right) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px;
490:     let pixel_y = cam.half_h - dot(relative_to_camera, cam.up) * inverse_depth * cam.focal_px;
491:     let projected_radius = radius * cam.focal_px / (camera_depth - radius).max(0.001);
492:     !outside_target(pixel_x, pixel_y, projected_radius, width, height)
493: }
494: 
495: pub(super) fn chunk_distance_sq(chunk: &ChunkDraw, position: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
496:     let half = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
497:     let dx = chunk.origin[0] + half - position[0];
498:     let dz = chunk.origin[2] + half - position[2];
499:     dx * dx + dz * dz
500: }
````

````rust
  1: //! SVO atlas decoding and MIP filtering.
  2: //!
  3: //! The atlas is the GPU-serialized octree shared with every other renderer:
  4: //! 4 `u32` per node (see the core's `OctreeGpuSerializer`). This module owns
  5: //! the two pieces of *data preparation* the splatter needs:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`decode_node`] — one node's texels → leaf payload or child pointer.
  8: //! * [`build_mips`] — a per-node pyramid of filtered attributes (average
  9: //!   color, max light, occupancy), computed once per atlas upload so the
 10: //!   LOD path can draw a whole subtree as a single splat.
 11: 
 12: /// Voxel type constants shared with the core serializer.
 13: pub const VOXEL_AIR: u32 = 0;
 14: 
 15: /// Single CPU-renderer predicate mirroring the domain's emissive palette.
 16: /// Keeping this beside atlas decoding prevents traversal and shading from
 17: /// growing renderer-specific material lists.
 18: pub fn is_emissive(voxel_type: u32) -> bool {
 19:     u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok().is_some_and(|material| {
 20:         vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material)
 21:     })
 22: }
 23: 
 24: /// A decoded atlas node. Exactly one of the two shapes is meaningful:
 25: /// leaves carry material/color/light, while interiors carry
 26: /// `child_base`/`child_mask`.
 27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 28: pub struct DecodedNode {
 29:     pub is_leaf: bool,
 30:     pub child_base: usize,
 31:     pub child_mask: u32,
 32:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 33:     /// Leaf albedo in the renderer's 0..255 working range.
 34:     pub color: [f32; 3],
 35:     /// Leaf scalar BFS light level, 0..15.
 36:     pub light: f32,
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// Reads node `node_idx` out of the texel stream. Returns `None` when the
 40: /// index runs past the atlas (defensive: a truncated upload must degrade to
 41: /// missing geometry, not out-of-bounds panics).
 42: pub fn decode_node(atlas: &[u32], node_idx: usize) -> Option<DecodedNode> {
 43:     let t = node_idx * 4;
 44:     if t + 3 >= atlas.len() {
 45:         return None;
 46:     }
 47:     let is_leaf = atlas[t] == 1;
 48:     if is_leaf {
 49:         let packed_color = atlas[t + 2];
 50:         Some(DecodedNode {
 51:             is_leaf: true,
 52:             child_base: 0,
 53:             child_mask: 0,
 54:             voxel_type: atlas[t + 1],
 55:             color: [
 56:                 ((packed_color >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
 57:                 ((packed_color >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
 58:                 (packed_color & 0xFF) as f32,
 59:             ],
 60:             light: (atlas[t + 3] & 0xFF) as f32,
 61:         })
 62:     } else {
 63:         Some(DecodedNode {
 64:             is_leaf: false,
 65:             child_base: atlas[t + 1] as usize,
 66:             child_mask: atlas[t + 2],
 67:             voxel_type: 0,
 68:             color: [0.0; 3],
 69:             light: 0.0,
 70:         })
 71:     }
 72: }
 73: 
 74: /// Per-node MIP-filtered attributes, rebuilt on every atlas upload.
 75: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
 76: pub struct MipNode {
 77:     /// Occupancy-weighted average RGB of the subtree, 0..255 per channel.
 78:     pub color: [f32; 3],
 79:     /// Max BFS light level in the subtree (0..15).
 80:     pub light: f32,
 81:     /// Fraction of the subtree volume that is solid, 0..1.
 82:     pub occupancy: f32,
 83: }
 84: 
 85: /// Bottom-up MIP filtering over the whole atlas. Node order in the arena is
 86: /// not guaranteed (`SparseVoxelOctree::set` appends children after parents,
 87: /// `BuildOctreeUseCase` pushes the root last), so each subtree is resolved by
 88: /// memoized recursion instead of a single directional sweep. Still O(n): every
 89: /// node is computed exactly once.
 90: pub fn build_mips(atlas: &[u32]) -> Vec<MipNode> {
 91:     let node_count = atlas.len() / 4;
 92:     let mut mips = vec![MipNode::default(); node_count];
 93:     let mut done = vec![false; node_count];
 94:     for i in 0..node_count {
 95:         compute_mip(atlas, i, &mut mips, &mut done);
 96:     }
 97:     mips
 98: }
 99: 
100: fn compute_mip(atlas: &[u32], i: usize, mips: &mut [MipNode], done: &mut [bool]) {
101:     if done[i] {
102:         return;
103:     }
104:     // Marked before descending: a malformed cycle degrades to a zero mip
105:     // instead of infinite recursion.
106:     done[i] = true;
107: 
108:     let t = i * 4;
109:     if atlas[t] == 1 {
110:         // Leaf.
111:         let voxel_type = atlas[t + 1];
112:         if voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR {
113:             let c = atlas[t + 2];
114:             mips[i] = MipNode {
115:                 color: [
116:                     ((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
117:                     ((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
118:                     (c & 0xFF) as f32,
119:                 ],
120:                 // Bits 0-7 are the scalar level; occlusion and the RGB
121:                 // channels live in the higher bits (see OctreeGpuSerializer).
122:                 light: (atlas[t + 3] & 0xFF) as f32,
123:                 occupancy: 1.0,
124:             };
125:         }
126:     } else {
127:         let child_base = atlas[t + 1] as usize;
128:         let child_mask = atlas[t + 2];
129:         let mut acc = MipNode::default();
130:         for child in 0..8usize {
131:             if child_mask & (1 << child) == 0 {
132:                 continue;
133:             }
134:             let idx = child_base + child;
135:             if idx >= mips.len() {
136:                 continue;
137:             }
138:             compute_mip(atlas, idx, mips, done);
139:             let m = mips[idx];
140:             let w = m.occupancy / 8.0;
141:             acc.color[0] += m.color[0] * w;
142:             acc.color[1] += m.color[1] * w;
143:             acc.color[2] += m.color[2] * w;
144:             acc.light = acc.light.max(m.light);
145:             acc.occupancy += w;
146:         }
147:         if acc.occupancy > 0.0 {
148:             let inv = 1.0 / acc.occupancy;
149:             acc.color[0] *= inv;
150:             acc.color[1] *= inv;
151:             acc.color[2] *= inv;
152:         }
153:         mips[i] = acc;
154:     }
155: }
156: 
157: #[cfg(test)]
158: mod tests {
159:     use super::is_emissive;
160:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
161:         VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
162:     };
163: 
164:     #[test]
165:     fn emissive_palette_matches_the_domain() {
166:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_LIGHT as u32));
167:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_RED_LIGHT as u32));
168:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_GLIMMER as u32));
169:         assert!(!is_emissive(VOXEL_AIR as u32));
170:         assert!(!is_emissive(u32::MAX));
171:     }
172: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Pinhole camera for the splatter, matching the GPU shaders' yaw/pitch
 2: //! basis exactly (same formulas as `drivers::webgl`'s per-frame uniforms),
 3: //! so switching renderers never changes the framing.
 4: 
 5: use crate::application::ports::{DynamicLight, FrameParams, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 6: 
 7: use super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 8: 
 9: pub fn dot(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
10:     a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
11: }
12: 
13: /// Camera basis + per-frame light state, derived once per frame.
14: pub struct Camera {
15:     pub pos: [f32; 3],
16:     pub right: [f32; 3],
17:     pub up: [f32; 3],
18:     pub forward: [f32; 3],
19:     /// Focal length in pixels: h / (2 * tan(fov/2)).
20:     pub focal_px: f32,
21:     pub half_w: f32,
22:     pub half_h: f32,
23:     pub flashlight: bool,
24:     /// Per-frame dynamic lights (flares), pre-flickered by the engine.
25:     pub dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
26:     pub dynamic_light_count: usize,
27: }
28: 
29: impl Camera {
30:     pub fn new(
31:         frame: &FrameParams,
32:         width: usize,
33:         height: usize,
34:         settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
35:     ) -> Self {
36:         let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
37:         let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
38:         Self {
39:             pos: frame.camera_pos,
40:             right: [cy, 0.0, -sy],
41:             up: [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy],
42:             forward: [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy],
43:             focal_px: height as f32 / (2.0 * settings.fov_tan),
44:             half_w: width as f32 / 2.0,
45:             half_h: height as f32 / 2.0,
46:             flashlight: frame.flashlight,
47:             dynamic_lights: frame.dynamic_lights,
48:             dynamic_light_count: frame.dynamic_light_count as usize,
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs
````rust
  1: //! The player's flashlight — a true spotlight cone.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module is the **single specification** of the cone light's shape.
  4: //! The GPU shaders implement the same formula in GLSL (see
  5: //! `drivers::shaders::chunks::SPOT_CONE_GLSL`); the constants below are
  6: //! quoted there, so a tuning change here must be mirrored there and
  7: //! vice versa. The beam is defined by four independent factors, multiplied:
  8: //!
  9: //! 1. **Cone** — smoothstep between an inner angle (full strength) and an
 10: //!    outer angle (zero), measured between the beam direction and the ray
 11: //!    from the lamp to the surface point. This is what makes it a *cone*
 12: //!    rather than a screen-centered glow.
 13: //! 2. **Range** — smoothstep fade from `RANGE_FULL` to `RANGE_END` world
 14: //!    units, so the beam dies in fog instead of clipping.
 15: //! 3. **Facing** — Lambert-ish response of the surface normal against the
 16: //!    beam, floored at `FACING_FLOOR` so grazing surfaces inside the cone
 17: //!    still read (the beam has width in reality).
 18: //! 4. **Occlusion** — one SVO shadow ray from the lamp toward the surface
 19: //!    (CPU path only; toggleable via `RenderToggles::flashlight_occlusion`).
 20: //!
 21: //! The lamp sits slightly forward of and below the camera (a hand-held
 22: //! light, not an eye-mounted one), which gives near surfaces a believable
 23: //! parallax between view and beam.
 24: 
 25: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 26: 
 27: use super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 28: use super::raycast::trace_svo;
 29: 
 30: /// Inner cone half-angle: full-strength core of the beam.
 31: pub const INNER_DEG: f32 = 11.0;
 32: /// Outer cone half-angle: intensity reaches zero here.
 33: pub const OUTER_DEG: f32 = 24.0;
 34: /// Distance (world units) up to which the beam is at full strength.
 35: pub const RANGE_FULL: f32 = 3.0;
 36: /// Distance at which the beam has fully faded.
 37: pub const RANGE_END: f32 = 14.0;
 38: /// Minimum facing response inside the cone (beam width fake).
 39: pub const FACING_FLOOR: f32 = 0.08;
 40: /// Lamp offset from the eye: forward and slightly down.
 41: pub const LAMP_FORWARD: f32 = 0.18;
 42: pub const LAMP_DOWN: f32 = 0.10;
 43: /// Move secondary rays out of geometry immediately surrounding the lamp.
 44: const OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS: f32 = 0.15;
 45: /// Stop immediately before the physical receiver face. This is deliberately
 46: /// independent of splat/LOD size: representation changes must not change the
 47: /// lamp-to-receiver segment being tested.
 48: const OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 49: /// Warm-white beam tint, matching the GPU paths.
 50: pub const TINT: [f32; 3] = [1.0, 0.96, 0.85];
 51: 
 52: fn smoothstep01(t: f32) -> f32 {
 53:     let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 54:     t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
 55: }
 56: 
 57: /// Angular falloff: 1 inside the inner cone, 0 outside the outer cone,
 58: /// smooth in between. `alignment` is cos(angle between beam and forward).
 59: pub fn cone_falloff(alignment: f32) -> f32 {
 60:     let inner_cos = INNER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 61:     let outer_cos = OUTER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 62:     if alignment <= outer_cos {
 63:         0.0
 64:     } else {
 65:         smoothstep01((alignment - outer_cos) / (inner_cos - outer_cos))
 66:     }
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Distance falloff: 1 out to [`RANGE_FULL`], 0 at [`RANGE_END`].
 70: pub fn range_falloff(dist: f32) -> f32 {
 71:     1.0 - smoothstep01((dist - RANGE_FULL) / (RANGE_END - RANGE_FULL))
 72: }
 73: 
 74: /// Length passed to `trace_svo`, whose origin has already moved
 75: /// [`OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS`] away from the lamp.
 76: fn occlusion_trace_length(lamp_to_receiver: f32) -> Option<f32> {
 77:     let length = lamp_to_receiver - OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS - OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS;
 78:     (length > 0.0).then_some(length)
 79: }
 80: 
 81: /// RGB contribution of the flashlight on a surface point.
 82: ///
 83: /// `surface_pos`/`surface_normal` describe the physical receiver face.
 84: /// Occlusion depends only on that lamp-to-face segment, never on the splat
 85: /// size chosen by LOD. `toggles` controls both the optional SVO occlusion ray
 86: /// and its near-to-far traversal order.
 87: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 88: pub fn beam_contribution(
 89:     cam: &Camera,
 90:     atlas: &[u32],
 91:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 92:     surface_pos: [f32; 3],
 93:     surface_normal: [f32; 3],
 94:     toggles: &crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles,
 95: ) -> [f32; 3] {
 96:     // The hand-held lamp position (forward of and below the eye).
 97:     let lamp = [
 98:         cam.pos[0] + cam.forward[0] * LAMP_FORWARD,
 99:         cam.pos[1] + cam.forward[1] * LAMP_FORWARD - LAMP_DOWN,
100:         cam.pos[2] + cam.forward[2] * LAMP_FORWARD,
101:     ];
102: 
103:     let to_surf = [
104:         surface_pos[0] - lamp[0],
105:         surface_pos[1] - lamp[1],
106:         surface_pos[2] - lamp[2],
107:     ];
108:     let dist = dot(to_surf, to_surf).sqrt();
109:     let safe_dist = dist.max(0.0001);
110:     let beam = [
111:         to_surf[0] / safe_dist,
112:         to_surf[1] / safe_dist,
113:         to_surf[2] / safe_dist,
114:     ];
115: 
116:     let cone = cone_falloff(dot(beam, cam.forward));
117:     if cone <= 0.0 {
118:         return [0.0; 3];
119:     }
120:     let range = range_falloff(dist);
121:     if range <= 0.0 {
122:         return [0.0; 3];
123:     }
124:     let facing = (-dot(beam, surface_normal)).max(FACING_FLOOR);
125: 
126:     // Occlusion: trace the geometric lamp-to-face segment. Both endpoint
127:     // biases are fixed world-space tolerances; tying the receiver bias to a
128:     // coarse node's half-extent made shadows jump when LOD changed.
129:     if toggles.flashlight_occlusion {
130:         let ray_origin = [
131:             lamp[0] + beam[0] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
132:             lamp[1] + beam[1] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
133:             lamp[2] + beam[2] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
134:         ];
135:         let blocked = occlusion_trace_length(dist).is_some_and(|max_trace| {
136:             trace_svo(
137:                 atlas,
138:                 chunks,
139:                 ray_origin,
140:                 beam,
141:                 max_trace,
142:                 toggles.front_to_back,
143:             )
144:             .is_some()
145:         });
146:         if blocked {
147:             return [0.0; 3];
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151:     let intensity = cone * range * facing;
152:     [
153:         intensity * TINT[0],
154:         intensity * TINT[1],
155:         intensity * TINT[2],
156:     ]
157: }
158:

177:

180:     }
181: 
182:     #[test]
183:     fn cone_is_full_inside_inner_angle_and_zero_outside_outer() {
184:         assert_eq!(cone_falloff(1.0), 1.0);
185:         assert_eq!(cone_falloff((INNER_DEG - 1.0).to_radians().cos()), 1.0);
186:         assert_eq!(cone_falloff((OUTER_DEG + 1.0).to_radians().cos()), 0.0);
187:         let mid = cone_falloff(((INNER_DEG + OUTER_DEG) * 0.5).to_radians().cos());
188:         assert!(mid > 0.0 && mid < 1.0, "smooth transition, got {mid}");
189:     }
190: 
191:     #[test]
192:     fn range_fades_between_full_and_end() {
193:         assert_eq!(range_falloff(0.0), 1.0);
194:         assert_eq!(range_falloff(RANGE_FULL), 1.0);
195:         assert_eq!(range_falloff(RANGE_END), 0.0);
196:         let mid = range_falloff((RANGE_FULL + RANGE_END) * 0.5);
197:         assert!((mid - 0.5).abs() < 1e-5, "smoothstep midpoint, got {mid}");
198:     }

204:         let endpoint_from_lamp = OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS + trace;
205:         assert!((endpoint_from_lamp - (distance - OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS)).abs() < 1.0e-6);
206:     }
````

````rust
 1: //! CPU microvoxel splatting renderer — a software implementation of
 2: //! [`crate::application::ports::RendererPort`] for machines with no usable
 3: //! GPU (or `?renderer=cpu`).
 4: //!
 5: //! Instead of marching a ray per pixel, the CPU path inverts the loop: it
 6: //! walks the SVO front-to-back and *splats* nodes onto a z-buffered
 7: //! framebuffer, sized by their projected footprint. The module is split by
 8: //! responsibility — each file owns exactly one concern:
 9: //!
10: //! | module         | concern                                              |
11: //! |----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
12: //! | [`settings`]   | tuning knobs + the shared optimization switchboard   |
13: //! | [`atlas`]      | SVO texel decoding and per-upload MIP filtering      |
14: //! | [`raycast`]    | secondary rays (flashlight occlusion, shadow rays)   |
15: //! | [`camera`]     | yaw/pitch basis identical to the GPU shaders         |
16: //! | [`flashlight`] | the spotlight cone — the single spec of its shape    |
17: //! | [`shading`]    | per-splat lighting: ambient, AO, flares, fog         |
18: //! | [`rasterizer`] | facade; split target + traversal frame pipeline     |
19: //!
20: //! This module is platform-free (no web-sys): the browser driver only blits
21: //! the RGBA buffer (`drivers::cpu_canvas`). All geometry/shading logic is
22: //! natively unit-tested in [`tests`].
23: 
24: mod atlas;
25: mod camera;
26: mod flashlight;
27: mod rasterizer;
28: mod raycast;
29: mod settings;
30: mod shading;
31: #[cfg(test)]
32: mod tests;
33: 
34: pub use rasterizer::{SoftwareRasterizer, SoftwareRasterizerTelemetry};
35: pub use raycast::{RayHit, trace_svo};
36: pub use settings::{CpuRenderSettings, CpuShadowMode};
````

````rust
  1: //! CPU microvoxel rasterizer facade and frame pipeline.
  2: //!
  3: //! The persistent renderer owns reusable allocations, settings, telemetry,
  4: //! atlas data, and the amortized shadow cache. Focused child modules own the
  5: //! two dense algorithms:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`target`] — framebuffer, fine depth, conservative hierarchical Z;
  8: //! * [`traversal`] — projection, SVO walking, LOD, and virtual subdivision.
  9: //!
 10: //! Color remains in [`super::shading`], secondary rays in
 11: //! [`super::raycast`], and per-frame camera math in [`super::camera`].

 14: mod traversal;

 16: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, Environment, FrameParams, RendererPort};

 26: /// Per-frame counters for the HUD; tests also use them to prove termination
 27: /// and safety-cap behavior.
 28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
 29: pub struct SoftwareRasterizerTelemetry {
 30:     pub visited_nodes: usize,
 31:     pub budget_exhausted: bool,
 32:     pub max_virtual_depth: usize,
 33:     pub splat_count: usize,
 34:     pub pixel_writes: usize,
 35: }
 36: 
 37: /// Non-optional safety caps. The node cap degrades to current-fidelity/MIP
 38: /// splats; the write cap stops inside the exact pixel loop.
 39: const MAX_VISITED_NODES: usize = 150_000;
 40: const MAX_PIXEL_WRITES: usize = 2_000_000;
 41: /// Above this write level, hero shadow rays are no longer affordable.
 42: const SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET: usize = 1_500_000;
 43: 
 44: /// Persistent state for the CPU renderer. The struct is intentionally the
 45: /// allocation-owning facade; rendering algorithms live in focused modules.
 46: pub struct SoftwareRasterizer {
 47:     target: RenderTarget,
 48:     /// SVO atlas texels: four `u32`s per node.
 49:     atlas: Vec<u32>,
 50:     mips: Vec<MipNode>,
 51: 
 52:     // Public counters are retained for compatibility; `telemetry()` is the
 53:     // stable snapshot API used by the browser driver and tests.
 54:     pub visited_nodes: usize,
 55:     pub budget_exhausted: bool,
 56:     pub max_virtual_depth_reached: usize,
 57:     pub splat_count: usize,
 58:     pub pixel_writes: usize,
 59: 
 60:     pub settings: CpuRenderSettings,
 61:     /// Position-hashed hero-shadow cache; each entry retraces every fourth
 62:     /// frame, staggered by its hash.
 63:     shadow_cache: Vec<f32>,
 64:     frame_index: usize,
 65:     /// Current level atmosphere, captured once at the start of `draw`.
 66:     environment: Environment,
 67: }
 68: 
 69: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 70:     pub fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {

114:     /// Test seam and frame clear: atmosphere chooses the background; target
115:     /// storage owns color/depth/HZ reset mechanics.
116:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
117:         let background = if self.environment.outdoor {
118:             [
119:                 (self.environment.sky_color[0] * 255.0) as u8,
120:                 (self.environment.sky_color[1] * 255.0) as u8,
121:                 (self.environment.sky_color[2] * 255.0) as u8,
122:             ]
123:         } else {
124:             [0, 0, 0]
125:         };
126:         self.target.clear(background);
127:     }

129:     /// Frame-policy wrapper around the pixel-only target operation. It keeps
130:     /// the exact in-loop write cap and renderer telemetry out of `target`.
131:     fn splat(&mut self, cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, z: f32, rgb: [u8; 3]) {
132:         if self.pixel_writes >= MAX_PIXEL_WRITES {
133:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
134:             return;
135:         }
136:         self.splat_count += 1;
137: 
138:         let result = self.target.write_splat(
139:             SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, z, rgb),
140:             MAX_PIXEL_WRITES - self.pixel_writes,
141:             self.settings.toggles.hierarchical_z,
142:         );
143:         self.pixel_writes += result.pixel_writes;
144:         self.budget_exhausted |= result.budget_exhausted;
145:     }
````
