````rust
147:     /// Shades one exact box and writes its square splat. Retained as a narrow
148:     /// test seam; lighting itself remains in `shading`.
149:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
150:     pub(super) fn shade_and_splat(
151:         &mut self,
152:         cam: &Camera,
153:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
154:         center: [f32; 3],
155:         world_size: f32,
156:         px: f32,
157:         py: f32,
158:         half_px: f32,
159:         dist: f32,
160:         base_color: [f32; 3],
161:         light_level: f32,
162:         is_emissive: bool,
163:         crowded_siblings: u32,
164:         shadow_factor: f32,
165:     ) {
166:         let surface = SplatSurface {
167:             center,
168:             world_size,
169:             dist,
170:             base_color,
171:             light_level,
172:             is_emissive,
173:             crowded_siblings,
174:             shadow_factor,
175:         };
176:         let rgb = shading::shade(
177:             cam,
178:             &self.environment,
179:             &self.settings,
180:             &self.atlas,
181:             chunks,
182:             &surface,
183:         );
184:         self.splat(px, py, half_px, dist, rgb);
185:     }
186: 
187:     /// Hero-light visibility, amortized through a position-hashed cache.
188:     fn shadow_factor(
189:         &mut self,
190:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
191:         center: [f32; 3],
192:         is_emissive: bool,
193:         dist: f32,
194:     ) -> f32 {
195:         let affordable = dist <= 24.0 && self.pixel_writes < SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET;
196:         if self.settings.shadows != CpuShadowMode::Hero || is_emissive || !affordable {
197:             return 1.0;
198:         }
199: 
200:         let ix = center[0].floor() as i32;
201:         let iy = center[1].floor() as i32;
202:         let iz = center[2].floor() as i32;
203:         let hash_key = (ix.wrapping_mul(73_856_093)
204:             ^ iy.wrapping_mul(19_349_663)
205:             ^ iz.wrapping_mul(83_492_791)) as usize;
206:         let cache_index = hash_key % self.shadow_cache.len();
207: 
208:         let should_trace = (hash_key + self.frame_index).is_multiple_of(4);
209:         if !should_trace && self.shadow_cache[cache_index] != 0.0 {
210:             return self.shadow_cache[cache_index];
211:         }
212: 
213:         let light_position = [
214:             (center[0] / 3.0).floor() * 3.0 + 1.5,
215:             3.6,
216:             (center[2] / 3.0).floor() * 3.0 + 1.5,
217:         ];
218:         let to_light = [
219:             light_position[0] - center[0],
220:             light_position[1] - center[1],
221:             light_position[2] - center[2],
222:         ];
223:         let distance_to_light = dot(to_light, to_light).sqrt();
224:         let factor = if distance_to_light > 0.001 {
225:             let inverse_distance = 1.0 / distance_to_light;
226:             let direction = to_light.map(|component| component * inverse_distance);
227:             let origin = [
228:                 center[0] + direction[0] * 0.05,
229:                 center[1] + direction[1] * 0.05,
230:                 center[2] + direction[2] * 0.05,
231:             ];
232:             if trace_svo(
233:                 &self.atlas,
234:                 chunks,
235:                 origin,
236:                 direction,
237:                 distance_to_light - 0.05,
238:                 self.settings.toggles.front_to_back,
239:             )
240:             .is_some()
241:             {
242:                 0.25
243:             } else {
244:                 1.0
245:             }
246:         } else {
247:             1.0
248:         };
249:         self.shadow_cache[cache_index] = factor;
250:         factor
251:     }

253:     fn reset_telemetry(&mut self) {
254:         self.visited_nodes = 0;
255:         self.budget_exhausted = false;
256:         self.max_virtual_depth_reached = 0;
257:         self.splat_count = 0;
258:         self.pixel_writes = 0;
259:     }
260: 
261:     fn draw_flare_cores(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, cam: &Camera) {
262:         for light in frame.active_dynamic_lights() {
263:             let relative = [
264:                 light.position[0] - cam.pos[0],
265:                 light.position[1] - cam.pos[1],
266:                 light.position[2] - cam.pos[2],
267:             ];
268:             let camera_depth = dot(relative, cam.forward);
269:             if camera_depth <= 0.1 || camera_depth > self.settings.max_draw_distance {
270:                 continue;
271:             }
272: 
273:             let pixel_x = cam.half_w + dot(relative, cam.right) / camera_depth * cam.focal_px;
274:             let pixel_y = cam.half_h - dot(relative, cam.up) / camera_depth * cam.focal_px;
275:             let half = (0.06 / camera_depth * cam.focal_px).clamp(1.0, 6.0);
276:             let intensity = light.intensity.clamp(0.0, 1.6) / 1.6;
277:             self.splat(
278:                 pixel_x,
279:                 pixel_y,
280:                 half,
281:                 camera_depth - 0.05,
282:                 [
283:                     (255.0 * intensity) as u8,
284:                     (150.0 * intensity) as u8,
285:                     (60.0 * intensity) as u8,
286:                 ],
287:             );
288:         }
289:     }
290: }
291: 
292: impl RendererPort for SoftwareRasterizer {
293:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
294:         self.atlas = texels.to_vec();
295:         // MIP attributes are rebuilt on upload, never per frame.
296:         self.mips = build_mips(&self.atlas);
297:     }
298: 
299:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
300:         self.environment = frame.environment;
301:         self.clear();
302:         self.reset_telemetry();
303:         if self.atlas.is_empty() {
304:             return;
305:         }
306: 
307:         let camera = Camera::new(frame, self.width(), self.height(), &self.settings);
308:         let mut order: Vec<&ChunkDraw> = chunks.iter().collect();
309: 
310:         // OPTIMIZATION (front-to-back): nearest chunks populate depth first.
311:         if self.settings.toggles.front_to_back {
312:             order.sort_by(|a, b| {
313:                 chunk_distance_sq(a, frame.camera_pos)
314:                     .total_cmp(&chunk_distance_sq(b, frame.camera_pos))
315:             });
316:         }
317: 
318:         for chunk in order {
319:             // OPTIMIZATION (distance cull): reject chunks outside the draw
320:             // distance or conservative screen bounds.
321:             if self.settings.toggles.distance_cull
322:                 && !chunk_visible(
323:                     chunk,
324:                     &camera,
325:                     self.width(),
326:                     self.height(),
327:                     self.settings.max_draw_distance,
328:                 )
329:             {
330:                 continue;
331:             }
332:             self.render_chunk(&camera, chunks, chunk);
333:         }
334: 
335:         // Flare cores use the ordinary fine depth buffer, so walls occlude
336:         // them without a separate visibility query.
337:         self.draw_flare_cores(frame, &camera);
338:         self.frame_index = self.frame_index.wrapping_add(1);
339:     }
340: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Stack-based SVO ray traversal — the CPU twin of the GLSL `raymarchSVO`.
  2: //!
  3: //! Used for *secondary* rays only (flashlight-beam occlusion and hero-light
  4: //! shadow rays); primary visibility comes from splatting, not marching.
  5: //! The algorithm matches the raymarch shader step for step:
  6: //!
  7: //! 1. Slab-test every chunk AABB and optionally sort hits near-to-far
  8: //!    ([`trace_svo`], controlled by `rt_f2b`).
  9: //! 2. Inside a chunk, descend toward the octant containing the current
 10: //!    point; **empty-space skip** jumps a whole empty leaf/octant in one
 11: //!    step via its AABB exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel DDA.
 12: //! 3. After a skip, pop every ancestor the point exited (a skip through a
 13: //!    shared plane can leave several boxes at once).
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 16: 
 17: use super::atlas::decode_node;
 18: 
 19: /// A solid-leaf intersection: ray parameter and the voxel's material type.
 20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 21: pub struct RayHit {
 22:     pub t: f32,
 23:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 24: }
 25: 
 26: /// Keeps slab divisions finite for axis-aligned rays. `f32::signum()` is
 27: /// zero for `0.0`, so multiplying it by epsilon would leave the divisor at
 28: /// zero; choose the sign explicitly instead.
 29: fn nonzero_direction(component: f32) -> f32 {
 30:     if component.abs() >= 1.0e-4 {
 31:         component
 32:     } else if component.is_sign_negative() {
 33:         -1.0e-4
 34:     } else {
 35:         1.0e-4
 36:     }
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// One saved traversal level: the parent node and its bounds.
 40: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 41: struct TraversalFrame {
 42:     node_idx: usize,
 43:     b_min: [f32; 3],
 44:     b_max: [f32; 3],
 45: }
 46: 
 47: /// The mutable cursor of one chunk march: current node, its bounds, and the
 48: /// ancestor stack (an SVO chunk is at most 8 levels deep, +1 slack).
 49: struct TraversalCursor {
 50:     stack: [TraversalFrame; 9],
 51:     stack_ptr: usize,
 52:     node: usize,
 53:     b_min: [f32; 3],
 54:     b_max: [f32; 3],
 55: }
 56: 
 57: impl TraversalCursor {
 58:     fn at_root(root: usize, world_size: f32) -> Self {
 59:         Self {
 60:             stack: [TraversalFrame {
 61:                 node_idx: 0,
 62:                 b_min: [0.0; 3],
 63:                 b_max: [0.0; 3],
 64:             }; 9],
 65:             stack_ptr: 0,
 66:             node: root,
 67:             b_min: [0.0; 3],
 68:             b_max: [world_size; 3],
 69:         }
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     fn push(&mut self) {
 73:         if self.stack_ptr < 8 {
 74:             self.stack[self.stack_ptr] = TraversalFrame {
 75:                 node_idx: self.node,
 76:                 b_min: self.b_min,
 77:                 b_max: self.b_max,
 78:             };
 79:             self.stack_ptr += 1;
 80:         }
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     /// Pops EVERY level `p` exited: a skip through a plane shared by several
 84:     /// ancestor boxes leaves `p` outside more than one of them, and
 85:     /// descending from a box that no longer contains `p` corrupts the
 86:     /// traversal (wall cracks). Returns `false` when `p` left the chunk.
 87:     fn pop_exited(&mut self, p: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 88:         while p[0] < self.b_min[0]
 89:             || p[0] > self.b_max[0]
 90:             || p[1] < self.b_min[1]
 91:             || p[1] > self.b_max[1]
 92:             || p[2] < self.b_min[2]
 93:             || p[2] > self.b_max[2]
 94:         {
 95:             if self.stack_ptr == 0 {
 96:                 return false;
 97:             }
 98:             self.stack_ptr -= 1;
 99:             let frame = self.stack[self.stack_ptr];
100:             self.node = frame.node_idx;
101:             self.b_min = frame.b_min;
102:             self.b_max = frame.b_max;
103:         }
104:         true
105:     }
106: }
107: 
108: /// Advances the ray to `bounds`' exit and nudges every tied axis just past
109: /// its plane. Leaving an axis exactly *on* its plane stalls the march (t
110: /// stops advancing), so the epsilon push is required for termination.
111: fn skip_to_exit(ro: [f32; 3], rd: [f32; 3], b_min: [f32; 3], b_max: [f32; 3]) -> (f32, [f32; 3]) {
112:     let exit_plane = |axis: usize| {
113:         if rd[axis] > 0.0 {
114:             b_max[axis]
115:         } else {
116:             b_min[axis]
117:         }
118:     };
119:     let t_max_planes = [
120:         (exit_plane(0) - ro[0]) / rd[0],
121:         (exit_plane(1) - ro[1]) / rd[1],
122:         (exit_plane(2) - ro[2]) / rd[2],
123:     ];
124:     let t_exit = t_max_planes[0].min(t_max_planes[1]).min(t_max_planes[2]);
125:     let mut p = [
126:         ro[0] + t_exit * rd[0],
127:         ro[1] + t_exit * rd[1],
128:         ro[2] + t_exit * rd[2],
129:     ];
130:     for axis in 0..3 {
131:         if (t_exit - t_max_planes[axis]).abs() < 0.0001 {
132:             p[axis] = exit_plane(axis) + if rd[axis] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 };
133:         }
134:     }
135:     (t_exit, p)
136: }
137: 
138: /// Marches one chunk's SVO from `t_entry`. `ro`/`rd` are chunk-local.
139: /// Returns the first solid leaf hit, or `None`.
140: fn raymarch_svo_single(
141:     atlas: &[u32],
142:     ro: [f32; 3],
143:     rd: [f32; 3],
144:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
145:     t_entry: f32,
146:     world_size: f32,
147: ) -> Option<RayHit> {
148:     let mut t = t_entry;
149:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
150:     let mut cursor = TraversalCursor::at_root(chunk_root_idx, world_size);
151: 
152:     // Step budget: a bounded march can never hang a frame even on a
153:     // malformed atlas. 160 comfortably covers the deepest real traversals.
154:     const MAX_STEPS: i32 = 160;
155:     for _ in 0..MAX_STEPS {
156:         let node = decode_node(atlas, cursor.node)?;
157: 
158:         if node.is_leaf {
159:             if node.voxel_type != 0 {
160:                 return Some(RayHit {
161:                     t,
162:                     voxel_type: node.voxel_type,
163:                 });
164:             }
165:             // TRAVERSAL: empty-space skip — one step to this empty
166:             // leaf's exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel stepping.
167:             (t, p) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, cursor.b_min, cursor.b_max);
168:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
169:                 return None;
170:             }
171:             continue;
172:         }
173: 
174:         let center = [
175:             (cursor.b_min[0] + cursor.b_max[0]) * 0.5,
176:             (cursor.b_min[1] + cursor.b_max[1]) * 0.5,
177:             (cursor.b_min[2] + cursor.b_max[2]) * 0.5,
178:         ];
179:         let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
180:         let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
181:         let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
182:         let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
183: 
184:         // The octant's own bounds, picked axis-by-axis from the parent box
185:         // and its center plane.
186:         //
187:         // BUG FIX (cone light): `oct_min[1]` used to read `center[1]` in
188:         // both branches. Every secondary ray crossing an empty lower-Y
189:         // octant computed a too-near exit plane, stalled until the step
190:         // budget ran out, and reported "no hit" — so the flashlight beam
191:         // shone through floors and hero-shadow rays never found occluders.
192:         let oct_min = [
193:             if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cursor.b_min[0] },
194:             if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cursor.b_min[1] },
195:             if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cursor.b_min[2] },
196:         ];
197:         let oct_max = [
198:             if ox == 1 { cursor.b_max[0] } else { center[0] },
199:             if oy == 1 { cursor.b_max[1] } else { center[1] },
200:             if oz == 1 { cursor.b_max[2] } else { center[2] },
201:         ];
202: 
203:         if (node.child_mask & (1 << child_idx)) != 0 {
204:             // Descend into the occupied octant.
205:             cursor.push();
206:             cursor.b_min = oct_min;
207:             cursor.b_max = oct_max;
208:             cursor.node = node.child_base + child_idx;
209:         } else {
210:             // TRAVERSAL: masked-out (air) octant skipped in one step.
211:             (t, p) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, oct_min, oct_max);
212:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
213:                 return None;
214:             }
215:         }
216:     }
217:     None
218: }
219: 
220: /// Traces a world-space ray through every resident chunk. Returns the first
221: /// solid hit within `max_t`.
222: pub fn trace_svo(
223:     atlas: &[u32],
224:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
225:     origin: [f32; 3],
226:     direction: [f32; 3],
227:     max_t: f32,
228:     front_to_back: bool,
229: ) -> Option<RayHit> {
230:     struct ChunkHit {
231:         idx: usize,
232:         t_min: f32,
233:     }
234: 
235:     let mut hits = Vec::with_capacity(chunks.len());
236: 
237:     // Axis-aligned rays divide by the direction components; clamp near-zero
238:     // components so the slab test stays finite.
239:     let safe_rd = direction.map(nonzero_direction);
240:     let inv_rd = [1.0 / safe_rd[0], 1.0 / safe_rd[1], 1.0 / safe_rd[2]];
241: 
242:     for (i, chunk) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
243:         let local_ro = [
244:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
245:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
246:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
247:         ];
248: 
249:         // Slab test against the chunk's [0, world_size]^3 cube.
250:         let mut t_entry = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
251:         let mut t_exit = f32::INFINITY;
252:         for axis in 0..3 {
253:             let t1 = (0.0 - local_ro[axis]) * inv_rd[axis];
254:             let t2 = (chunk.world_size - local_ro[axis]) * inv_rd[axis];
255:             t_entry = t_entry.max(t1.min(t2));
256:             t_exit = t_exit.min(t1.max(t2));
257:         }
258: 
259:         if t_entry < t_exit && t_exit > 0.0 && t_entry < max_t {
260:             hits.push(ChunkHit {
261:                 idx: i,
262:                 t_min: t_entry.max(0.0),
263:             });
264:         }
265:     }
266: 
267:     // OPTIMIZATION (rt_f2b): nearest chunk first permits the first valid hit
268:     // to return immediately. The disabled reference path visits input order
269:     // and explicitly retains the nearest hit, producing the same answer.
270:     if front_to_back {
271:         hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.t_min.total_cmp(&b.t_min));
272:     }
273: 
274:     let mut closest = None;
275:     for hit in hits {
276:         let chunk = &chunks[hit.idx];
277:         let local_ro = [
278:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
279:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
280:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
281:         ];
282: 
283:         if let Some(ray_hit) = raymarch_svo_single(
284:             atlas,
285:             local_ro,
286:             safe_rd,
287:             chunk.root_index as usize,
288:             hit.t_min,
289:             chunk.world_size,
290:         ) {
291:             // BUG FIX (cone light): the old code ignored `max_t` once inside
292:             // a chunk, so a wall *behind* the lit surface could "occlude"
293:             // the flashlight ray and randomly black out beam splats.
294:             if ray_hit.t <= max_t {
295:                 if front_to_back {
296:                     return Some(ray_hit);
297:                 }
298:                 if closest.is_none_or(|current: RayHit| ray_hit.t < current.t) {
299:                     closest = Some(ray_hit);
300:                 }
301:             }
302:         }
303:     }
304: 
305:     closest
306: }
307: 
308: #[cfg(test)]
309: mod tests {
310:     use super::nonzero_direction;
311: 
312:     #[test]
313:     fn axis_aligned_zero_gets_a_finite_slab_divisor() {
314:         for component in [0.0, -0.0, 1.0e-8, -1.0e-8] {
315:             let safe = nonzero_direction(component);
316:             assert!(safe != 0.0);
317:             assert!((1.0 / safe).is_finite());
318:         }
319:     }
320: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Tuning knobs for the CPU splatter.
 2: //!
 3: //! Two kinds of control live here:
 4: //!
 5: //! * **Quality/perf scalars** (`CpuRenderSettings`) — continuous knobs the
 6: //!   settings menu and the URL adjust: internal resolution, LOD thresholds,
 7: //!   fog shape, draw distance.
 8: //! * **Optimization switches** (`toggles`) — the shared
 9: //!   [`RenderToggles`] switchboard; every labeled optimization in this
10: //!   renderer can be turned off individually to fall back to the simple
11: //!   reference behavior.
12: //!
13: //! The struct is plain data: the browser driver copies it in once per frame
14: //! (`drivers::cpu_canvas`), so the rasterizer itself never touches globals.
15: 
16: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;
17: 
18: /// Per-splat shadow tracing mode.
19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
20: pub enum CpuShadowMode {
21:     /// No shadow rays at all.
22:     Off,
23:     /// Trace toward the nearest assumed ceiling fixture, amortized over
24:     /// frames through a position-hashed cache (see
25:     /// `rasterizer::SoftwareRasterizer::shadow_factor`).
26:     Hero,
27: }
28: 
29: /// All scalar knobs for the software rasterizer, plus the shared
30: /// optimization switchboard.
31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
32: pub struct CpuRenderSettings {
33:     /// Internal resolution multiplier on top of the driver's 480x270 cap
34:     /// (0.25 ..= 1.0).
35:     pub internal_scale: f32,
36:     /// Projected-radius threshold (px) below which a subtree becomes one
37:     /// MIP splat (0.25 ..= 2.0). Smaller = more detail, more nodes visited.
38:     pub lod_cutoff_px: f32,
39:     /// A collapsed solid leaf is virtually subdivided until its splat is at
40:     /// most this many half-pixels wide (2.0 ..= 16.0).
41:     pub max_splat_half_px: f32,
42:     /// Recursion cap for that virtual subdivision (3 ..= 8).
43:     pub max_virtual_depth: u8,
44:     /// World-space floor for virtual subdivision, so degenerate splits
45:     /// can't recurse into dust.
46:     pub min_split_size: f32,
47:     /// Exponential fog density (0.003 ..= 0.03).
48:     pub fog_density: f32,
49:     /// Distance where fog starts accumulating.
50:     pub fog_start: f32,
51:     /// Chunk/node rejection distance in world units.
52:     pub max_draw_distance: f32,
53:     /// Minimum subtree occupancy for a distant MIP splat to draw at all —
54:     /// preserves sparse far detail without spraying near-empty splats.
55:     pub min_mip_occupancy: f32,
56:     /// Per-splat shadow rays (Off / Hero).
57:     pub shadows: CpuShadowMode,
58:     /// tan(vertical FOV / 2); 0.767 = the 75-degree default.
59:     pub fov_tan: f32,
60:     /// Per-optimization on/off switches shared with the GPU paths.
61:     pub toggles: RenderToggles,
62: }
63: 
64: impl Default for CpuRenderSettings {
65:     fn default() -> Self {
66:         Self {
67:             internal_scale: 1.0,
68:             lod_cutoff_px: 1.0,
69:             max_splat_half_px: 12.0,
70:             max_virtual_depth: 5,
71:             min_split_size: 0.02,
72:             fog_density: 0.015,
73:             fog_start: 0.0,
74:             max_draw_distance: 96.0,
75:             min_mip_occupancy: 0.25,
76:             shadows: CpuShadowMode::Off,
77:             fov_tan: 0.767, // 75 deg vertical FOV
78:             toggles: RenderToggles::default(),
79:         }
80:     }
81: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading.rs
````rust
  1: //! Per-splat shading — the CPU path's lighting model, one small function
  2: //! per light term. Because it runs per *splat* (not per pixel), it can
  3: //! afford to be richer than the GPU paths:
  4: //!
  5: //! * BFS-propagated static light (same atlas data as the GPU),
  6: //! * per-face directional response (tops bright, bottoms dark),
  7: //! * contact AO from octant crowding,
  8: //! * the flashlight cone ([`super::flashlight`]),
  9: //! * dynamic point lights (dropped flares),
 10: //! * exponential distance fog toward the level's palette.
 11: //!
 12: //! A splat has no true normal (it is an axis-aligned box seen from some
 13: //! direction), so the normal is *approximated* from the squared components
 14: //! of the camera→center direction: the axis you look at most contributes
 15: //! most. This soft blend is deliberate — see the
 16: //! `test_face_shading_discontinuity` regression test.
 17: 
 18: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, Environment};
 19: 
 20: use super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 21: use super::flashlight;
 22: use super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 23: 
 24: /// Everything the lighting model needs to know about one splat.
 25: pub struct SplatSurface {
 26:     /// World-space center of the shaded box.
 27:     pub center: [f32; 3],
 28:     /// World-space side length of the box.
 29:     pub world_size: f32,
 30:     /// Camera-space depth (used for fog).
 31:     pub dist: f32,
 32:     /// Albedo, 0..255 per channel.
 33:     pub base_color: [f32; 3],
 34:     /// BFS light level, 0..15.
 35:     pub light_level: f32,
 36:     pub is_emissive: bool,
 37:     /// Number of occupied siblings in the parent octant (contact AO).
 38:     pub crowded_siblings: u32,
 39:     /// Hero-light shadow factor, 1.0 = unshadowed.
 40:     pub shadow_factor: f32,
 41: }
 42: 
 43: /// Squared directional weights and outward signs of the camera→surface
 44: /// vector; the shared basis for the approximate normal and face response.
 45: struct AxisBlend {
 46:     /// Normalized squared weights per axis (sum to 1).
 47:     weights: [f32; 3],
 48:     /// Which side of each axis faces the camera (+1/-1).
 49:     signs: [f32; 3],
 50:     valid: bool,
 51: }
 52: 
 53: impl AxisBlend {
 54:     fn from_to_camera(to_cam: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 55:         let sq = [
 56:             to_cam[0] * to_cam[0],
 57:             to_cam[1] * to_cam[1],
 58:             to_cam[2] * to_cam[2],
 59:         ];
 60:         let sum = sq[0] + sq[1] + sq[2];
 61:         if sum <= 1e-6 {
 62:             return Self {
 63:                 weights: [0.0; 3],
 64:                 signs: [1.0; 3],
 65:                 valid: false,
 66:             };
 67:         }
 68:         Self {
 69:             weights: [sq[0] / sum, sq[1] / sum, sq[2] / sum],
 70:             signs: [
 71:                 if to_cam[0] > 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
 72:                 if to_cam[1] > 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
 73:                 if to_cam[2] > 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 },
 74:             ],
 75:             valid: true,
 76:         }
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     /// The blended approximate surface normal (unit-ish).
 80:     fn normal(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 81:         let n = [
 82:             self.signs[0] * self.weights[0],
 83:             self.signs[1] * self.weights[1],
 84:             self.signs[2] * self.weights[2],
 85:         ];
 86:         let len = dot(n, n).sqrt().max(0.001);
 87:         [n[0] / len, n[1] / len, n[2] / len]
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     /// Signed vertical component of the approximate normal (for the
 91:     /// hemisphere ambient mix).
 92:     fn n_y(&self) -> f32 {
 93:         self.signs[1] * self.weights[1]
 94:     }
 95: }
 96: 
 97: /// Directional face response: upward faces brightest (1.0), downward
 98: /// darkest (0.35), walls in between with a subtle cardinal variation —
 99: /// identical weights to the GPU surface shader.
100: fn face_response(blend: &AxisBlend) -> f32 {
101:     if !blend.valid {
102:         return 0.8;
103:     }
104:     let y_resp = if blend.signs[1] > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.35 };
105:     let wall_resp = 0.65 + 0.1 * blend.signs[0] + 0.05 * blend.signs[2];
106:     blend.weights[1] * y_resp + (blend.weights[0] + blend.weights[2]) * wall_resp
107: }
108: 
109: /// Contact AO from octant crowding, clamped so corners never go pure black.
110: fn contact_ao(crowded_siblings: u32) -> f32 {
111:     let raw = 1.0 - 0.04 * crowded_siblings.saturating_sub(1) as f32;
112:     (raw * 1.3).clamp(0.22, 1.0)
113: }
114: 
115: /// Hemisphere ambient: a fluorescent yellow-green top against a dark olive
116: /// bottom indoors; a cool neutral daylight pair outdoors.
117: fn ambient_term(
118:     env: &Environment,
119:     light_norm: f32,
120:     blend: &AxisBlend,
121:     ao: f32,
122:     face: f32,
123: ) -> [f32; 3] {
124:     let t_mix = blend.n_y() * 0.5 + 0.5;
125:     let (up, down) = if env.outdoor {
126:         ([0.98, 1.02, 1.08], [0.56, 0.58, 0.55])
127:     } else {
128:         ([1.05, 1.0, 0.7], [0.6, 0.55, 0.35])
129:     };
130:     let mut ambient = [0.0; 3];
131:     for c in 0..3 {
132:         let hemi = down[c] * (1.0 - t_mix) + up[c] * t_mix;
133:         ambient[c] = hemi * light_norm * ao * face;
134:     }
135:     ambient
136: }
137: 
138: /// Dynamic point lights (dropped flares): quadratic falloff, no occlusion
139: /// test — the CPU path has no ray budget for one per light, and the small
140: /// radius keeps light from reading through far walls.
141: fn dynamic_light_term(cam: &Camera, center: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
142:     let mut sum = [0.0f32; 3];
143:     for light in &cam.dynamic_lights[..cam.dynamic_light_count] {
144:         let lx = light.position[0] - center[0];
145:         let ly = light.position[1] - center[1];
146:         let lz = light.position[2] - center[2];
147:         let d2 = lx * lx + ly * ly + lz * lz;
148:         let r2 = light.radius * light.radius;
149:         if d2 >= r2 {
150:             continue;
151:         }
152:         let atten = (1.0 - d2 / r2).powi(2) * light.intensity;
153:         sum[0] += light.color[0] * atten;
154:         sum[1] += light.color[1] * atten;
155:         sum[2] += light.color[2] * atten;
156:     }
157:     sum
158: }
159: 
160: /// Exponential fog toward the level palette's clear color. Returns final
161: /// display RGB.
162: fn fog_blend(
163:     color: [f32; 3],
164:     dist: f32,
165:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
166:     env: &Environment,
167: ) -> [u8; 3] {
168:     let fog = (-settings.fog_density * (dist - settings.fog_start).max(0.0)).exp();
169:     // Indoors the haze is the hand-tuned sickly brown; outdoors it fades to
170:     // the environment's bright sky haze.
171:     let clear = if env.outdoor {
172:         [
173:             env.fog_color[0] * 255.0,
174:             env.fog_color[1] * 255.0,
175:             env.fog_color[2] * 255.0,
176:         ]
177:     } else {
178:         [0.15 * 255.0, 0.125 * 255.0, 0.055 * 255.0]
179:     };
180:     let mut out = [0u8; 3];
181:     for c in 0..3 {
182:         out[c] = (color[c] * fog + clear[c] * (1.0 - fog)).clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8;
183:     }
184:     out
185: }
186: 
187: /// Full lighting for one splat: combines every term above and returns
188: /// display-ready RGB.
189: pub fn shade(
190:     cam: &Camera,
191:     env: &Environment,
192:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
193:     atlas: &[u32],
194:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
195:     surface: &SplatSurface,
196: ) -> [u8; 3] {
197:     // Emissive fixtures skip lighting entirely: they *are* the light.
198:     if surface.is_emissive {
199:         let boosted = [
200:             surface.base_color[0] * 1.5,
201:             surface.base_color[1] * 1.5,
202:             surface.base_color[2] * 1.5,
203:         ];
204:         return fog_blend(boosted, surface.dist, settings, env);
205:     }
206: 
207:     let to_cam = [
208:         surface.center[0] - cam.pos[0],
209:         surface.center[1] - cam.pos[1],
210:         surface.center[2] - cam.pos[2],
211:     ];
212:     let blend = AxisBlend::from_to_camera(to_cam);
213: 
214:     let face = face_response(&blend);
215:     let ao = contact_ao(surface.crowded_siblings);
216:     let light_norm = (surface.light_level / 15.0) * surface.shadow_factor * env.ambient_scale;
217:     let ambient = ambient_term(env, light_norm, &blend, ao, face);
218: 
219:     let beam = if cam.flashlight && blend.valid {
220:         let normal = blend.normal();
221:         // Shade the visible face, not the box center: offset half a box
222:         // along the approximate normal.
223:         let surface_pos = [
224:             surface.center[0] + normal[0] * surface.world_size * 0.5,
225:             surface.center[1] + normal[1] * surface.world_size * 0.5,
226:             surface.center[2] + normal[2] * surface.world_size * 0.5,
227:         ];
228:         flashlight::beam_contribution(cam, atlas, chunks, surface_pos, normal, &settings.toggles)
229:     } else {
230:         [0.0; 3]
231:     };
232: 
233:     let dynamic = dynamic_light_term(cam, surface.center);
234: 
235:     let mut lit = [0.0f32; 3];
236:     for c in 0..3 {
237:         lit[c] = surface.base_color[c] * (ambient[c] + beam[c] + dynamic[c]);
238:     }
239:     fog_blend(lit, surface.dist, settings, env)
240: }
````

````rust
 13: /// depth-2 SVO (4^3) with one solid voxel, serialized like production.
 14: fn one_voxel_atlas(color: u32, light: u8) -> (Vec<u32>, u32) {
 15:     let mut svo = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
 16:     svo.set(1, 1, 1, 1, color, [light; 3], 0);
 17:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 18:     (gpu.texel_data, svo.root as u32)
 19: }

 21: fn frame_at(pos: [f32; 3], yaw: f32) -> FrameParams {
 22:     FrameParams {
 23:         camera_pos: pos,
 24:         yaw,
 25:         pitch: 0.0,
 26:         flashlight: false,
 27:         ..FrameParams::default()
 28:     }
 29: }
 30: 
 31: fn center_pixel(r: &SoftwareRasterizer) -> [u8; 4] {
 32:     let idx = (r.height() / 2 * r.width() + r.width() / 2) * 4;
 33:     let fb = r.framebuffer();
 34:     [fb[idx], fb[idx + 1], fb[idx + 2], fb[idx + 3]]
 35: }

592:     // Two-voxel column along z: near wall at cell z=1, far wall at z=2,
593:     // camera looking down the column. The near wall face is lit; if we
594:     // remove it the far wall would be lit — here we just assert the lit
595:     // face is the near one by depth.

607:     // the near voxel: an occlusion trace stopping short of the far surface
608:     // must report the near wall.

617:     assert!(hit.is_some(), "near wall must occlude");

619: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Renderer optimization toggles — one switch per labeled optimization.
  2: //!
  3: //! Every renderer in the engine (GPU surfaces, GPU face splats, the SVO
  4: //! raymarcher, and the CPU splatter) is written as a *correct, simple
  5: //! reference path* plus a set of clearly labeled optimizations layered on
  6: //! top. Each optimization can be disabled at runtime, which serves three
  7: //! purposes:
  8: //!
  9: //! 1. **Debugging** — when a frame looks wrong, binary-search the toggles to
 10: //!    find which optimization broke it.
 11: //! 2. **Benchmarking** — measure exactly what each optimization buys on a
 12: //!    given machine (the HUD shows frame times).
 13: //! 3. **Documentation** — the toggle list *is* the catalog of every shortcut
 14: //!    the pipeline takes.
 15: //!
 16: //! The struct is plain data with no browser dependencies, so it is natively
 17: //! unit-tested. It crosses the wasm boundary as a bitfield (one `AtomicU32`
 18: //! in `lib.rs`). Each browser driver snapshots it once at the frame boundary;
 19: //! platform-free render code receives the snapshot by value.
 20: //!
 21: //! URL controls: `?rt_hiz=0&rt_shadows=0` … (`rt_<name>=0|1`). The settings
 22: //! menu calls the `set_render_toggle(name, enabled)` wasm export with the
 23: //! same names.
 24: 
 25: /// One on/off switch per optimization, across all render paths.
 26: ///
 27: /// Everything defaults to **on**. Correctness-preserving switches fall back
 28: /// to a slower, simpler path; explicitly documented quality/features
 29: /// (`mip_lod`, cone occlusion, face budget, shadows, dither) intentionally
 30: /// alter fidelity so their cost and artifacts can be isolated.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 32: pub struct RenderToggles {
 33:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 34:     // CPU splatter (SoftwareRasterizer)
 35:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 36:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): 8x8-tile coarse hierarchical z-buffer. Rejects a
 37:     /// whole octree subtree with a handful of tile reads when something
 38:     /// nearer already covers its screen bounds. Off = every node is tested
 39:     /// per-pixel by the fine z-buffer only.
 40:     pub hierarchical_z: bool,
 41:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + raymarch): near-to-far traversal (chunks sorted
 42:     /// by distance, octants visited nearest-first). Maximizes early exits
 43:     /// and z-rejection. Off = input order plus explicit nearest-hit
 44:     /// comparison; identical image, more traversal/overdraw.
 45:     pub front_to_back: bool,
 46:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): coarse-to-fine LOD — a subtree whose projection
 47:     /// fits in ~a pixel is drawn as one MIP-filtered splat instead of being
 48:     /// descended. Off = full descent to leaves regardless of distance, except
 49:     /// for the renderer's non-optional malformed/workload safety cap.
 50:     pub mip_lod: bool,
 51:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): the flashlight's occlusion ray (one SVO trace per
 52:     /// shaded splat while the flashlight is on). This is a *quality*
 53:     /// optimization: off means the beam shines through walls but shading
 54:     /// gets cheaper.
 55:     pub flashlight_occlusion: bool,
 56:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 57:     // GPU paths (surface / splat / raymarch)
 58:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 59:     /// Hero-light shadow-map pass (surface + splat renderers). Off = no
 60:     /// shadow pass, no shadow lookups; the strongest light simply doesn't
 61:     /// cast shadows.
 62:     pub shadow_pass: bool,
 63:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): per-cell instance-range culling. Face instances
 64:     /// are grouped into spatial cells; invisible cells are skipped and
 65:     /// visible neighbors coalesce into one instanced draw. Off = every
 66:     /// resident face is drawn every frame.
 67:     pub cell_culling: bool,
 68:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): stop submitting whole far chunks after the
 69:     /// profile's face budget is exhausted. Off = draw every visible face;
 70:     /// useful as the correctness/reference path when diagnosing pop-out.
 71:     pub face_budget: bool,
 72:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + raster GPU): chunk-level visibility culling
 73:     /// (distance + behind-camera tests). Off = every resident chunk is
 74:     /// submitted.
 75:     pub distance_cull: bool,
 76:     /// Dither/grain/banding-noise post effects (GPU). A visual feature more
 77:     /// than a speedup; toggle to isolate its contribution to the image.
 78:     pub dither: bool,
 79:     /// `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2` GPU frame timing for the HUD. Off =
 80:     /// no queries issued (some drivers stall on them).
 81:     pub gpu_timer: bool,
 82: }
 83: 
 84: impl Default for RenderToggles {
 85:     fn default() -> Self {
 86:         Self {
 87:             hierarchical_z: true,
 88:             front_to_back: true,
 89:             mip_lod: true,
 90:             flashlight_occlusion: true,
 91:             shadow_pass: true,
 92:             cell_culling: true,
 93:             face_budget: true,
 94:             distance_cull: true,
 95:             dither: true,
 96:             gpu_timer: true,
 97:         }
 98:     }
 99: }
100: 
101: /// Canonical query-name/bit ordering used by parsing and bitfield round trips.
102: const TOGGLE_BITS: [(&str, u32); 10] = [
103:     ("hiz", 1 << 0),
104:     ("f2b", 1 << 1),
105:     ("mips", 1 << 2),
106:     ("beam_occlusion", 1 << 3),
107:     ("shadows", 1 << 4),
108:     ("cells", 1 << 5),
109:     ("budget", 1 << 6),
110:     ("cull", 1 << 7),
111:     ("dither", 1 << 8),
112:     ("timer", 1 << 9),
113: ];
114: 
115: impl RenderToggles {
116:     fn field_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut bool> {
117:         Some(match name {
118:             "hiz" => &mut self.hierarchical_z,
119:             "f2b" => &mut self.front_to_back,
120:             "mips" => &mut self.mip_lod,
121:             "beam_occlusion" => &mut self.flashlight_occlusion,
122:             "shadows" => &mut self.shadow_pass,
123:             "cells" => &mut self.cell_culling,
124:             "budget" => &mut self.face_budget,
125:             "cull" => &mut self.distance_cull,
126:             "dither" => &mut self.dither,
127:             "timer" => &mut self.gpu_timer,
128:             _ => return None,
129:         })
130:     }
131: 
132:     fn field(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
133:         let mut copy = *self;
134:         copy.field_mut(name).map(|b| *b)
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Sets one toggle by its short name. Unknown names are ignored (the
138:     /// settings menu and old URLs must never crash the engine).
139:     pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, enabled: bool) {
140:         if let Some(field) = self.field_mut(name) {
141:             *field = enabled;
142:         }
143:     }
144: 
145:     /// Reads one toggle by its short name. Returning `None` for unknown
146:     /// names keeps diagnostics and browser tests on the same catalog as the
147:     /// parser and setter.
148:     pub fn enabled(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
149:         self.field(name)
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Packs the toggles into a bitfield for the atomic global in `lib.rs`.
153:     pub fn to_bits(self) -> u32 {
154:         let mut bits = 0;
155:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
156:             if self.field(name).expect("table names match fields") {
157:                 bits |= bit;
158:             }
159:         }
160:         bits
161:     }
162: 
163:     /// Inverse of [`Self::to_bits`].
164:     pub fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Self {
165:         let mut toggles = Self::default();
166:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
167:             toggles.set(name, bits & bit != 0);
168:         }
169:         toggles
170:     }
171: }
172: 
173: /// Applies `rt_<name>=0|1` pairs from a URL query (with or without the
174: /// leading `?`) on top of the defaults. Unknown keys and malformed values
175: /// are ignored, matching the generation-knob parser's tolerance.
176: pub fn parse_render_toggles(query: &str) -> RenderToggles {
177:     let mut toggles = RenderToggles::default();
178:     for pair in query.trim_start_matches('?').split('&') {
179:         let Some((key, value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
180:             continue;
181:         };
182:         let Some(name) = key.strip_prefix("rt_") else {
183:             continue;
184:         };
185:         match value {
186:             "0" | "false" | "off" => toggles.set(name, false),
187:             "1" | "true" | "on" => toggles.set(name, true),
188:             _ => {}
189:         }
190:     }
191:     toggles
192: }
193:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/light_volume.rs
````rust
 1: //! Baked 3D light-volume upload, shared by the surface and splat drivers.
 2: 
 3: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 4: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
 5: 
 6: use crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload;
 7: 
 8: /// Uploads a chunk's baked RGB light volume as a linearly-filtered 3D
 9: /// texture (the fragment shaders sample it at world positions).
10: pub fn upload_light_volume(gl: &Gl, mesh: &SurfaceMeshPayload) -> Result<WebGlTexture, JsValue> {
11:     let texture = gl
12:         .create_texture()
13:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create light texture"))?;
14:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Some(&texture));
15:     // RGB rows are width*3 bytes — rarely 4-aligned, and the default
16:     // unpack alignment of 4 makes texImage3D reject the upload.
17:     gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1);
18:     gl.tex_image_3d_with_opt_u8_array(
19:         Gl::TEXTURE_3D,
20:         0,
21:         Gl::RGB8 as i32,
22:         mesh.light_volume_size[0] as i32,
23:         mesh.light_volume_size[1] as i32,
24:         mesh.light_volume_size[2] as i32,
25:         0,
26:         Gl::RGB,
27:         Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
28:         Some(&mesh.light_volume),
29:     )?;
30:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
31:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
32:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
33:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
34:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_R, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
35:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, None);
36:     Ok(texture)
37: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Per-frame light selection — one implementation for the surface and
  2: //! splat renderers, which previously carried diverging copies.
  3: //!
  4: //! Inputs: fixture lights from every visible chunk (deduplicated by id —
  5: //! a fixture near a chunk border is listed by several chunks) plus the
  6: //! frame's dynamic lights (dropped flares). The four most important lights
  7: //! win the shader's uniform slots; the most important *fixture* light also
  8: //! wins the hero shadow map (a flare at ankle height would collapse the
  9: //! top-down shadow frustum, so dynamic lights never own it).
 10: //!
 11: //! Importance = radius * sqrt(intensity) / (distance² + 0.1): bigger and
 12: //! brighter lights reach farther, nearby lights dominate.
 13: 
 14: use crate::application::ports::{FrameParams, LightSource};
 15: 
 16: /// Maximum shader light slots (matches the GLSL uniform arrays).
 17: pub const MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS: usize = 4;
 18: 
 19: /// The frame's selected lights, packed for `uniform[1i|3fv|4fv]` upload.
 20: pub struct SelectedLights {
 21:     pub count: usize,
 22:     pub positions: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 23:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 24:     /// Per light: radius, intensity, half_size.x, half_size.y.
 25:     pub params: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 26:     /// Slot index of the shadow-casting hero light, or -1.
 27:     pub hero_slot: i32,
 28:     /// Hero light's position/radius (meaningful when `hero_slot >= 0`).
 29:     pub hero_position: [f32; 3],
 30:     pub hero_radius: f32,
 31: }
 32: 
 33: /// Wraps the frame's dynamic lights as fixture-shaped sources with sentinel
 34: /// ids in the top range, so one selection pass handles both kinds.
 35: pub fn dynamic_light_sources(frame: &FrameParams) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 36:     frame
 37:         .active_dynamic_lights()
 38:         .iter()
 39:         .enumerate()
 40:         .map(|(i, d)| LightSource {
 41:             id: u64::MAX - i as u64,
 42:             position: d.position,
 43:             half_size: [0.25, 0.25],
 44:             color: d.color,
 45:             radius: d.radius,
 46:             intensity: d.intensity,
 47:             flicker_mode: 0,
 48:             enabled: true,
 49:         })
 50:         .collect()
 51: }
 52: 
 53: fn is_dynamic(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
 54:     light.id > u64::MAX - 16
 55: }
 56: 
 57: /// Selects and packs the frame's lights. `fixtures` should already be
 58: /// deduplicated by id (pass a `HashMap`'s values); `dynamic` comes from
 59: /// [`dynamic_light_sources`].
 60: pub fn select_lights<'a>(
 61:     fixtures: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
 62:     dynamic: &'a [LightSource],
 63:     frame: &FrameParams,
 64: ) -> SelectedLights {
 65:     let mut ranked: Vec<(&LightSource, f32)> = fixtures
 66:         .chain(dynamic.iter())
 67:         .map(|light| {
 68:             let dx = light.position[0] - frame.camera_pos[0];
 69:             let dy = light.position[1] - frame.camera_pos[1];
 70:             let dz = light.position[2] - frame.camera_pos[2];
 71:             let dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
 72:             (light, light.radius * light.intensity.sqrt() / (dist2 + 0.1))
 73:         })
 74:         .collect();
 75:     ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 76: 
 77:     let count = ranked.len().min(MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS);
 78:     let mut selected = SelectedLights {
 79:         count,
 80:         positions: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 81:         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 82:         params: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 83:         hero_slot: -1,
 84:         hero_position: [0.0; 3],
 85:         hero_radius: 0.0,
 86:     };
 87:     for (i, (light, _)) in ranked[..count].iter().enumerate() {
 88:         selected.positions[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
 89:         selected.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
 90:         selected.params[i * 4] = light.radius;
 91:         selected.params[i * 4 + 1] = light.intensity;
 92:         selected.params[i * 4 + 2] = light.half_size[0];
 93:         selected.params[i * 4 + 3] = light.half_size[1];
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     // Hero shadow: the strongest *fixture* light in the selected slots.
 97:     if let Some(slot) = ranked[..count].iter().position(|(l, _)| !is_dynamic(l)) {
 98:         selected.hero_slot = slot as i32;
 99:         selected.hero_position = ranked[slot].0.position;
100:         selected.hero_radius = ranked[slot].0.radius;
101:     }
102:     selected
103: }
104: 
105: /// Flare-core uniforms (`uCoreCount`/`uCores`/`uCoreColors`), independent of
106: /// the merged light slots so a flare culled from the four shading lights
107: /// still shows its ember.
108: pub struct FlareCores {
109:     pub count: i32,
110:     /// xyz = position, w = pre-flickered intensity.
111:     pub pos_intensity: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
112:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
113: }
114: 
115: pub fn flare_cores(frame: &FrameParams) -> FlareCores {
116:     let cores = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
117:     let mut packed = FlareCores {
118:         count: cores.len() as i32,
119:         pos_intensity: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
120:         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
121:     };
122:     for (i, c) in cores.iter().enumerate() {
123:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4..i * 4 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.position);
124:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4 + 3] = c.intensity;
125:         packed.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.color);
126:     }
127:     packed
128: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/math.rs
````rust
  1: //! Camera and light matrices — column-major, ready for `uniformMatrix4fv`.
  2: 
  3: use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
  4: 
  5: /// View + projection for the raster paths, from the same yaw/pitch basis
  6: /// the raymarcher and the CPU splatter use, so every renderer frames the
  7: /// world identically.
  8: pub fn camera_matrices(
  9:     frame: &FrameParams,
 10:     width: i32,
 11:     height: i32,
 12:     max_draw_distance: f32,
 13: ) -> ([f32; 16], [f32; 16]) {
 14:     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
 15:     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
 16:     let right = [cy, 0.0, -sy];
 17:     let up = [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy];
 18:     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
 19:     let p = frame.camera_pos;
 20:     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
 21:     let view = [
 22:         right[0],
 23:         up[0],
 24:         -forward[0],
 25:         0.0,
 26:         right[1],
 27:         up[1],
 28:         -forward[1],
 29:         0.0,
 30:         right[2],
 31:         up[2],
 32:         -forward[2],
 33:         0.0,
 34:         -dot(right, p),
 35:         -dot(up, p),
 36:         dot(forward, p),
 37:         1.0,
 38:     ];
 39:     let near = 0.03;
 40:     let far = max_draw_distance + 10.0;
 41:     let f = 1.0 / crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
 42:     let aspect = width as f32 / height.max(1) as f32;
 43:     let projection = [
 44:         f / aspect,
 45:         0.0,
 46:         0.0,
 47:         0.0,
 48:         0.0,
 49:         f,
 50:         0.0,
 51:         0.0,
 52:         0.0,
 53:         0.0,
 54:         (far + near) / (near - far),
 55:         -1.0,
 56:         0.0,
 57:         0.0,
 58:         (2.0 * far * near) / (near - far),
 59:         0.0,
 60:     ];
 61:     (projection, view)
 62: }
 63: 
 64: pub fn ortho_matrix(left: f32, right: f32, bottom: f32, top: f32, near: f32, far: f32) -> [f32; 16] {
 65:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
 66:     m[0] = 2.0 / (right - left);
 67:     m[5] = 2.0 / (top - bottom);
 68:     m[10] = -2.0 / (far - near);
 69:     m[12] = -(right + left) / (right - left);
 70:     m[13] = -(top + bottom) / (top - bottom);
 71:     m[14] = -(far + near) / (far - near);
 72:     m[15] = 1.0;
 73:     m
 74: }
 75: 
 76: /// View matrix for a light looking straight down (-Y), up = -Z. Used by
 77: /// the hero-light shadow pass (ceiling fixtures shine downward).
 78: pub fn look_at_matrix_down(eye: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 16] {
 79:     let forward = [0.0, -1.0, 0.0];
 80:     let up = [0.0, 0.0, -1.0f32];
 81:     let right = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0f32];
 82: 
 83:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
 84:     m[0] = right[0];
 85:     m[1] = up[0];
 86:     m[2] = -forward[0];
 87: 
 88:     m[4] = right[1];
 89:     m[5] = up[1];
 90:     m[6] = -forward[1];
 91: 
 92:     m[8] = right[2];
 93:     m[9] = up[2];
 94:     m[10] = -forward[2];
 95: 
 96:     m[12] = -(right[0] * eye[0] + right[1] * eye[1] + right[2] * eye[2]);
 97:     m[13] = -(up[0] * eye[0] + up[1] * eye[1] + up[2] * eye[2]);
 98:     m[14] = -(-forward[0] * eye[0] + -forward[1] * eye[1] + -forward[2] * eye[2]);
 99:     m[15] = 1.0;
100:     m
101: }
102: 
103: pub fn multiply_matrices(a: &[f32; 16], b: &[f32; 16]) -> [f32; 16] {
104:     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
105:     for col in 0..4 {
106:         for row in 0..4 {
107:             m[col * 4 + row] = a[row] * b[col * 4]
108:                 + a[4 + row] * b[col * 4 + 1]
109:                 + a[8 + row] * b[col * 4 + 2]
110:                 + a[12 + row] * b[col * 4 + 3];
111:         }
112:     }
113:     m
114: }
````
