## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/section_locator.rs
````rust
  1: //! Names the section of the world the player is standing in, for the HUD.
  2: //!
  3: //! The locator re-derives the deterministic region plan for the player's
  4: //! current region (cached per region key, so the plan is recomputed only on
  5: //! a region crossing) and classifies the position against, in priority
  6: //! order: anomaly footprints, assembly footprints, and circulation spines.
  7: //! Platform-agnostic — no browser types — so the classification is natively
  8: //! unit-testable.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 11: use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::{RegionPlan, SpaceProgram};
 12: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 13: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 14: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 15: use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan};
 16: 
 17: /// Backrooms level ids, mirroring the engine's.
 18: const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
 19: 
 20: pub struct SectionLocator {
 21:     seed: u32,
 22:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 23:     noise: SimpleNoiseProvider,
 24:     cached_region: Option<(i64, i64)>,
 25:     plan: Option<RegionPlan>,
 26: }
 27: 
 28: impl SectionLocator {
 29:     pub fn new(seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> Self {
 30:         Self {
 31:             seed,
 32:             config,
 33:             noise: SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
 34:             cached_region: None,
 35:             plan: None,
 36:         }
 37:     }
 38: 
 39:     /// Human-readable "where am I" line for the HUD, e.g.
 40:     /// `LEVEL 0 · PILLAR EXPANSE · REGION (2, -1)`.
 41:     pub fn describe(&mut self, level: u32, x: f32, z: f32) -> String {
 42:         if level == LEVEL_GRASSLAND {
 43:             return "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND".to_string();
 44:         }
 45:         let rx = (x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 46:         let rz = (z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 47:         let zone = self.zone_name(rx, rz, x, z);
 48:         format!("LEVEL {level} · {zone} · REGION ({rx}, {rz})")
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     fn zone_name(&mut self, rx: i64, rz: i64, x: f32, z: f32) -> &'static str {
 52:         if self.cached_region != Some((rx, rz)) {
 53:             self.plan = Some(generate_region_plan(
 54:                 self.seed,
 55:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 56:                 REGION_SIZE,
 57:                 &self.config,
 58:                 &self.noise,
 59:             ));
 60:             self.cached_region = Some((rx, rz));
 61:         }
 62:         let plan = self.plan.as_ref().expect("plan cached above");
 63: 
 64:         // Anomalies dominate: standing inside one matters more than which
 65:         // office footprint it swallowed.
 66:         for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 67:             if anomaly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 68:                 return match anomaly.kind {
 69:                     AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => "PILLAR EXPANSE",
 70:                     AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => "BLACKOUT EXPANSE",
 71:                     AnomalyKind::PitLattice => "PIT LATTICE",
 72:                     AnomalyKind::RedRoom => "RED LOOP",
 73:                     AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => "ARCHWAY ANCHOR",
 74:                 };
 75:             }
 76:         }
 77:         for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 78:             if assembly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 79:                 return program_name(assembly.program);
 80:             }
 81:         }
 82:         for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 83:             if corridor.distance(x, z) <= corridor.width * 0.5 {
 84:                 return program_name(corridor.spine_kind);
 85:             }
 86:         }
 87:         "OPEN FABRIC"
 88:     }
 89: }
 90: 
 91: fn program_name(program: SpaceProgram) -> &'static str {
 92:     match program {
 93:         SpaceProgram::Arrival => "ARRIVAL",
 94:         SpaceProgram::Reception => "RECEPTION",
 95:         SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => "MAIN CORRIDOR",
 96:         SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall => "SECONDARY HALL",
 97:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => "OPEN OFFICE",
 98:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => "PRIVATE OFFICE",
 99:         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => "CONFERENCE ROOM",
100:         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => "WAITING AREA",
101:         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => "BREAK ROOM",
102:         SpaceProgram::Storage => "STORAGE",
103:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => "SERVER ROOM",
104:         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => "RESTROOM CORE",
105:         SpaceProgram::Stair => "STAIRWELL",
106:         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => "MECHANICAL",
107:         SpaceProgram::Atrium => "ATRIUM",
108:         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "ABANDONED EXPANSION",
109:     }
110: }
111: 
112: #[cfg(test)]
113: mod tests {
114:     use super::*;
115:     use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point;
116: 
117:     #[test]
118:     fn grassland_never_computes_a_plan() {
119:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
120:         assert_eq!(
121:             locator.describe(34, 12345.0, -9876.0),
122:             "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND"
123:         );
124:         assert!(locator.plan.is_none(), "no region plan needed outdoors");
125:     }
126: 
127:     #[test]
128:     fn spawn_is_on_the_main_corridor() {
129:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
130:         let at = spawn_point(42);
131:         let text = locator.describe(0, at.x, at.z);
132:         assert!(
133:             text.contains("MAIN CORRIDOR") || text.contains("ARRIVAL"),
134:             "spawn should sit on readable circulation, got: {text}"
135:         );
136:         assert!(text.starts_with("LEVEL 0 · "), "{text}");
137:         assert!(text.contains("REGION (0, 0)"), "{text}");
138:     }
139: 
140:     #[test]
141:     fn region_plan_is_cached_until_a_region_crossing() {
142:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
143:         locator.describe(0, 5.0, 5.0);
144:         let first = locator.cached_region;
145:         locator.describe(0, 6.0, 6.0);
146:         assert_eq!(locator.cached_region, first, "same region: no recompute");
147:         locator.describe(0, 5.0 + REGION_SIZE, 5.0);
148:         assert_ne!(locator.cached_region, first, "crossing must recompute");
149:     }
150: 
151:     #[test]
152:     fn forced_anomaly_is_reported_at_its_own_center() {
153:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
154:         config.anomalies.forced_kind =
155:             Some(vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
156:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, config);
157:         // Find the forced instance's center via the same plan the locator
158:         // uses; standing on its center must classify as the anomaly.
159:         let plan = generate_region_plan(
160:             42,
161:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
162:             REGION_SIZE,
163:             &config,
164:             &SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
165:         );
166:         let forced = plan
167:             .anomalies
168:             .iter()
169:             .find(|a| a.kind == vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
170:         if let Some(instance) = forced {
171:             let c = instance.footprint.center;
172:             let text = locator.describe(0, c.x, c.z);
173:             assert!(text.contains("PILLAR EXPANSE"), "{text}");
174:         }
175:     }
176: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/console_telemetry.rs
````rust
 1: //! Browser implementation of the core's `TelemetryPort`:
 2: //! `performance.now()` for durations, `console.log` for output.
 3: 
 4: use vackrooms::use_cases::ports::TelemetryPort;
 5: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 6: 
 7: pub struct ConsoleTelemetry;
 8: 
 9: /// Shared instance handed to use cases as `&'static dyn TelemetryPort`.
10: pub static CONSOLE_TELEMETRY: ConsoleTelemetry = ConsoleTelemetry;
11: 
12: impl TelemetryPort for ConsoleTelemetry {
13:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64 {
14:         web_sys::window()
15:             .and_then(|w| w.performance())
16:             .map(|p| (p.now() * 1000.0) as u64)
17:             .unwrap_or(0)
18:     }
19: 
20:     fn log(&self, message: &str) {
21:         web_sys::console::log_1(&JsValue::from_str(message));
22:     }
23: }
````

## File: Cargo.toml
````toml
 1: # Workspace root. Layout:
 2: #   .              -> `vackrooms` core: Entities + Use Cases + Interface Adapters,
 3: #                     plus the native dev server binary (Frameworks & Drivers).
 4: #                     The library is platform-agnostic and also compiles to wasm32.
 5: #   wasm_frontend  -> Browser front end (wasm-bindgen + WebGL2 driver).
 6: #   wasm_raycaster -> Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (kept for reference).
 7: [workspace]
 8: members = [".", "wasm_frontend", "wasm_raycaster"]
 9: 
10: [package]
11: name = "vackrooms"
12: version = "0.1.0"
13: edition = "2024"
14: 
15: [dependencies]
16: # default-features disabled so the `os_rng`/getrandom backend is never pulled in;
17: # every RNG in the engine is deterministically seeded (StdRng::seed_from_u64),
18: # which keeps the core buildable on wasm32-unknown-unknown.
19: rand = { version = "0.10.2", default-features = false, features = ["std", "std_rng"] }
````

  3: ## What is complete

  5: The face path is much better than the original “one raw face per voxel” direction: `faceinstances.rs` derives its instances from the same greedy `MergedQuad` source as the mesh shadow caster, caps large faces to 2.5 world units so flat lighting cannot smear across a huge wall, and buckets them into cells for range-level culling.   7: The GPU driver is also real rather than conceptual. It uploads one packed instance page per chunk, uses instanced drawing, enables hardware depth testing and back-face culling, keeps the 128px/256px hero-shadow profile split, and sets a 40,000-face low-spec budget versus 150,000 high-spec budget.  11: ## Why it locks up
 12: 
 13: The lockup is **not primarily a GPU splat issue**. The game remains single-threaded WASM: when a new section is required, `LocalChunkSource::load()` synchronously performs the full pipeline—halo generation, crop, surface-mesh/face-instance extraction, SVO construction, GPU serialization, and collision-AABB extraction—before the browser can render the next frame.  14: 
 15: Your engine does limit the *number* of loads per tick, and it loads coarse chunks before later refinement, but each selected load is still an indivisible, blocking job. The codebase’s architecture notes explicitly identify that there is no background meshing thread in single-threaded WASM; the current answer is time slicing, while Web Worker/WASM-thread generation is listed as the future solution.  16: 
 17: The likely trigger when crossing into another chunk is therefore:
 18: 
 19: ```text
 20: Player crosses streaming boundary
 21: -> required resident set changes
 22: -> Engine calls synchronous ChunkSource::load()
 23: -> one whole chunk pipeline runs on the main WASM/UI thread
 24: -> rendering/input/event loop cannot run
 25: -> visible freeze
 26: ```
 27: 
 28: The initial load may feel acceptable because it happens behind the loading overlay. Later section generation happens while the player is moving, so the same cost becomes a lock-up.
 29: 
 30: ## Multithreading target
 31: 
 32: Move **only pure chunk construction** to workers first. Keep the game loop, WebGL, renderer resource ownership, player state, input, and chunk-store mutation on the main thread.
 33: 
 34: ```text
 35: Main thread
 36:   StreamingPolicy decides required chunk keys
 37:   -> enqueue (origin, LOD, seed, config, request generation)
 38:   -> continue rendering current resident set
 39:   <- receive completed ChunkPayload
 40:   -> validate request is still wanted
 41:   -> upload face/mesh/light GPU buffers
 42:   -> install collision + chunk payload
 43: 
 44: Worker pool
 45:   Generate architectural VoxelGrid with halo
 46:   -> BFS voxel lighting
 47:   -> build greedy surface mesh / face instances
 48:   -> build SVO + serialize atlas data
 49:   -> extract collision AABBs
 50:   -> post ChunkPayload back
 51: ```
 52: 
 53: This split is clean because `LocalChunkSource::load()` already encapsulates exactly those pure operations, and its output is a self-contained `ChunkPayload`.  55: ## Do this before threads
 56: 
 57: Before adding workers, add per-stage timing around `load()` so you know what actually freezes:
 58: 
 59: - Region/architectural generation
 60: - BFS light propagation
 61: - Surface mesh + face-instance extraction
 62: - SVO build
 63: - GPU serialization
 64: - Collision extraction
 65: - Main-thread GPU buffer upload
 66: 
 67: Your telemetry already has a port architecture, and the renderer already exposes GPU timing and splat counts, so adding per-chunk CPU stage timings will identify whether the main offender is generation, mesh extraction, SVO recursion, or WebGL upload.  69: Also make the main thread reject stale work: if the player has moved away before a worker completes a chunk, discard its payload rather than uploading it. Worker results must be keyed by `(origin, lod, generation_epoch)` so an old fine result cannot overwrite a newer resident decision.
 70: 
 71: ## Worker constraints
 72: 
 73: WebAssembly threads with shared memory require cross-origin isolation in browsers, typically `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` plus `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. If you do not want to impose that immediately, use ordinary Web Workers with a second WASM instance and transfer completed typed-array payloads back; it will still remove the visible UI freeze, though payload transfer/allocation overhead must be measured.
 74: 
 75: Do **not** share a WebGL context with generation workers. WebGL buffer and texture creation should remain on the render thread; workers should output plain serialized chunk data.
 76: 
 77: ## The flashlight-grey bug
 78: 
 79: Your wall source color is still correct in the underlying world data: `VOXELWALL` maps to `0xddcc66`, which is the yellow-beige wall color you expect.  80: 
 81: So if the flashlight turns the wall grey, the defect is in the **splat shader’s lighting combination**, not in architecture generation or the face-instance material ID. The GPU face instance carries a material field, baked light, AO, normal axis, and flags; the driver also passes flashlight state, the 3D light volume, up to four lights, and the hero shadow map into the splat shader.  82: 
 83: The most likely failure modes are:
 84: 
 85: 1. **Direct flashlight light is added as neutral grey after albedo is lost**, such as writing `vec3(lightAmount)` instead of multiplying yellow wall albedo by illumination.
 86: 2. **The flashlight bypasses or overwrites the material palette**, especially if the shader branches into a generic “lit surface” color.
 87: 3. **The 3D light volume is treated as grayscale intensity instead of RGB indirect light**, removing the warm/yellow information under direct illumination.
 88: 4. **The flat vertex-stage light output uses a white direct term but fails to preserve `materialColor`**, then fog simply mixes the already-grey result.
 89: 5. **The face material mapping differs from the greedy shader mapping**, so wall instances resolve to a default grey material rather than `VOXELWALL`.
 90: 
 91: The evidence points away from missing material data: `PackedFaceInstance` explicitly uploads `material`, and wall color is defined in the core SVO builder.  92: 
 93: ## Correct lighting rule
 94: 
 95: Every non-emissive surface should follow this rule:
 96: 
 97: \[
 98: \text{final surface color} =
 99: \text{wall albedo} \times
100: (\text{indirect light} + \text{direct flashlight/light contribution})
101: \]
102: 
103: Not this:
104: 
105: \[
106: \text{final surface color} =
107: \text{indirectly colored wall} + \text{white flashlight replacement}
108: \]
109: 
110: In shader terms, make the material color the immutable base:
111: 
112: ```glsl
113: vec3 albedo = materialColor(aFaceMeta.w); // wall -> vec3(0.867, 0.800, 0.400)
114: 
115: vec3 indirect = sampleLightVolume(faceCenter) * aoTerm;
116: vec3 direct = flashlightTerm + selectedFixtureTerms;
117: vec3 lighting = max(indirect, vec3(0.04)) + direct;
118: 
119: // Preserve material hue under all direct illumination.
120: vec3 lit = albedo * lighting;
121: 
122: // Only emissive fixtures bypass ordinary albedo lighting.
123: if (isEmissive) {
124:     lit = max(lit, emissiveFixtureColor);
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: The flashlight should make the walls become **brighter yellow**, perhaps slightly desaturated at extreme brightness after tone mapping, but never neutral grey.
129: 
130: ## Lighting restoration order
131: 
132: 1. Render `materialColor` only—no fog, lights, AO, or shadow—and verify walls are unmistakably `0xddcc66`.
133: 2. Add baked light-volume RGB multiplied by albedo; verify dark walls remain yellow-brown rather than grey.
134: 3. Add AO and face-direction bands.
135: 4. Add flashlight alone; verify it brightens yellow, not replaces it.
136: 5. Add fixture lights.
137: 6. Add hero shadow.
138: 7. Add fog last.
139: 
140: This isolates the exact pass that destroys the wall color instead of tuning all lighting at once.
141: 
142: ## Best next change
143: 
144: Do **not** begin with all the complexity of shared-memory WASM threads. First, profile and split `LocalChunkSource::load()` into measurable stages; then put that pure pipeline in a worker queue while the current renderer keeps drawing the previous resident set. In parallel, add the material-only shader debug mode and fix the flashlight equation before changing any more lighting aesthetics. [ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/6575456/ab41dcc8-f278-45ea-bf6f-5471d0de6e55/repomix-output.json?AWSAccessKeyId=ASIA2F3EMEYEUNKBDGCY&Signature=F%2FDYJSkuyq%2F7o9epLmsNDjRFXyQ%3D&x-amz-security-token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEPL%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJGMEQCIBLo83%2BRB7u8wThue5C96yz28Sm1LtoJD9cbXhhWUtThAiB7Yfj0JmF4YAPykj5galiYafeTL6BujDFOWTtD2sQmEir8BAi7%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F8BEAEaDDY5OTc1MzMwOTcwNSIMVbIUrxiHU%2FAKYJ87KtAEZcM0pjXLz2Mkg7pl18xV%2FSYpnjZ5NXbFXxF7X5YnbhlIZVljbiApa4J0XFqb3WVStFYHwUhqm76dFL%2Flkq47gQdRdM%2F%2B7oA5ZuxGOiZv6EbJTXr2HCnUbMUK4zA8BYKZiavzkpjIUDfM3hmxJHfBPEXoHIxKbyPVkPxEN6P9NA9WqsuQIFxJ4hCMuQHIpKqKm5MDki38U0G4OKlwjEEN2UGQSY4ZT2TWeV%2BN0Z%2FKyf2OZ87FwQKq%2FovUMVnZLweb9mhzeb7nTCNJgCDT3aGIE67RnOQAOuKFQ48L%2B%2FNcK%2BNtz%2Flm7%2BHXpONNlgK2%2F0ulovyLBa%2FGlRMBKwkUrPR38yjD9EdOfNzc31CpiCIaH6q4Mzlqnxfq6XBwPfdhkKI2OlxmaVx3CZ4ybTSBYln1uKZOsTwaQWaYIAyFy9G0NLOEb4q%2F3B%2FLvpfpQHWDG4KDUezz%2BKjIwitmArnFsCpLfxppZfRMmLPV%2BLvE%2BU%2Bk7BFyMXc%2FymY8CrcLyIIu208NHKYsR0%2F22nqqfmneV1RTYVng%2BIlUgdIkvMHhIMdZoy%2FPFjCnuMv3DYCatMnlLg93t%2B2fbOFExP%2Fo0dzDoC7cx3SxyBJ%2BMl0%2B0t45LjpGTwzIHChQKrbuSRtgPmMXs%2FgSuWe06SWIrT5UOdYlr%2B3q%2BE%2FzOYxxcd9tyWMLVOQE5YwnOrcl5TrnrLcPoAoj9L88UQwVXF3qWPSuZQtRLnFSZlKo0LT55j%2Fhr6lfrUyqpVFy9yseh4s2rIkxEuN2kYdTYJUik7u1j1ESyX%2FnJyCwpzCt3sTSBjqZAZvHbt1emQDF054tPL%2F6z%2B0gwNXwe%2BYK8YoT2BbL0J%2FznQgBxYy%2Bf%2F6AfY%2Bgql6QoxtiXr0pLcxg0oAOnPBMqtsKILP1HJiaMofgZb0ndEIbfYJacko5EeBwKmVgnOA3vEPZuBVt7EmuTmu4kVNnwR%2F8xxsfVP7DgGtlhBAZiqMVRaje%2Fkf2njBCdm5cJBKZEmpN9E3Xs4nMeg%3D%3D&Expires=1783708928)

 1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
 2: 
 3: /// Interface for rendering the grid.
 4: pub trait GridRenderer {
 5:     fn render(&self, grid: &Grid) -> String;
 6: }
 7: 
 8: /// A concrete adapter that renders the Grid as an ASCII string.
 9: /// This fulfills the Clean Architecture requirement of decoupling the domain logic
10: /// from the presentation layer.
11: pub struct AsciiRenderer;
12: 
13: impl GridRenderer for AsciiRenderer {
14:     fn render(&self, grid: &Grid) -> String {
15:         let mut output = String::new();
16: 
17:         for y in 0..grid.depth() {
18:             // Top walls for this row
19:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
20:                 let cell = grid.get(x, y).unwrap();
21:                 output.push('+');
22:                 if cell.walls[0] {
23:                     // North
24:                     output.push_str("---");
25:                 } else {
26:                     output.push_str("   ");
27:                 }
28:             }
29:             output.push_str("+\n");
30: 
31:             // Side walls for this row
32:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
33:                 let cell = grid.get(x, y).unwrap();
34:                 if cell.walls[3] {
35:                     // West
36:                     output.push('|');
37:                 } else {
38:                     output.push(' ');
39:                 }
40:                 output.push_str("   "); // Inside of the room
41:             }
42:             // East wall of the last cell in the row
43:             let last_cell = grid.get(grid.width() - 1, y).unwrap();
44:             if last_cell.walls[1] {
45:                 // East
46:                 output.push('|');
47:             } else {
48:                 output.push(' ');
49:             }
50:             output.push('\n');
51:         }
52: 
53:         // Bottom walls for the last row
54:         for x in 0..grid.width() {
55:             let cell = grid.get(x, grid.depth() - 1).unwrap();
56:             output.push('+');
57:             if cell.walls[2] {
58:                 // South
59:                 output.push_str("---");
60:             } else {
61:                 output.push_str("   ");
62:             }
63:         }
64:         output.push_str("+\n");
65: 
66:         output
67:     }
68: }
69:

 1: //! Immutable anomaly plans and deterministic encounter-state snapshots.
 2: //!
 3: //! The public surface remains a single `anomaly` namespace for callers, while
 4: //! its internals follow the domain's actual vocabulary:
 5: //!
 6: //! - [`geometry`] owns rectilinear bounds and coordinate transforms;
 7: //! - [`phenomena`] owns immutable anomaly instances and family parameters;
 8: //! - [`traversal`] owns semantic gates and hazards;
 9: //! - [`reality`] owns snapshots, transitions, and RTY v2 transport.
10: //!
11: //! The planner owns instance placement. Stateful geometry remains pure: a
12: //! chunk is sampled from an [`AnomalyInstance`] plus the matching stamp in a
13: //! [`RealitySnapshot`].
14: 
15: mod geometry;
16: mod phenomena;
17: mod reality;
18: mod traversal;
19:

21: pub use phenomena::*;
22: pub use reality::*;
23: pub use traversal::*;
24: 
25: /// SplitMix64 finalizer shared by stable anomaly identities and fingerprints.
26: /// It stays private to the anomaly aggregate; callers consume only the stable
27: /// domain values produced from it.
28: fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
29:     value ^= value >> 30;
30:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
31:     value ^= value >> 27;
32:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
33:     value ^ (value >> 31)
34: }

## File: src/domain/entities/grid.rs
````rust
 1: use super::cell::Cell;
 2: 
 3: /// Represents the overall 2D layout of the Backrooms level.
 4: /// Contains a flat vector of cells mapped to 2D coordinates for O(1) access.
 5: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 6: pub struct Grid {
 7:     width: usize,
 8:     depth: usize,
 9:     cells: Vec<Cell>,
10: }
11: 
12: impl Grid {
13:     /// Creates a new grid of dimensions width x depth, filled with default unvisited cells.
14:     /// Complexity: O(w * d) to allocate and initialize.
15:     pub fn new(width: usize, depth: usize) -> Self {
16:         let size = width * depth;
17:         let cells = vec![Cell::new(); size];
18: 
19:         Self {
20:             width,
21:             depth,
22:             cells,
23:         }
24:     }
25: 
26:     /// Returns the width of the grid.
27:     /// Complexity: O(1)
28:     pub fn width(&self) -> usize {
29:         self.width
30:     }
31: 
32:     /// Returns the depth (length along the Z axis, or Y in 2D array terms) of the grid.
33:     /// Complexity: O(1)
34:     pub fn depth(&self) -> usize {
35:         self.depth
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Retrieves an immutable reference to a cell at (x, y).
39:     /// Returns None if out of bounds.
40:     /// Complexity: O(1)
41:     pub fn get(&self, x: usize, y: usize) -> Option<&Cell> {
42:         if x >= self.width || y >= self.depth {
43:             None
44:         } else {
45:             Some(&self.cells[y * self.width + x])
46:         }
47:     }
48: 
49:     /// Retrieves a mutable reference to a cell at (x, y).
50:     /// Returns None if out of bounds.
51:     /// Complexity: O(1)
52:     pub fn get_mut(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize) -> Option<&mut Cell> {
53:         if x >= self.width || y >= self.depth {
54:             None
55:         } else {
56:             Some(&mut self.cells[y * self.width + x])
57:         }
58:     }
59: }
60:

64:

## File: src/domain/use_cases/level_builder.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
 2: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 3:     VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid,
 4: };
 5: 
 6: /// Strategy Pattern for generating dense VoxelGrids from abstract room Grids.
 7: /// This fulfills the "engine should be extensible for other backrooms levels" rule.
 8: pub trait LevelBuilder {
 9:     fn build_voxels(&self, grid: &Grid) -> VoxelGrid;
10: }
11: 
12: /// Concrete implementation for Backrooms Level 0.
13: /// Uses smaller voxels (e.g. 8x8x4 per room) to allow realistic light sources.
14: pub struct Level0Builder {
15:     pub room_size: usize,
16:     pub wall_height: usize,
17: }
18: 
19: impl LevelBuilder for Level0Builder {
20:     fn build_voxels(&self, grid: &Grid) -> VoxelGrid {
21:         let rs = self.room_size;
22:         let wh = self.wall_height;
23: 
24:         // Voxel grid dimensions
25:         let vw = grid.width() * rs;
26:         let vh = wh + 3; // Floor (1) + Walls (wh) + Ceiling (1) + Recessed Lights (1)
27:         let vd = grid.depth() * rs;
28: 
29:         let mut voxels = VoxelGrid::new(vw, vh, vd);
30: 
31:         for gy in 0..grid.depth() {
32:             for gx in 0..grid.width() {
33:                 let cell = grid.get(gx, gy).unwrap();
34:                 let base_x = gx * rs;
35:                 let base_z = gy * rs;
36: 
37:                 for lx in 0..rs {
38:                     for lz in 0..rs {
39:                         let vx = base_x + lx;
40:                         let vz = base_z + lz;
41: 
42:                         // Floor
43:                         voxels.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
44: 
45:                         // Walls
46:                         let is_north_wall = lz == 0 && cell.walls[0];
47:                         let is_east_wall = lx == rs - 1 && cell.walls[1];
48:                         let is_south_wall = lz == rs - 1 && cell.walls[2];
49:                         let is_west_wall = lx == 0 && cell.walls[3];
50: 
51:                         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
52:                         let wall_type = if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
53:                             VOXEL_RED_WALL
54:                         } else {
55:                             VOXEL_WALL
56:                         };
57: 
58:                         if is_north_wall || is_east_wall || is_south_wall || is_west_wall {
59:                             for h in 1..=wh {
60:                                 voxels.set(vx, h, vz, wall_type);
61:                             }
62:                         }
63: 
64:                         // Checkerboard fluorescent lights (Realistic light sources)
65:                         // With 16x16 rooms, we can model actual recessed 2x6 fluorescent fixtures.
66:                         let mut is_light = false;
67:                         if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Blackout {
68:                             // Two fixtures per room
69:                             let fixture1 = lx >= 4 && lx < 6 && lz >= 5 && lz < 11;
70:                             let fixture2 = lx >= 10 && lx < 12 && lz >= 5 && lz < 11;
71:                             if fixture1 || fixture2 {
72:                                 is_light = true;
73:                             }
74:                         }
75: 
76:                         if is_light {
77:                             // Recessed light: hole in the ceiling, light block above it
78:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 2, vz, VOXEL_AIR); // hole
79:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT); // light emitting block above
80:                         } else {
81:                             voxels.set(vx, vh - 2, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
82:                         }
83:                     }
84:                 }
85:             }
86:         }
87: 
88:         voxels
89:     }
90: }
````

## File: src/domain/use_cases/path_tracer.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_LIGHT, VoxelGrid};
  2: use rand::RngExt;
  3: use rand::SeedableRng;
  4: use rand::rngs::StdRng;
  5: 
  6: /// A simple 3D DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) Raycaster
  7: fn cast_ray(
  8:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
  9:     x: f32,
 10:     y: f32,
 11:     z: f32,
 12:     dx: f32,
 13:     dy: f32,
 14:     dz: f32,
 15:     max_steps: usize,
 16: ) -> Option<(usize, usize, usize, u8)> {
 17:     let step_x = if dx > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 18:     let step_y = if dy > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 19:     let step_z = if dz > 0.0 { 1 } else { -1 };
 20: 
 21:     let mut t_max_x = if dx != 0.0 {
 22:         (x.floor() + if dx > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - x) / dx
 23:     } else {
 24:         f32::INFINITY
 25:     };
 26:     let mut t_max_y = if dy != 0.0 {
 27:         (y.floor() + if dy > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - y) / dy
 28:     } else {
 29:         f32::INFINITY
 30:     };
 31:     let mut t_max_z = if dz != 0.0 {
 32:         (z.floor() + if dz > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 } - z) / dz
 33:     } else {
 34:         f32::INFINITY
 35:     };
 36: 
 37:     let t_delta_x = if dx != 0.0 {
 38:         (1.0 / dx).abs()
 39:     } else {
 40:         f32::INFINITY
 41:     };
 42:     let t_delta_y = if dy != 0.0 {
 43:         (1.0 / dy).abs()
 44:     } else {
 45:         f32::INFINITY
 46:     };
 47:     let t_delta_z = if dz != 0.0 {
 48:         (1.0 / dz).abs()
 49:     } else {
 50:         f32::INFINITY
 51:     };
 52: 
 53:     let mut ix = x as isize;
 54:     let mut iy = y as isize;
 55:     let mut iz = z as isize;
 56: 
 57:     for _ in 0..max_steps {
 58:         if t_max_x < t_max_y {
 59:             if t_max_x < t_max_z {
 60:                 ix += step_x;
 61:                 t_max_x += t_delta_x;
 62:             } else {
 63:                 iz += step_z;
 64:                 t_max_z += t_delta_z;
 65:             }
 66:         } else {
 67:             if t_max_y < t_max_z {
 68:                 iy += step_y;
 69:                 t_max_y += t_delta_y;
 70:             } else {
 71:                 iz += step_z;
 72:                 t_max_z += t_delta_z;
 73:             }
 74:         }
 75: 
 76:         if ix < 0
 77:             || iy < 0
 78:             || iz < 0
 79:             || ix >= grid.width() as isize
 80:             || iy >= grid.height() as isize
 81:             || iz >= grid.depth() as isize
 82:         {
 83:             break;
 84:         }
 85: 
 86:         let vx = ix as usize;
 87:         let vy = iy as usize;
 88:         let vz = iz as usize;
 89: 
 90:         let v = grid.get(vx, vy, vz);
 91:         if v != VOXEL_AIR {
 92:             return Some((vx, vy, vz, v));
 93:         }
 94:     }
 95:     None
 96: }
 97: 
 98: /// Bakes lighting into the VoxelGrid using Monte Carlo Path Tracing
 99: pub fn bake_path_traced_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid) {
100:     let w = grid.width();
101:     let h = grid.height();
102:     let d = grid.depth();
103: 
104:     let rays_per_voxel = 64;
105:     let max_bounces = 1; // 0 for direct only, 1 for one bounce
106:     let max_steps = 30; // Max ray distance
107: 
108:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(42);
109: 
110:     // We only need to bake lighting into AIR blocks that are adjacent to solid blocks,
111:     // but for simplicity we can bake all AIR blocks, or directly bake solid blocks.
112:     // Actually, baking solid blocks is better. We evaluate light slightly outside the solid block face.
113:     // Since our map_voxel_grid just uses `grid.get_light(x, y, z)` for the solid block itself,
114:     // we can just store the light level in the solid block!
115: 
116:     for z in 0..d {
117:         for y in 0..h {
118:             for x in 0..w {
119:                 let v = grid.get(x, y, z);
120:                 if v == VOXEL_AIR || v == VOXEL_LIGHT {
121:                     continue;
122:                 }
123: 
124:                 // It's a solid block. Let's do path tracing from its center slightly offset by normals.
125:                 // To keep it simple, we shoot rays from the center of the block. If it immediately hits itself,
126:                 // we ignore it. Actually, start rays from the adjacent AIR voxels.
127: 
128:                 let mut total_light = 0.0;
129: 
130:                 // Find an adjacent air voxel to act as the emission point
131:                 let mut px = x as f32 + 0.5;
132:                 let mut py = y as f32 + 0.5;
133:                 let mut pz = z as f32 + 0.5;
134: 
135:                 // Shift point slightly towards the air
136:                 if x > 0 && grid.get(x - 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
137:                     px -= 0.55;
138:                 } else if x < w - 1 && grid.get(x + 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
139:                     px += 0.55;
140:                 } else if y > 0 && grid.get(x, y - 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
141:                     py -= 0.55;
142:                 } else if y < h - 1 && grid.get(x, y + 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
143:                     py += 0.55;
144:                 } else if z > 0 && grid.get(x, y, z - 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
145:                     pz -= 0.55;
146:                 } else if z < d - 1 && grid.get(x, y, z + 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
147:                     pz += 0.55;
148:                 } else {
149:                     continue; // Completely surrounded by solids, no light needed
150:                 }
151: 
152:                 for _ in 0..rays_per_voxel {
153:                     // Random spherical direction
154:                     let theta = rng.random::<f32>() * 2.0 * std::f32::consts::PI;
155:                     let phi = (rng.random::<f32>() * 2.0 - 1.0).acos();
156:                     let dx = phi.sin() * theta.cos();
157:                     let dy = phi.cos();
158:                     let dz = phi.sin() * theta.sin();
159: 
160:                     if let Some((_hx, _hy, _hz, hit_type)) =
161:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py, pz, dx, dy, dz, max_steps)
162:                     {
163:                         if hit_type == VOXEL_LIGHT {
164:                             total_light += 1.0;
165:                         } else if max_bounces > 0 {
166:                             // Secondary bounce (simplified)
167:                             // We don't do a full recursive call to avoid stack/performance issues,
168:                             // just a small probability addition to simulate ambient bounce.
169:                             // If we hit a wall, it bounces a bit of light.
170:                             total_light += 0.05;
171:                         }
172:                     }
173:                 }
174: 
175:                 // Normalize and map to 0-15 scale for compatibility with voxel_mapper
176:                 let mut light_level = ((total_light / rays_per_voxel as f32) * 15.0 * 2.0) as u8;
177:                 if light_level > 15 {
178:                     light_level = 15;
179:                 }
180: 
181:                 grid.set_light(x, y, z, light_level);
182:             }
183:         }
184:     }
185: }
186: 
187: /// Bakes directional face occlusion using DDA raycasting.
188: /// Casts short rays (1-4 voxels) outward from the 6 cardinal faces of each solid block.
189: /// If a ray hits another solid block within the occlusion distance, that face gets shaded (bit set to 1).
190: pub fn bake_face_occlusion(grid: &mut VoxelGrid) {
191:     let w = grid.width();
192:     let h = grid.height();
193:     let d = grid.depth();
194: 
195:     let occlusion_dist = 4; // Max steps to cast
196: 
197:     for z in 0..d {
198:         for y in 0..h {
199:             for x in 0..w {
200:                 let v = grid.get(x, y, z);
201:                 if v == VOXEL_AIR || v == VOXEL_LIGHT {
202:                     continue; // We only need occlusion for solid faces
203:                 }
204: 
205:                 let mut mask = 0u8;
206:                 let px = x as f32 + 0.5;
207:                 let py = y as f32 + 0.5;
208:                 let pz = z as f32 + 0.5;
209: 
210:                 // +X face
211:                 if x < w - 1 && grid.get(x + 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
212:                     if let Some(_) =
213:                         cast_ray(grid, px + 0.51, py, pz, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, occlusion_dist)
214:                     {
215:                         mask |= 1;
216:                     }
217:                 }
218:                 // -X face
219:                 if x > 0 && grid.get(x - 1, y, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
220:                     if let Some(_) =
221:                         cast_ray(grid, px - 0.51, py, pz, -1.0, 0.0, 0.0, occlusion_dist)
222:                     {
223:                         mask |= 2;
224:                     }
225:                 }
226:                 // +Y face
227:                 if y < h - 1 && grid.get(x, y + 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
228:                     if let Some(_) =
229:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py + 0.51, pz, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, occlusion_dist)
230:                     {
231:                         mask |= 4;
232:                     }
233:                 }
234:                 // -Y face
235:                 if y > 0 && grid.get(x, y - 1, z) == VOXEL_AIR {
236:                     if let Some(_) =
237:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py - 0.51, pz, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0, occlusion_dist)
238:                     {
239:                         mask |= 8;
240:                     }
241:                 }
242:                 // +Z face
243:                 if z < d - 1 && grid.get(x, y, z + 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
244:                     if let Some(_) =
245:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py, pz + 0.51, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, occlusion_dist)
246:                     {
247:                         mask |= 16;
248:                     }
249:                 }
250:                 // -Z face
251:                 if z > 0 && grid.get(x, y, z - 1) == VOXEL_AIR {
252:                     if let Some(_) =
253:                         cast_ray(grid, px, py, pz - 0.51, 0.0, 0.0, -1.0, occlusion_dist)
254:                     {
255:                         mask |= 32;
256:                     }
257:                 }
258: 
259:                 grid.set_face_occlusion(x, y, z, mask);
260:             }
261:         }
262:     }
263: }
````

## File: src/frameworks_drivers/simple_noise.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 2: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 3: 
 4: /// SimpleNoiseProvider is a concrete implementation of the NoiseProvider port.
 5: /// It resides in the Frameworks/Drivers layer.
 6: /// In a production scenario, this might wrap `noise-rs` or SIMD-accelerated noise.
 7: /// For Dependency Minimalism, we implement a basic seeded value noise.
 8: pub struct SimpleNoiseProvider;
 9: 
10: impl SimpleNoiseProvider {
11:     pub fn new() -> Self {
12:         Self
13:     }
14: 
15:     /// A deterministic pseudo-random hash function for 2D integer coordinates.
16:     fn hash2d(seed: u32, x: i32, y: i32) -> f32 {
17:         // Simple hash mixing
18:         let mut h = seed
19:             .wrapping_add(x as u32 ^ 0x9E3779B9)
20:             .wrapping_add(y as u32 ^ 0x85EBCA6B);
21:         h ^= h >> 16;
22:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EBCA6B);
23:         h ^= h >> 13;
24:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2AE35);
25:         h ^= h >> 16;
26: 
27:         // Normalize to [-1.0, 1.0]
28:         ((h as f32) / (std::u32::MAX as f32)) * 2.0 - 1.0
29:     }
30: 
31:     /// Linear interpolation
32:     fn lerp(a: f32, b: f32, t: f32) -> f32 {
33:         a + t * (b - a)
34:     }
35: 
36:     /// Smoothstep for softer transitions
37:     fn smoothstep(t: f32) -> f32 {
38:         t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
39:     }
40: }
41: 
42: impl NoiseProvider for SimpleNoiseProvider {
43:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32 {
44:         // Scale frequency to make the fields low-frequency
45:         let freq = 0.05;
46:         let x = position.x * freq;
47:         let y = position.z * freq;
48: 
49:         let x0 = x.floor() as i32;
50:         let x1 = x0 + 1;
51:         let y0 = y.floor() as i32;
52:         let y1 = y0 + 1;
53: 
54:         let tx = x - (x0 as f32);
55:         let ty = y - (y0 as f32);
56: 
57:         let u = Self::smoothstep(tx);
58:         let v = Self::smoothstep(ty);
59: 
60:         let v00 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y0);
61:         let v10 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y0);
62:         let v01 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y1);
63:         let v11 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y1);
64: 
65:         let nx0 = Self::lerp(v00, v10, u);
66:         let nx1 = Self::lerp(v01, v11, u);
67: 
68:         Self::lerp(nx0, nx1, v)
69:     }
70: }
71: 
72: #[cfg(test)]
73: mod tests {
74:     use super::*;
75: 
76:     #[test]
77:     fn test_noise_determinism() {
78:         let provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
79:         let pos = Position::new(42.5, -17.2);
80: 
81:         let val1 = provider.evaluate_2d(123, pos);
82:         let val2 = provider.evaluate_2d(123, pos);
83:         let val3 = provider.evaluate_2d(999, pos);
84: 
85:         assert_eq!(val1, val2);
86:         assert_ne!(val1, val3);
87:     }
88: }
````

  1: use crate::adapters::json_presenter::JsonPresenter;
  2: use crate::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
  3: use crate::adapters::voxel_mapper::VoxelMapper;
  4: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
  5: use crate::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
  6: 
  7: /// WebRendererAdapter acts as a Presenter in Clean Architecture.
  8: /// It translates the core domain object (VoxelGrid) into formats
  9: /// suitable for the Web Presentation layer.
 10: pub struct WebRendererAdapter;
 11: 
 12: impl WebRendererAdapter {
 13:     /// Translates VoxelGrid into a JSON string representing greedy-meshed quads.
 14:     pub fn to_json(grid: &VoxelGrid, _chunk_size: f32) -> String {
 15:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(0.1);
 16:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid(grid);
 17:         JsonPresenter::render_voxels(&quads)
 18:     }
 19: 
 20:     /// Converts VoxelGrid into a Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) and serializes
 21:     /// the flattened node texture buffer and structural metadata to JSON.
 22:     pub fn to_octree_json(grid: &VoxelGrid, depth: u32, world_size: f32) -> String {
 23:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
 24:         let svo = builder.execute(grid, depth, world_size);
 25:         let gpu_data = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 26: 
 27:         let mut json = String::with_capacity(gpu_data.texel_data.len() * 8 + 128);
 28:         json.push_str("{\"root\":");
 29:         json.push_str(&svo.root.to_string());
 30:         json.push_str(",\"depth\":");
 31:         json.push_str(&svo.depth.to_string());
 32:         json.push_str(",\"world_size\":");
 33:         json.push_str(&svo.world_size.to_string());
 34:         json.push_str(",\"nodes\":[");
 35: 
 36:         for (i, &val) in gpu_data.texel_data.iter().enumerate() {
 37:             json.push_str(&val.to_string());
 38:             if i < gpu_data.texel_data.len() - 1 {
 39:                 json.push(',');
 40:             }
 41:         }
 42:         json.push_str("]}");
 43:         json
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     /// High-performance Binary Serializer for SVO Raymarching:
 47:     /// Compiles SVO nodes directly to little-endian bytes to avoid JSON parsing cost.
 48:     ///
 49:     /// BINARY SCHEMATIC (Byte offset -> payload):
 50:     /// - `0..4`: `root` node index (u32, little-endian)
 51:     /// - `4..8`: `depth` of tree (u32, little-endian)
 52:     /// - `8..12`: `world_size` scale (f32, little-endian)
 53:     /// - `12..16`: `texture_width` (u32, little-endian)
 54:     /// - `16..20`: `texture_height` (u32, little-endian)
 55:     /// - `20..24`: `voxel_scale` (f32, little-endian)
 56:     /// - `24..28`: `chunk_size` (f32, little-endian)
 57:     /// - `28..`: flat `u32` texel array data (4 * width * height * 4 bytes)
 58:     pub fn to_octree_binary(
 59:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
 60:         depth: u32,
 61:         world_size: f32,
 62:         voxel_scale: f32,
 63:         chunk_size: f32,
 64:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
 65:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
 66:         let svo = builder.execute(grid, depth, world_size);
 67:         let gpu_data = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 68: 
 69:         let header_size = 28; // 7 values * 4 bytes
 70:         let mut binary = Vec::with_capacity(header_size + gpu_data.texel_data.len() * 4);
 71: 
 72:         binary.extend_from_slice(&(svo.root as u32).to_le_bytes());
 73:         binary.extend_from_slice(&depth.to_le_bytes());
 74:         binary.extend_from_slice(&world_size.to_le_bytes());
 75:         binary.extend_from_slice(&gpu_data.texture_width.to_le_bytes());
 76:         binary.extend_from_slice(&gpu_data.texture_height.to_le_bytes());
 77:         binary.extend_from_slice(&voxel_scale.to_le_bytes());
 78:         binary.extend_from_slice(&chunk_size.to_le_bytes());
 79: 
 80:         for &val in &gpu_data.texel_data {
 81:             binary.extend_from_slice(&val.to_le_bytes());
 82:         }
 83: 
 84:         binary
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: 
 88: #[cfg(test)]
 89: mod tests {
 90:     use super::*;
 91:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
 92: 
 93:     #[test]
 94:     fn test_to_json_format() {
 95:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(2, 2, 2);
 96:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
 97:         let json = WebRendererAdapter::to_json(&grid, 2.0);
 98:         assert!(json.starts_with("["));
 99:     }
100: 
101:     #[test]
102:     fn test_to_octree_binary_format() {
103:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(2, 2, 2);
104:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
105:         let binary = WebRendererAdapter::to_octree_binary(&grid, 8, 25.6, 0.1, 20.0);
106: 
107:         // Header is 28 bytes
108:         assert!(binary.len() >= 28);
109:         // Total bytes must be aligned to 4-byte boundaries
110:         assert_eq!(binary.len() % 4, 0);
111:     }
112: }

 1: //! The pluggable level-generator port: each Backrooms "level" (Level 0
 2: //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
 3: //!
 4: //! Contract for implementors:
 5: //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
 6: //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
 7: //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
 8: //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
 9: //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
10: //!   ~1 world unit wide.
11: //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
12: //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
13: //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the
14: //!   orchestrating use case runs the BFS lighting pass afterwards.

25: pub const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;

## File: src/use_cases/ports.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 2: 
 3: /// The Ports layer implements the Dependency Inversion Principle (SOLID).
 4: /// Instead of the Use Cases depending on a concrete external noise library or framework,
 5: /// the Use Cases define the interface (Port) they need, and the external layers
 6: /// (Adapters/Drivers) must implement this interface.
 7: 
 8: /// NoiseProvider is a pure interface for extracting deterministic continuous noise.
 9: /// We use this to evaluate the Macro Field (Drift, Density, Motif Selection).
10: pub trait NoiseProvider {
11:     /// Returns a noise value, ideally in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
12:     /// The function must be deterministic given the same seed and position.
13:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32;
14: }
15: 
16: /// TelemetryPort abstracts wall-clock access and log emission so Use Cases
17: /// never touch `std::time` or stdout directly. Both are frameworks concerns,
18: /// and `SystemTime::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
19: pub trait TelemetryPort {
20:     /// Monotonic-ish timestamp in microseconds from an arbitrary epoch.
21:     /// Only ever used to compute durations, never absolute dates.
22:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64;
23:     /// Emits one log line to whatever sink the outer layer provides.
24:     fn log(&self, message: &str);
25: }
26: 
27: /// Silent TelemetryPort used by default and in tests.
28: pub struct NullTelemetry;
29: 
30: impl TelemetryPort for NullTelemetry {
31:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64 {
32:         0
33:     }
34:     fn log(&self, _message: &str) {}
35: }
36: 
37: /// Shared instance so constructors can hand out `&'static dyn TelemetryPort`
38: /// without forcing callers to own a telemetry object.
39: pub static NULL_TELEMETRY: NullTelemetry = NullTelemetry;
````

## File: static/worker.js
````javascript
 1: // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, running the
 2: // full chunk pipeline off the main thread. The onmessage handler is
 3: // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
 4: // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
 5: // promise chain.
 6: //
 7: // Protocol (main -> worker):
 8: //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
 9: //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality } one chunk order;
10: //                                                        reality is Uint32Array
11: // (worker -> main):
12: //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality, ms, buf }
13: //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
14: import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";
15: 
16: let wasmReady = null;
17: function ensureWasm() {
18:   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
19:   return wasmReady;
20: }
21: 
22: let queue = Promise.resolve();
23: onmessage = (event) => {
24:   const m = event.data;
25:   queue = queue.then(async () => {
26:     await ensureWasm();
27:     if (m.type === "init") {
28:       worker_init(m.query, m.seed >>> 0);
29:     } else if (m.type === "gen") {
30:       const t0 = performance.now();
31:       const reality = new Uint32Array(m.reality);
32:       const bytes = worker_generate(
33:         m.requestId >>> 0,
34:         m.ox,
35:         m.oz,
36:         m.level,
37:         m.lod,
38:         reality
39:       );
40:       const ms = performance.now() - t0;
41:       console.debug(
42:         `[WORKER] chunk (${m.ox}, ${m.oz}) lod ${m.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
43:       );
44:       postMessage(
45:         {
46:           type: "done",
47:           requestId: m.requestId,
48:           ox: m.ox,
49:           oz: m.oz,
50:           level: m.level,
51:           lod: m.lod,
52:           reality,
53:           ms,
54:           buf: bytes.buffer,
55:         },
56:         [bytes.buffer]
57:       );
58:     }
59:   });
60: };
````

## File: tests/collision_diagnostics.rs

  4: /// Collision Diagnostic Tests — TDD Phase 1
  5: ///
  6: /// WHY THESE TESTS EXIST:
  7: /// The player reported spawning inside a wall.  Before changing any logic
  8: /// we must prove (a) what coordinates the spawn point produces and (b) whether
  9: /// the floor voxel's collision box overlaps the player's AABB at spawn.
 10: ///
 11: /// Test-first order:
 12: ///   1. Prove the exact world-space coordinates the chunk generator places floor/wall
 13: ///      voxels at for the (0,0) hub chunk in low-spec mode.
 14: ///   2. Prove the spawn point (5.0, 1.7, 5.0) does NOT overlap any wall voxel.
 15: ///   3. Prove the floor voxel box does NOT block the player at spawn.
 16: ///   4. Prove terminal velocity is sane (<= 5 world-units/second).
 17: ///
 18: /// If test 2 or 3 fails, it proves the bug.  Then we add a fix and verify
 19: /// the test passes.
 20: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 21: 
 22: /// The JavaScript side extracts wall collision boxes from the SVO.
 23: /// This Rust analogue extracts the same information directly from the VoxelGrid
 24: /// so we can verify coordinates without the JS/SVO layer.
 25: fn grid_wall_boxes_at_spawn_x(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 26:     // Returns (minX, maxX, minY, maxY, minZ, maxZ) for every solid wall voxel
 27:     // at approximately x=5 world-units inside the chunk.
 28:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 29:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 30:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 31:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 32: 
 33:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 34:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 35: 
 36:     for y in 0..grid.height() {
 37:         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 38:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
 39:                 let vt = grid.get(x, y, z);
 40:                 if vt == VOXEL_WALL {
 41:                     let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 42:                     let wy = y as f32 * scale;
 43:                     let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 44:                     // The JS collision system gives walls a 1-voxel-size box
 45:                     boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, wy, wy + scale, wz, wz + scale));
 46:                 }
 47:             }
 48:         }
 49:     }
 50:     boxes
 51: }
 52: 
 53: fn floor_boxes(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 54:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 55:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 56:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 57:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 58: 
 59:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 60:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 61: 
 62:     for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 63:         for x in 0..grid.width() {
 64:             let vt = grid.get(x, 0, z);
 65:             if vt == VOXEL_FLOOR {
 66:                 let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 67:                 let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 68:                 // Floor voxel: y=0 to y=scale
 69:                 boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, 0.0_f32, scale, wz, wz + scale));
 70:             }
 71:         }
 72:     }
 73:     boxes
 74: }
 75: 
 76: /// Player AABB: eye-level at pos.y, feet at pos.y - 1.65, head at pos.y + 0.1
 77: fn player_overlaps(
 78:     pos: (f32, f32, f32),
 79:     radius: f32,
 80:     vbox: (f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32),
 81: ) -> bool {
 82:     let (px, py, pz) = pos;
 83:     let p_min_x = px - radius;
 84:     let p_max_x = px + radius;
 85:     let p_min_y = py - 1.65;
 86:     let p_max_y = py + 0.1;
 87:     let p_min_z = pz - radius;
 88:     let p_max_z = pz + radius;
 89:     let (v_min_x, v_max_x, v_min_y, v_max_y, v_min_z, v_max_z) = vbox;
 90: 
 91:     p_max_x > v_min_x
 92:         && p_min_x < v_max_x
 93:         && p_max_y > v_min_y
 94:         && p_min_y < v_max_y
 95:         && p_max_z > v_min_z
 96:         && p_min_z < v_max_z
 97: }

````rust
  1: //! Binary transport format for [`ChunkPayload`] between the generation
  2: //! workers and the main thread. One chunk becomes one contiguous byte
  3: //! buffer, so the browser can move it with a zero-copy `postMessage`
  4: //! transfer instead of structured-cloning a deep object graph.
  5: //!
  6: //! The format is little-endian, length-prefixed, and versioned by a magic
  7: //! header. Decode is defensive: any truncated or mismatched buffer yields
  8: //! `None` and the driver simply drops that chunk (the streamer re-requests).
  9: //! Platform-free and natively round-trip tested.
 10: 
 11: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 12: use crate::application::ports::{
 13:     ChunkPayload, FaceCellRange, FaceInstanceSet, LightSource, PackedFaceInstance, PackedVertex,
 14:     SurfaceMeshPayload,
 15: };
 16: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{PitHazard, TraversalGate};
 17: 
 18: /// "VKC" + version 3. Version 3 adds anomaly traversal/hazard semantics.
 19: const MAGIC: u32 = 0x564B_4303;
 20: 
 21: pub fn encode_chunk_payload(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u8> {
 22:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
 23:         64 + payload.nodes.len() * 4
 24:             + payload.surface.vertices.len() * 10
 25:             + payload.surface.indices.len() * 4
 26:             + payload.surface.light_volume.len()
 27:             + payload.surface.faces.instances.len() * 16
 28:             + payload.collision.len() * 24
 29:             + payload.traversal_gates.len() * TraversalGate::WORDS * 4
 30:             + payload.pit_hazards.len() * PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS * 4,
 31:     );
 32:     put_u32(&mut out, MAGIC);
 33:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.root);
 34:     put_f32(&mut out, payload.world_size);
 35: 
 36:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.nodes.len() as u32);
 37:     for &n in &payload.nodes {
 38:         put_u32(&mut out, n);
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     let s = &payload.surface;
 42:     put_u32(&mut out, s.vertices.len() as u32);
 43:     for v in &s.vertices {
 44:         for c in v.position {
 45:             put_u16(&mut out, c);
 46:         }
 47:         out.extend_from_slice(&[v.normal_axis, v.material, v.static_indirect, v.ao]);
 48:     }
 49:     put_u32(&mut out, s.indices.len() as u32);
 50:     for &i in &s.indices {
 51:         put_u32(&mut out, i);
 52:     }
 53:     put_aabb(&mut out, &s.bounds);
 54:     out.push(s.lod);
 55:     put_f32(&mut out, s.voxel_scale);
 56:     for d in s.light_volume_size {
 57:         put_u32(&mut out, d);
 58:     }
 59:     put_u32(&mut out, s.light_volume.len() as u32);
 60:     out.extend_from_slice(&s.light_volume);
 61: 
 62:     put_u32(&mut out, s.lights.len() as u32);
 63:     for l in &s.lights {
 64:         out.extend_from_slice(&l.id.to_le_bytes());
 65:         for c in l.position {
 66:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 67:         }
 68:         for c in l.half_size {
 69:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 70:         }
 71:         for c in l.color {
 72:             put_f32(&mut out, c);
 73:         }
 74:         put_f32(&mut out, l.radius);
 75:         put_f32(&mut out, l.intensity);
 76:         out.push(l.flicker_mode);
 77:         out.push(u8::from(l.enabled));
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     put_u32(&mut out, s.faces.instances.len() as u32);
 81:     for inst in &s.faces.instances {
 82:         for c in inst.position {
 83:             put_u16(&mut out, c);
 84:         }
 85:         out.extend_from_slice(&[
 86:             inst.extent_u,
 87:             inst.extent_v,
 88:             inst.normal_axis,
 89:             inst.material,
 90:             inst.baked_light,
 91:             inst.ao,
 92:             inst.flags,
 93:         ]);
 94:     }
 95:     put_u32(&mut out, s.faces.cells.len() as u32);
 96:     for cell in &s.faces.cells {
 97:         out.extend_from_slice(&cell.cell);
 98:         put_u32(&mut out, cell.offset);
 99:         put_u32(&mut out, cell.count);
100:     }
101:     put_f32(&mut out, s.faces.cell_size);
102: 
103:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.collision.len() as u32);
104:     for aabb in &payload.collision {
105:         put_aabb(&mut out, aabb);
106:     }
107: 
108:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.traversal_gates.len() as u32);
109:     for gate in &payload.traversal_gates {
110:         for word in gate.to_words() {
111:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
112:         }
113:     }
114:     put_u32(&mut out, payload.pit_hazards.len() as u32);
115:     for hazard in &payload.pit_hazards {
116:         let mut words = Vec::with_capacity(PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS);
117:         hazard.write_words(&mut words);
118:         for word in words {
119:             put_u32(&mut out, word);
120:         }
121:     }
122:     out
123: }

125: pub fn decode_chunk_payload(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
126:     let mut r = Reader { bytes, pos: 0 };
127:     if r.u32()? != MAGIC {
128:         return None;
129:     }
130:     let root = r.u32()?;
131:     let world_size = r.f32()?;
132: 
133:     let node_count = r.len(4)?;
134:     let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(node_count);
135:     for _ in 0..node_count {
136:         nodes.push(r.u32()?);
137:     }
138: 
139:     let vertex_count = r.len(10)?;
140:     let mut vertices = Vec::with_capacity(vertex_count);
141:     for _ in 0..vertex_count {
142:         vertices.push(PackedVertex {
143:             position: [r.u16()?, r.u16()?, r.u16()?],
144:             normal_axis: r.u8()?,
145:             material: r.u8()?,
146:             static_indirect: r.u8()?,
147:             ao: r.u8()?,
148:         });
149:     }
150:     let index_count = r.len(4)?;
151:     let mut indices = Vec::with_capacity(index_count);
152:     for _ in 0..index_count {
153:         indices.push(r.u32()?);
154:     }
155:     let bounds = r.aabb()?;
156:     let lod = r.u8()?;
157:     let voxel_scale = r.f32()?;
158:     let light_volume_size = [r.u32()?, r.u32()?, r.u32()?];
159:     let volume_len = r.len(1)?;
160:     let light_volume = r.slice(volume_len)?.to_vec();
161: 
162:     let light_count = r.len(39)?;
163:     let mut lights = Vec::with_capacity(light_count);
164:     for _ in 0..light_count {
165:         lights.push(LightSource {
166:             id: r.u64()?,
167:             position: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
168:             half_size: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
169:             color: [r.f32()?, r.f32()?, r.f32()?],
170:             radius: r.f32()?,
171:             intensity: r.f32()?,
172:             flicker_mode: r.u8()?,
173:             enabled: r.u8()? != 0,
174:         });
175:     }
176: 
177:     let instance_count = r.len(13)?;
178:     let mut instances = Vec::with_capacity(instance_count);
179:     for _ in 0..instance_count {
180:         instances.push(PackedFaceInstance {
181:             position: [r.u16()?, r.u16()?, r.u16()?],
182:             extent_u: r.u8()?,
183:             extent_v: r.u8()?,
184:             normal_axis: r.u8()?,
185:             material: r.u8()?,
186:             baked_light: r.u8()?,
187:             ao: r.u8()?,
188:             flags: r.u8()?,
189:             reserved: [0; 3],
190:         });
191:     }
192:     let cell_count = r.len(11)?;
193:     let mut cells = Vec::with_capacity(cell_count);
194:     for _ in 0..cell_count {
195:         cells.push(FaceCellRange {
196:             cell: [r.u8()?, r.u8()?, r.u8()?],
197:             offset: r.u32()?,
198:             count: r.u32()?,
199:         });
200:     }
201:     let cell_size = r.f32()?;
202: 
203:     let collision_count = r.len(24)?;
204:     let mut collision = Vec::with_capacity(collision_count);
205:     for _ in 0..collision_count {
206:         collision.push(r.aabb()?);
207:     }
208: 
209:     let gate_count = r.len(TraversalGate::WORDS * 4)?;
210:     let mut traversal_gates = Vec::with_capacity(gate_count);
211:     for _ in 0..gate_count {
212:         let mut words = [0u32; TraversalGate::WORDS];
213:         for word in &mut words {
214:             *word = r.u32()?;
215:         }
216:         traversal_gates.push(TraversalGate::from_words(&words)?);
217:     }
218:     let hazard_count = r.len(PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS * 4)?;
219:     let mut pit_hazards = Vec::with_capacity(hazard_count);
220:     for _ in 0..hazard_count {
221:         let mut words = [0u32; PitHazard::TRANSPORT_WORDS];
222:         for word in &mut words {
223:             *word = r.u32()?;
224:         }
225:         pit_hazards.push(PitHazard::from_transport_words(&words)?);
226:     }
227: 
228:     Some(ChunkPayload {
229:         root,
230:         nodes,
231:         world_size,
232:         surface: SurfaceMeshPayload {
233:             vertices,
234:             indices,
235:             bounds,
236:             lod,
237:             light_volume,
238:             light_volume_size,
239:             lights,
240:             faces: FaceInstanceSet {
241:                 instances,
242:                 cells,
243:                 cell_size,
244:             },
245:             voxel_scale,
246:         },
247:         collision,
248:         traversal_gates,
249:         pit_hazards,
250:     })
251: }

253: fn put_u16(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u16) {
254:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
255: }
256: fn put_u32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {
257:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
258: }
259: fn put_f32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: f32) {
260:     out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
261: }
262: fn put_aabb(out: &mut Vec<u8>, aabb: &Aabb) {
263:     for c in aabb.min {
264:         put_f32(out, c);
265:     }
266:     for c in aabb.max {
267:         put_f32(out, c);
268:     }
269: }
270: 
271: struct Reader<'a> {
272:     bytes: &'a [u8],
273:     pos: usize,
274: }
275: 
276: impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
277:     fn slice(&mut self, n: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
278:         let end = self.pos.checked_add(n)?;
279:         let s = self.bytes.get(self.pos..end)?;
280:         self.pos = end;
281:         Some(s)
282:     }
283:     fn u8(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
284:         Some(self.slice(1)?[0])
285:     }
286:     fn u16(&mut self) -> Option<u16> {
287:         Some(u16::from_le_bytes(self.slice(2)?.try_into().ok()?))
288:     }
289:     fn u32(&mut self) -> Option<u32> {
290:         Some(u32::from_le_bytes(self.slice(4)?.try_into().ok()?))
291:     }
292:     fn u64(&mut self) -> Option<u64> {
293:         Some(u64::from_le_bytes(self.slice(8)?.try_into().ok()?))
294:     }
295:     fn f32(&mut self) -> Option<f32> {
296:         Some(f32::from_le_bytes(self.slice(4)?.try_into().ok()?))
297:     }
298:     fn aabb(&mut self) -> Option<Aabb> {
299:         Some(Aabb::new(
300:             [self.f32()?, self.f32()?, self.f32()?],
301:             [self.f32()?, self.f32()?, self.f32()?],
302:         ))
303:     }
304:     /// Reads a length prefix and sanity-bounds it: each element occupies at
305:     /// least `min_element_bytes`, so a corrupt length cannot force a huge
306:     /// allocation before the reads start failing.
307:     fn len(&mut self, min_element_bytes: usize) -> Option<usize> {
308:         let n = self.u32()? as usize;
309:         let remaining = self.bytes.len().saturating_sub(self.pos);
310:         if n.saturating_mul(min_element_bytes.max(1)) > remaining {
311:             return None;
312:         }
313:         Some(n)
314:     }
315: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/face_instances.rs
````rust
  1: //! Converts greedy-merged quads into the splat renderer's compact face
  2: //! instances: one error-selected, axis-aligned surface rectangle each.
  3: //!
  4: //! The instances derive from the *same* [`MergedQuad`] list as the indexed
  5: //! mesh, so the splat renderer's visible boundary and the mesh-based shadow
  6: //! caster can never disagree. Two transformations happen on the way:
  7: //!
  8: //! * **Extent capping** — a merged quad longer than [`MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS`]
  9: //!   on either axis is split into pieces, because the splat path lights each
 10: //!   face with one flat sample; one sample across a 10 u wall would smear.
 11: //! * **Cell bucketing** — instances are sorted by [`FACE_CELL_UNITS`] cell so
 12: //!   the driver can draw or cull contiguous ranges with zero per-frame
 13: //!   rebuild work.
 14: //!
 15: //! Like the rest of the adapters layer this is platform-free and natively
 16: //! unit-tested.
 17: 
 18: use vackrooms::adapters::voxel_mapper::{FaceDirection, MergedQuad};
 19: 
 20: use crate::adapters::surface_mesh::material_id;
 21: use crate::application::ports::{
 22:     FACE_INSTANCE_FLAG_EMISSIVE, FaceCellRange, FaceInstanceSet, POSITION_FIXED_SCALE,
 23:     PackedFaceInstance,
 24: };
 25: 
 26: /// Longest face edge in world units before a quad is split. Keeps one flat
 27: /// per-face light/shadow sample honest on large merged planes.
 28: pub const MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS: f32 = 2.5;
 29: /// World size of one culling cell (matches the extent cap so a face never
 30: /// spans more than ~two cells).
 31: pub const FACE_CELL_UNITS: f32 = 2.5;
 32: 
 33: /// Builds the face-instance page for one chunk from its greedy quads.
 34: /// `voxel_scale` is the world size of one voxel cell at this LOD; quad
 35: /// geometry is exact multiples of it.
 36: pub fn build_face_instances(quads: &[MergedQuad], voxel_scale: f32) -> FaceInstanceSet {
 37:     let max_cells = ((MAX_FACE_EXTENT_UNITS / voxel_scale).floor() as u32).max(1);
 38:     let mut instances = Vec::with_capacity(quads.len());
 39:     for quad in quads {
 40:         emit_capped(quad, voxel_scale, max_cells, &mut instances);
 41:     }
 42: 
 43:     // Sort by culling cell so each cell's instances form one contiguous run.
 44:     let cell_of = |inst: &PackedFaceInstance| -> [u8; 3] {
 45:         let mut cell = [0u8; 3];
 46:         for axis in 0..3 {
 47:             let world = inst.position[axis] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE;
 48:             cell[axis] = (world / FACE_CELL_UNITS).floor().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8;
 49:         }
 50:         cell
 51:     };
 52:     instances.sort_by_key(|inst| {
 53:         let c = cell_of(inst);
 54:         (c[0], c[1], c[2])
 55:     });
 56: 
 57:     let mut cells: Vec<FaceCellRange> = Vec::new();
 58:     for (index, inst) in instances.iter().enumerate() {
 59:         let cell = cell_of(inst);
 60:         match cells.last_mut() {
 61:             Some(range) if range.cell == cell => range.count += 1,
 62:             _ => cells.push(FaceCellRange {
 63:                 cell,
 64:                 offset: index as u32,
 65:                 count: 1,
 66:             }),
 67:         }
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     FaceInstanceSet {
 71:         instances,
 72:         cells,
 73:         cell_size: FACE_CELL_UNITS,
 74:     }
 75: }
 76: 
 77: /// Face frame of one quad: the fixed plane coordinate plus the two in-plane
 78: /// axes. U/V axis assignment matches the splat vertex shader (U = X for
 79: /// Y/Z-normal faces, Y for X-normal faces; V = the remaining axis).
 80: struct FaceFrame {
 81:     /// World axis index the face is perpendicular to.
 82:     plane_axis: usize,
 83:     /// Face plane coordinate along `plane_axis`.
 84:     plane: f32,
 85:     u_axis: usize,
 86:     v_axis: usize,
 87:     min_u: f32,
 88:     min_v: f32,
 89:     cells_u: u32,
 90:     cells_v: u32,
 91: }
 92: 
 93: fn face_frame(quad: &MergedQuad, s: f32) -> FaceFrame {
 94:     let cells = |len: f32| ((len / s).round() as u32).max(1);
 95:     match quad.dir {
 96:         // Horizontal faces: `w` spans X, `h` spans Z (see surface_mesh).
 97:         FaceDirection::Up | FaceDirection::Down => FaceFrame {
 98:             plane_axis: 1,
 99:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::Up {
100:                 quad.y + s
101:             } else {
102:                 quad.y
103:             },
104:             u_axis: 0,
105:             v_axis: 2,
106:             min_u: quad.x,
107:             min_v: quad.z,
108:             cells_u: cells(quad.w),
109:             cells_v: cells(quad.h),
110:         },
111:         // Z-normal faces: `w` spans X, `h` spans Y.
112:         FaceDirection::North | FaceDirection::South => FaceFrame {
113:             plane_axis: 2,
114:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::South {
115:                 quad.z + s
116:             } else {
117:                 quad.z
118:             },
119:             u_axis: 0,
120:             v_axis: 1,
121:             min_u: quad.x,
122:             min_v: quad.y,
123:             cells_u: cells(quad.w),
124:             cells_v: cells(quad.h),
125:         },
126:         // X-normal faces: `h` spans Y, `w` spans Z.
127:         FaceDirection::East | FaceDirection::West => FaceFrame {
128:             plane_axis: 0,
129:             plane: if quad.dir == FaceDirection::East {
130:                 quad.x + s
131:             } else {
132:                 quad.x
133:             },
134:             u_axis: 1,
135:             v_axis: 2,
136:             min_u: quad.y,
137:             min_v: quad.z,
138:             cells_u: cells(quad.h),
139:             cells_v: cells(quad.w),
140:         },
141:     }
142: }
143: 
144: fn emit_capped(
145:     quad: &MergedQuad,
146:     s: f32,
147:     max_cells: u32,
148:     out: &mut Vec<PackedFaceInstance>,
149: ) {
150:     let frame = face_frame(quad, s);
151:     let material = material_id(quad.v_type);
152:     let flags = if vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material) {
153:         FACE_INSTANCE_FLAG_EMISSIVE
154:     } else {
155:         0
156:     };
157:     let normal_axis = normal_axis(quad.dir);
158: 
159:     let mut u_off = 0;
160:     while u_off < frame.cells_u {
161:         let piece_u = max_cells.min(frame.cells_u - u_off);
162:         let mut v_off = 0;
163:         while v_off < frame.cells_v {
164:             let piece_v = max_cells.min(frame.cells_v - v_off);
165:             let center_u = frame.min_u + (u_off as f32 + piece_u as f32 * 0.5) * s;
166:             let center_v = frame.min_v + (v_off as f32 + piece_v as f32 * 0.5) * s;
167:             let mut position = [0.0f32; 3];
168:             position[frame.plane_axis] = frame.plane;
169:             position[frame.u_axis] = center_u;
170:             position[frame.v_axis] = center_v;
171:             out.push(PackedFaceInstance {
172:                 position: position.map(pack_position),
173:                 extent_u: piece_u.min(u8::MAX as u32) as u8,
174:                 extent_v: piece_v.min(u8::MAX as u32) as u8,
175:                 normal_axis,
176:                 material,
177:                 baked_light: quad.light,
178:                 ao: quad.ao,
179:                 flags,
180:                 reserved: [0; 3],
181:             });
182:             v_off += piece_v;
183:         }
184:         u_off += piece_u;
185:     }
186: }
187: 
188: fn pack_position(value: f32) -> u16 {
189:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE)
190:         .round()
191:         .clamp(0.0, u16::MAX as f32) as u16
192: }
193: 
194: /// Same encoding as `surface_mesh::normal_axis` / the shaders' `normalForAxis`.
195: fn normal_axis(dir: FaceDirection) -> u8 {
196:     match dir {
197:         FaceDirection::Up => 0,
198:         FaceDirection::Down => 1,
199:         FaceDirection::North => 2,
200:         FaceDirection::South => 3,
201:         FaceDirection::East => 4,
202:         FaceDirection::West => 5,
203:     }
204: }
205:

214:     }
