## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/collision.rs
````rust
  1: //! Axis-aligned collision primitives and the sliding-collision world.
  2: //!
  3: //! Collision geometry is *derived from the SVO itself* (solid leaf nodes of
  4: //! type WALL / RED_WALL become world-space boxes), so the physical world and
  5: //! the rendered world can never drift apart.
  6: 
  7: /// Axis-aligned bounding box in world space.
  8: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  9: pub struct Aabb {
 10:     pub min: [f32; 3],
 11:     pub max: [f32; 3],
 12: }
 13: 
 14: impl Aabb {
 15:     pub fn new(min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 16:         Self { min, max }
 17:     }
 18: 
 19:     pub fn intersects(&self, other: &Aabb) -> bool {
 20:         self.max[0] > other.min[0]
 21:             && self.min[0] < other.max[0]
 22:             && self.max[1] > other.min[1]
 23:             && self.min[1] < other.max[1]
 24:             && self.max[2] > other.min[2]
 25:             && self.min[2] < other.max[2]
 26:     }
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Player capsule approximated as an AABB, matching the original client:
 30: /// radius 0.35 around the eye, extending 1.65 below and 0.1 above eye level.
 31: pub const PLAYER_RADIUS: f32 = 0.35;
 32: pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET: f32 = 1.65;
 33: pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD: f32 = 0.1;
 34: 
 35: /// Builds the player's AABB from an eye-level position.
 36: pub fn player_aabb(eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> Aabb {
 37:     Aabb::new(
 38:         [
 39:             eye_pos[0] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
 40:             eye_pos[1] - PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET,
 41:             eye_pos[2] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
 42:         ],
 43:         [
 44:             eye_pos[0] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
 45:             eye_pos[1] + PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD,
 46:             eye_pos[2] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
 47:         ],
 48:     )
 49: }
 50: 
 51: /// The set of solid boxes the player can collide with.
 52: /// Rebuilt whenever the chunk set changes.
 53: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 54: pub struct CollisionWorld {
 55:     boxes: Vec<Aabb>,
 56: }
 57: 
 58: impl CollisionWorld {
 59:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 60:         Self { boxes: Vec::new() }
 61:     }
 62: 
 63:     pub fn rebuild<'a, I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Aabb>>(&mut self, boxes: I) {
 64:         self.boxes.clear();
 65:         self.boxes.extend(boxes.into_iter().copied());
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 69:         self.boxes.len()
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 73:         self.boxes.is_empty()
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     pub fn boxes(&self) -> &[Aabb] {
 77:         &self.boxes
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     /// True if a player standing at `eye_pos` overlaps any solid box.
 81:     pub fn collides(&self, eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 82:         let p = player_aabb(eye_pos);
 83:         self.boxes.iter().any(|b| p.intersects(b))
 84:     }
 85: }
 86: 
 87: #[cfg(test)]
 88: mod tests {
 89:     use super::*;
 90: 
 91:     #[test]
 92:     fn aabb_intersection_is_exclusive_on_touching_faces() {
 93:         let a = Aabb::new([0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]);
 94:         let touching = Aabb::new([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], [2.0, 1.0, 1.0]);
 95:         let overlapping = Aabb::new([0.9, 0.0, 0.0], [2.0, 1.0, 1.0]);
 96:         assert!(!a.intersects(&touching));
 97:         assert!(a.intersects(&overlapping));
 98:     }
 99: 
100:     #[test]
101:     fn player_collides_with_wall_at_waist_height() {
102:         let mut world = CollisionWorld::new();
103:         world.rebuild(&[Aabb::new([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1.2, 3.0, 5.0])]);
104:         // Eye at 1.7 — wall spans full height, player is 0.35 wide.
105:         assert!(world.collides([1.0, 1.7, 2.0]));
106:         assert!(!world.collides([0.0, 1.7, 2.0]));
107:     }
108: 
109:     #[test]
110:     fn player_does_not_collide_with_floor_slab_below_feet() {
111:         let mut world = CollisionWorld::new();
112:         // Floor slab 0.0..0.05 — feet bottom is at 1.7 - 1.65 = 0.05 exactly:
113:         // touching, not overlapping.
114:         world.rebuild(&[Aabb::new([-10.0, 0.0, -10.0], [10.0, 0.05, 10.0])]);
115:         assert!(!world.collides([0.0, 1.7, 0.0]));
116:     }
117: }
````

````rust
  1: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
  2: 
  3: const VOXEL_AIR: u8 = 0;
  4: const VOXEL_LIGHT: u8 = 4;
  5: 
  6: #[wasm_bindgen]
  7: pub struct CPURaycaster {
  8:     grid_data: Vec<u8>,
  9:     light_data: Vec<u8>,
 10:     width: usize,
 11:     height: usize,
 12:     depth: usize,
 13:     frame_buffer: Vec<u8>,
 14:     screen_width: usize,
 15:     screen_height: usize,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: #[wasm_bindgen]
 19: impl CPURaycaster {
 20:     #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
 21:     pub fn new(screen_width: usize, screen_height: usize) -> Self {
 22:         Self {
 23:             grid_data: Vec::new(),
 24:             light_data: Vec::new(),
 25:             width: 0,
 26:             height: 0,
 27:             depth: 0,
 28:             frame_buffer: vec![255; screen_width * screen_height * 4],
 29:             screen_width,
 30:             screen_height,
 31:         }
 32:     }
 33: 
 34:     pub fn set_grid(
 35:         &mut self,
 36:         width: usize,
 37:         height: usize,
 38:         depth: usize,
 39:         data: &[u8],
 40:         light: &[u8],
 41:     ) {
 42:         self.width = width;
 43:         self.height = height;
 44:         self.depth = depth;
 45:         self.grid_data = data.to_vec();
 46:         self.light_data = light.to_vec();
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     pub fn get_frame_buffer(&self) -> *const u8 {
 50:         self.frame_buffer.as_ptr()
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     fn get_voxel(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 54:         if x < 0
 55:             || y < 0
 56:             || z < 0
 57:             || x >= self.width as isize
 58:             || y >= self.height as isize
 59:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 60:         {
 61:             return VOXEL_AIR;
 62:         }
 63:         self.grid_data
 64:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     fn get_light(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 68:         if x < 0
 69:             || y < 0
 70:             || z < 0
 71:             || x >= self.width as isize
 72:             || y >= self.height as isize
 73:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 74:         {
 75:             return 0;
 76:         }
 77:         self.light_data
 78:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     pub fn render(&mut self, px: f32, py: f32, pz: f32, yaw: f32, pitch: f32, fov_deg: f32) {
 82:         // Clear background to dark fog
 83:         for i in (0..self.frame_buffer.len()).step_by(4) {
 84:             self.frame_buffer[i] = 10; // R
 85:             self.frame_buffer[i + 1] = 10; // G
 86:             self.frame_buffer[i + 2] = 10; // B
 87:             self.frame_buffer[i + 3] = 255; // A
 88:         }
 89: 
 90:         if self.width == 0 {
 91:             return;
 92:         }
 93: 
 94:         let fov_rad = fov_deg * std::f32::consts::PI / 180.0;
 95:         let half_fov = fov_rad / 2.0;
 96: 
 97:         let dir_x = -yaw.sin();
 98:         let dir_z = -yaw.cos();
 99:         let plane_x = yaw.cos() * half_fov.tan();
100:         let plane_z = -yaw.sin() * half_fov.tan();
101: 
102:         for x in 0..self.screen_width {
103:             let camera_x = 2.0 * (x as f32) / (self.screen_width as f32) - 1.0;
104:             let ray_dir_x = dir_x + plane_x * camera_x;
105:             let ray_dir_z = dir_z + plane_z * camera_x;
106: 
107:             let mut map_x = px.floor() as isize;
108:             let mut map_z = pz.floor() as isize;
109: 
110:             let delta_dist_x = if ray_dir_x == 0.0 {
111:                 f32::INFINITY
112:             } else {
113:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_x).abs()
114:             };
115:             let delta_dist_z = if ray_dir_z == 0.0 {
116:                 f32::INFINITY
117:             } else {
118:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_z).abs()
119:             };
120: 
121:             let mut side_dist_x;
122:             let mut side_dist_z;
123:             let step_x: isize;
124:             let step_z: isize;
125: 
126:             if ray_dir_x < 0.0 {
127:                 step_x = -1;
128:                 side_dist_x = (px - map_x as f32) * delta_dist_x;
129:             } else {
130:                 step_x = 1;
131:                 side_dist_x = (map_x as f32 + 1.0 - px) * delta_dist_x;
132:             }
133: 
134:             if ray_dir_z < 0.0 {
135:                 step_z = -1;
136:                 side_dist_z = (pz - map_z as f32) * delta_dist_z;
137:             } else {
138:                 step_z = 1;
139:                 side_dist_z = (map_z as f32 + 1.0 - pz) * delta_dist_z;
140:             }
141: 
142:             let mut hit = 0;
143:             let mut side = 0;
144:             let mut perp_wall_dist = 0.0;
145:             let mut hit_y = 0;
146: 
147:             let map_y = py.floor() as isize;
148:             let max_steps = 200;
149:             let mut steps = 0;
150: 
151:             while hit == 0 && steps < max_steps {
152:                 if side_dist_x < side_dist_z {
153:                     side_dist_x += delta_dist_x;
154:                     map_x += step_x;
155:                     side = 0;
156:                 } else {
157:                     side_dist_z += delta_dist_z;
158:                     map_z += step_z;
159:                     side = 1;
160:                 }
161: 
162:                 let v = self.get_voxel(map_x, map_y, map_z);
163:                 if v != VOXEL_AIR {
164:                     hit = v;
165:                     hit_y = map_y;
166:                 }
167:                 steps += 1;
168:             }
169: 
170:             if hit > 0 {
171:                 if side == 0 {
172:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_x - delta_dist_x;
173:                 } else {
174:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_z - delta_dist_z;
175:                 }
176: 
177:                 let line_height = (self.screen_height as f32 / perp_wall_dist).abs() as isize;
178:                 let pitch_offset = (pitch * self.screen_height as f32) as isize;
179: 
180:                 let mut draw_start =
181:                     -line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
182:                 let draw_start_clamped = if draw_start < 0 {
183:                     0
184:                 } else {
185:                     draw_start as usize
186:                 };
187:                 let mut draw_end = line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
188:                 if draw_end >= self.screen_height as isize {
189:                     draw_end = self.screen_height as isize - 1;
190:                 }
191:                 let draw_end_clamped = draw_end as usize;
192: 
193:                 let mut r = 200;
194:                 let mut g = 200;
195:                 let mut b = 200;
196: 
197:                 if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
198:                     r = 255;
199:                     g = 255;
200:                     b = 200;
201:                 } else if hit == 5 {
202:                     r = 150;
203:                     g = 30;
204:                     b = 30;
205:                 } else if hit == 1 {
206:                     r = 180;
207:                     g = 160;
208:                     b = 100;
209:                 }
210: 
211:                 let light = self.get_light(map_x, hit_y, map_z);
212:                 let light_factor = if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
213:                     1.0
214:                 } else {
215:                     light as f32 / 15.0
216:                 };
217:                 let fog_factor = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.05).exp();
218: 
219:                 r = (r as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
220:                 g = (g as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
221:                 b = (b as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
222: 
223:                 if side == 1 && hit != VOXEL_LIGHT {
224:                     r = (r as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
225:                     g = (g as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
226:                     b = (b as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
227:                 }
228: 
229:                 for y in draw_start_clamped..=draw_end_clamped {
230:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
231:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = r;
232:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = g;
233:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = b;
234:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
235:                 }
236: 
237:                 let floor_fog = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.01).exp(); // less fog on floor to see shape
238:                 for y in (draw_end_clamped + 1)..self.screen_height {
239:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
240:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
241:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
242:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
243:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
244:                 }
245: 
246:                 for y in 0..draw_start_clamped {
247:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
248:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (60.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
249:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (55.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
250:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (50.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
251:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
252:                 }
253:             }
254:         }
255:     }
256: }
````

## File: src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
  2: 
  3: /// Represents SVO flattened data formatted for direct WebGL2 texture upload.
  4: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  5: pub struct OctreeGpuData {
  6:     pub texture_width: u32,
  7:     pub texture_height: u32,
  8:     pub texel_data: Vec<u32>,
  9: }
 10: 
 11: /// GPU Adapter to flatten the Sparse Voxel Octree into a GPU-compatible texture format.
 12: ///
 13: /// DOCUMENTED ENCODING SCHEME (RGBA32UI texture format):
 14: /// Each SVO node occupies exactly one texel (4 x 32-bit unsigned integers: R, G, B, A).
 15: ///
 16: /// CHANNEL LAYOUT:
 17: /// - **R (x):** Node Type Flag
 18: ///   * `0` = Internal Parent Node
 19: ///   * `1` = Leaf Voxel Node
 20: ///
 21: /// - **G (y):** Payload 1
 22: ///   * If Internal Node (`R == 0`): `child_base_index` (uint32) - Index in the texture
 23: ///     of the first child. The remaining 7 children are stored contiguously at indices
 24: ///     `child_base_index + 1` through `child_base_index + 7`.
 25: ///   * If Leaf Node (`R == 1`): `voxel_type` (uint32) - Voxel type ID (e.g., WALL, FLOOR, etc.).
 26: ///
 27: /// - **B (z):** Payload 2
 28: ///   * If Internal Node (`R == 0`): `child_mask` (uint32) - 8-bit active children mask.
 29: ///     Bit `i` is `1` if child `i` is non-empty, and `0` if child `i` is empty air.
 30: ///   * If Leaf Node (`R == 1`): `color` (uint32) - 24-bit packed RGB color (`0xRRGGBB`).
 31: ///
 32: /// - **A (w):** Payload 3
 33: ///   * If Internal Node (`R == 0`): `0` (Padding).
 34: ///   * If Leaf Node (`R == 1`): packed lighting:
 35: ///     - bits 0-7:   scalar light level, the max of the RGB channels (0-15)
 36: ///     - bits 8-15:  face occlusion mask
 37: ///     - bits 16-19: red light channel (0-15)
 38: ///     - bits 20-23: green light channel (0-15)
 39: ///     - bits 24-27: blue light channel (0-15)
 40: pub struct OctreeGpuSerializer;
 41: 
 42: impl OctreeGpuSerializer {
 43:     /// Serializes SVO nodes into texture-ready data, padding the last row to maintain grid alignment.
 44:     pub fn serialize_to_gpu_data(octree: &SparseVoxelOctree) -> OctreeGpuData {
 45:         let num_nodes = octree.nodes.len();
 46:         let texture_width = 1024; // Standard GPU texture row size
 47:         let total_texels = ((num_nodes + texture_width - 1) / texture_width) * texture_width;
 48: 
 49:         let mut texel_data = Vec::with_capacity(total_texels * 4);
 50: 
 51:         for node in &octree.nodes {
 52:             match *node {
 53:                 SvoNode::Leaf {
 54:                     voxel_type,
 55:                     color,
 56:                     light_rgb,
 57:                     face_occlusion,
 58:                 } => {
 59:                     let [r, g, b] = light_rgb;
 60:                     let scalar = r.max(g).max(b) as u32;
 61:                     texel_data.push(1); // R
 62:                     texel_data.push(voxel_type as u32); // G
 63:                     texel_data.push(color); // B
 64:                     texel_data.push(
 65:                         scalar
 66:                             | (face_occlusion as u32) << 8
 67:                             | (r as u32 & 0xF) << 16
 68:                             | (g as u32 & 0xF) << 20
 69:                             | (b as u32 & 0xF) << 24,
 70:                     ); // A
 71:                 }
 72:                 SvoNode::Internal {
 73:                     child_base_index,
 74:                     child_mask,
 75:                 } => {
 76:                     texel_data.push(0); // R
 77:                     texel_data.push(child_base_index); // G
 78:                     texel_data.push(child_mask as u32); // B
 79:                     texel_data.push(0); // A
 80:                 }
 81:             }
 82:         }
 83: 
 84:         // Pad the last row with empty leaves to prevent out-of-bound shader fetches
 85:         let padded_nodes_count = total_texels - num_nodes;
 86:         for _ in 0..padded_nodes_count {
 87:             texel_data.push(1); // Leaf
 88:             texel_data.push(0); // Air
 89:             texel_data.push(0); // Color
 90:             texel_data.push(0); // Light Level
 91:         }
 92: 
 93:         let texture_height = (total_texels / texture_width) as u32;
 94: 
 95:         OctreeGpuData {
 96:             texture_width: texture_width as u32,
 97:             texture_height,
 98:             texel_data,
 99:         }
100:     }
101: }
102: 
103: #[cfg(test)]
104: mod tests {
105:     use super::*;
106: 
107:     #[test]
108:     fn test_gpu_serialization_padding() {
109:         let mut octree = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
110:         octree.set(0, 0, 0, 1, 0xFF00FF, [15; 3], 0);
111: 
112:         let gpu_data = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&octree);
113: 
114:         // Verification tests
115:         assert_eq!(gpu_data.texture_width, 1024);
116:         assert_eq!(
117:             gpu_data.texel_data.len(),
118:             (gpu_data.texture_width * gpu_data.texture_height * 4) as usize
119:         );
120: 
121:         // Index 0 maps to texel (0, 0)
122:         let index = 0;
123:         let tx = index % 1024;
124:         let ty = index / 1024;
125:         assert_eq!(tx, 0);
126:         assert_eq!(ty, 0);
127: 
128:         // Ensure child_base_index values stay within texture range
129:         for node in &octree.nodes {
130:             if let SvoNode::Internal {
131:                 child_base_index, ..
132:             } = *node
133:             {
134:                 let max_index = child_base_index + 7;
135:                 assert!(max_index < (gpu_data.texture_width * gpu_data.texture_height));
136:             }
137:         }
138:     }
139: }
````

## File: src/domain/use_cases/generate_maze.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
  2: use rand::Rng;
  3: #[allow(unused_imports)]
  4: use rand::RngExt;
  5: 
  6: /// Design Pattern: Strategy
  7: /// We use the Strategy pattern here to encapsulate the maze generation algorithm.
  8: /// This is the superior choice because different Backrooms levels (or even different regions of Level 0)
  9: /// might require different procedural generation rules. By decoupling the generation logic from the Grid entity,
 10: /// we ensure the Open/Closed Principle (workable iʃɛ́) — we can add new generators without modifying the Grid.
 11: pub trait MazeGenerator {
 12:     /// Generates the maze on the provided grid using the given random number generator.
 13:     fn generate<R: Rng + ?Sized>(&self, grid: &mut Grid, rng: &mut R);
 14: }
 15: 
 16: /// A concrete strategy for generating a maze using the Growing Tree algorithm.
 17: /// This algorithm produces non-linear, organic layouts suitable for the Backrooms,
 18: /// unlike standard depth-first search which produces long winding paths.
 19: pub struct GrowingTreeGenerator {
 20:     pub junction_density: f32,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: impl MazeGenerator for GrowingTreeGenerator {
 24:     fn generate<R: Rng + ?Sized>(&self, grid: &mut Grid, rng: &mut R) {
 25:         let width = grid.width();
 26:         let depth = grid.depth();
 27:         if width == 0 || depth == 0 {
 28:             return;
 29:         }
 30: 
 31:         // Starting point
 32:         let start_x = rng.random_range(0..width);
 33:         let start_y = rng.random_range(0..depth);
 34: 
 35:         if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(start_x, start_y) {
 36:             cell.visited = true;
 37:         }
 38: 
 39:         let mut frontier = vec![(start_x, start_y)];
 40: 
 41:         while !frontier.is_empty() {
 42:             // Pick a random cell from the frontier (this randomness defines the Growing Tree behavior)
 43:             let idx = rng.random_range(0..frontier.len());
 44:             let (cx, cy) = frontier[idx];
 45: 
 46:             // Define neighbors: (x, y, wall_here_idx, wall_there_idx)
 47:             // 0: North, 1: East, 2: South, 3: West
 48:             let neighbors: [(isize, isize, usize, usize); 4] = [
 49:                 (cx as isize, (cy as isize) - 1, 0, 2), // North
 50:                 ((cx as isize) + 1, cy as isize, 1, 3), // East
 51:                 (cx as isize, (cy as isize) + 1, 2, 0), // South
 52:                 ((cx as isize) - 1, cy as isize, 3, 1), // West
 53:             ];
 54: 
 55:             let mut unvisited = Vec::new();
 56:             for &(nx, ny, wall_here, wall_there) in &neighbors {
 57:                 if nx >= 0 && nx < width as isize && ny >= 0 && ny < depth as isize {
 58:                     let (nx_u, ny_u) = (nx as usize, ny as usize);
 59:                     if let Some(cell) = grid.get(nx_u, ny_u) {
 60:                         if !cell.visited {
 61:                             unvisited.push((nx_u, ny_u, wall_here, wall_there));
 62:                         }
 63:                     }
 64:                 }
 65:             }
 66: 
 67:             if unvisited.is_empty() {
 68:                 frontier.swap_remove(idx);
 69:             } else {
 70:                 let unvisited_idx = rng.random_range(0..unvisited.len());
 71:                 let (nx, ny, wall_here, wall_there) = unvisited[unvisited_idx];
 72: 
 73:                 // Knock down walls
 74:                 if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(cx, cy) {
 75:                     cell.walls[wall_here] = false;
 76:                 }
 77:                 if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(nx, ny) {
 78:                     cell.walls[wall_there] = false;
 79:                     cell.visited = true;
 80:                 }
 81: 
 82:                 frontier.push((nx, ny));
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85: 
 86:         // Add loops to break the "perfect maze" property and make it feel like the Backrooms
 87:         let base_openings = (width * depth) as f32 / 4.0;
 88:         let extra_openings = (base_openings * self.junction_density) as usize;
 89:         let mut actual_openings = 0;
 90:         let mut attempts = 0;
 91: 
 92:         while actual_openings < extra_openings && attempts < extra_openings * 3 {
 93:             attempts += 1;
 94:             let x = rng.random_range(0..width);
 95:             let y = rng.random_range(0..depth);
 96: 
 97:             // Blackout zones are knot-like dead-ends; suppress extra loops in them
 98:             if let Some(cell) = grid.get(x, y) {
 99:                 if cell.zone == crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone::Blackout {
100:                     continue;
101:                 }
102:             }
103: 
104:             let dir = rng.random_range(0..4);
105: 
106:             if let Some(cell) = grid.get_mut(x, y) {
107:                 cell.walls[dir] = false;
108:             }
109: 
110:             let (nx, ny) = match dir {
111:                 0 => (x as isize, y as isize - 1),
112:                 1 => (x as isize + 1, y as isize),
113:                 2 => (x as isize, y as isize + 1),
114:                 3 => (x as isize - 1, y as isize),
115:                 _ => unreachable!(),
116:             };
117: 
118:             if nx >= 0 && nx < width as isize && ny >= 0 && ny < depth as isize {
119:                 let (nx, ny) = (nx as usize, ny as usize);
120:                 let opposite_dir = (dir + 2) % 4;
121:                 if let Some(n_cell) = grid.get_mut(nx, ny) {
122:                     n_cell.walls[opposite_dir] = false;
123:                 }
124:             }
125: 
126:             actual_openings += 1;
127:         }
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: #[cfg(test)]
132: mod tests {
133:     use super::*;
134:     use crate::domain::entities::grid::Grid;
135:     use rand::SeedableRng;
136:     use rand::rngs::StdRng;
137: 
138:     #[test]
139:     fn test_generate_maze_visits_all_cells() {
140:         let mut grid = Grid::new(10, 10);
141:         let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(42);
142: 
143:         let generator = GrowingTreeGenerator {
144:             junction_density: 1.0,
145:         };
146:         generator.generate(&mut grid, &mut rng);
147: 
148:         for y in 0..grid.depth() {
149:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
150:                 let cell = grid.get(x, y).unwrap();
151:                 assert!(cell.visited, "Cell at ({}, {}) was not visited", x, y);
152:             }
153:         }
154:     }
155: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/grassland_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Level 34-B — "The Grassland".
  2: //!
  3: //! A safe, flat, endless grass plane you can noclip into from Level 0:
  4: //! * grass ground everywhere, with smooth-noise **lakes** of shallow water,
  5: //! * scattered **trees** (solid trunk, leaf canopy) on a hashed world grid,
  6: //! * a glowing **sky layer** at the top of the grid plus dim ground glow
  7: //!   sources hidden inside the turf, so the plane reads as daylight even
  8: //!   though lighting is the same BFS flood used indoors.
  9: //!
 10: //! Like every [`LevelGenerator`], all placement is a pure function of
 11: //! world-space coordinates so chunks tile seamlessly.
 12: 
 13: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 14:     VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
 15: };
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
 19: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 20: 
 21: /// Grid height in world units; the sky glow layer sits at the top.
 22: const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
 23: /// Trees sit on a world grid of this period (units); most cells are empty.
 24: const TREE_PERIOD: f32 = 9.0;
 25: /// Ground glow sources ("sun-lit turf") every N units.
 26: const GLOW_PERIOD: f32 = 3.2;
 27: 
 28: pub struct GrasslandLevel;
 29: 
 30: impl GrasslandLevel {
 31:     /// Uniform per-cell hash in [0, 1): samples the value noise exactly on
 32:     /// its lattice (provider frequency 0.05 → inputs that are multiples of
 33:     /// 20 hit lattice points, where the noise is a raw uniform hash).
 34:     fn hash(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, salt: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64) -> f32 {
 35:         let v = noise.evaluate_2d(
 36:             seed ^ salt,
 37:             Position::new(cx as f32 * 20.0, cz as f32 * 20.0),
 38:         );
 39:         (v * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999)
 40:     }
 41: }
 42: 
 43: impl LevelGenerator for GrasslandLevel {
 44:     fn generate(
 45:         &self,
 46:         chunk_pos: Position,
 47:         seed: u32,
 48:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 49:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 50:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
 51:         let s = config.voxel_scale;
 52:         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 53:         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 54:         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
 55:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
 56:         let sky_y = height - 1;
 57: 
 58:         for z in 0..depth {
 59:             for x in 0..width {
 60:                 let wx = chunk_pos.x + (x as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 61:                 let wz = chunk_pos.z + (z as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 62: 
 63:                 // Lakes: smooth blobs of the world-space noise field.
 64:                 let lake = noise.evaluate_2d(seed ^ 0x1A5E, Position::new(wx * 0.7, wz * 0.7));
 65:                 let ground = if lake > 0.62 {
 66:                     VOXEL_WATER
 67:                 } else {
 68:                     VOXEL_GRASS
 69:                 };
 70:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, ground);
 71: 
 72:                 // Sky glow: an unbroken luminous layer overhead.
 73:                 grid.set(x, sky_y, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 74: 
 75:                 // Ground glow grid keeps the turf bright at eye level (the
 76:                 // BFS light from the sky layer alone fades before the floor).
 77:                 let gx = wx.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 78:                 let gz = wz.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 79:                 if ground == VOXEL_GRASS && gx < s && gz < s {
 80:                     grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 81:                 }
 82: 
 83:                 // Trees: hashed world cells, never in water.
 84:                 let cell_x = (wx / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 85:                 let cell_z = (wz / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 86:                 if Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE5, cell_x, cell_z) > 0.6 && ground == VOXEL_GRASS {
 87:                     // Trunk position jittered inside the cell.
 88:                     let jx =
 89:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE6, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 90:                     let jz =
 91:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE7, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 92:                     let tx = cell_x as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jx;
 93:                     let tz = cell_z as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jz;
 94:                     let dx = wx - tx;
 95:                     let dz = wz - tz;
 96:                     let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 97: 
 98:                     let trunk_top = (2.2 / s) as usize;
 99:                     let canopy_top = (3.6 / s) as usize;
100:                     if d2 < (0.25f32).powi(2) {
101:                         for y in 1..trunk_top.min(height - 2) {
102:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_TREE);
103:                         }
104:                     }
105:                     if d2 < (1.6f32).powi(2) {
106:                         for y in trunk_top..canopy_top.min(height - 2) {
107:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_GRASS);
108:                         }
109:                     }
110:                 }
111:             }
112:         }
113: 
114:         grid
115:     }
116: }
````

````rust
 12: /// Presentation Layer & Driver:
 13: /// A minimalist, zero-dependency HTTP server that connects our
 14: /// Clean Architecture engine to the Browser Voxel Renderer.
 15: fn main() {
 16:     let port = 3000;
 17:     let listener = TcpListener::bind(format!("0.0.0.0:{}", port)).unwrap();
 18:     println!("--- Backrooms Engine Running ---");
 19:     println!("Server listening on http://localhost:{}", port);
 20:     println!("Open the above URL in your browser to view the Voxel Rendering.");
 21: 
 22:     for stream in listener.incoming() {
 23:         match stream {
 24:             Ok(stream) => {
 25:                 thread::spawn(move || {
 26:                     handle_client(stream);
 27:                 });
 28:             }
 29:             Err(e) => {
 30:                 eprintln!("Failed to accept connection: {}", e);
 31:             }
 32:         }
 33:     }
 34: }
 35: 
 36: fn handle_client(mut stream: TcpStream) {
 37:     let mut buffer = [0; 1024];
 38:     if let Ok(bytes_read) = stream.read(&mut buffer) {
 39:         if bytes_read == 0 {
 40:             return;
 41:         }
 42: 
 43:         let request = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer[..bytes_read]);
 44:         let request_line = request.lines().next().unwrap_or("");
 45: 
 46:         if request_line.starts_with("GET /maze") {
 47:             // Serve the Procedural Voxel Data with support for coordinate query parameters
 48:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
 49:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/maze");
 50: 
 51:             let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
 52:             let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
 53:             let mut spec = "high";
 54: 
 55:             if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
 56:                 let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
 57:                 for param in query.split('&') {
 58:                     let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
 59:                     if key_val.len() == 2 {
 60:                         match key_val[0] {
 61:                             "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 62:                             "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 63:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
 64:                             _ => {}
 65:                         }
 66:                     }
 67:                 }
 68:             }
 69: 
 70:             let config = if spec == "low" {
 71:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 72:             } else {
 73:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 74:             };
 75: 
 76:             let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 77:             let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
 78:             let generator =
 79:                 GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&noise_provider, &telemetry);
 80: 
 81:             let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 82: 
 83:             // Adapt to Web Format (greedy meshed faces)
 84:             let json = WebRendererAdapter::to_json(&chunk, config.chunk_size);
 85: 
 86:             let response = format!(
 87:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n{}",
 88:                 json.len(),
 89:                 json
 90:             );
 91:             let _ = stream.write_all(response.as_bytes());
 92:         } else if request_line.starts_with("GET /octree") {
 93:             // Serve the SVO Packed Data
 94:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
 95:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/octree");
 96: 
 97:             let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
 98:             let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
 99:             let mut spec = "high";
100: 
101:             if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
102:                 let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
103:                 for param in query.split('&') {
104:                     let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
105:                     if key_val.len() == 2 {
106:                         match key_val[0] {
107:                             "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
108:                             "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
109:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
110:                             _ => {}
111:                         }
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:             }
115: 
116:             let config = if spec == "low" {
117:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
118:             } else {
119:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
120:             };
121: 
122:             let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
123:             let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
124:             let generator =
125:                 GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&noise_provider, &telemetry);
126: 
127:             // Generate chunk at position with GeneratorConfig
128:             let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
129: 
130:             // Adapt to Web Format using SVO representation
131:             let depth = config.svo_depth();
132:             let world_size = config.svo_world_size();
133:             let binary = WebRendererAdapter::to_octree_binary(
134:                 &chunk,
135:                 depth,
136:                 world_size,
137:                 config.voxel_scale,
138:                 config.chunk_size,
139:             );
140: 
141:             let header = format!(
142:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
143:                 binary.len()
144:             );
145:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + binary.len());
146:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
147:             response.extend_from_slice(&binary);
148:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
149:         } else if request_line.starts_with("GET ") {
150:             // Static file service for the wasm front end (and the legacy page).
151:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
152:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/");
153:             let path = url.split('?').next().unwrap_or("/");
154:             serve_static(&mut stream, path);
155:         } else {
156:             let error = "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\n";
157:             let _ = stream.write_all(error.as_bytes());
158:         }
159:     }
160: }
161: 
162: /// Maps a URL path to a file under `static/` and serves it with the correct
163: /// MIME type. `application/wasm` matters: browsers refuse to instantiate
164: /// wasm streams served under the wrong content type.
165: fn serve_static(stream: &mut TcpStream, url_path: &str) {
166:     let relative = match url_path {
167:         "/" | "/index.html" => "index.html",
168:         "/legacy" => "legacy_threejs.html",
169:         other => other.trim_start_matches('/'),
170:     };
171: 
172:     // Path traversal guard: reject anything trying to escape `static/`.
173:     if relative.split('/').any(|seg| seg == "..") || relative.contains('\\') {
174:         let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n\r\n");
175:         return;
176:     }
177: 
178:     let file_path = format!("static/{}", relative);
179:     match fs::read(&file_path) {
180:         Ok(body) => {
181:             let mime = match file_path.rsplit('.').next() {
182:                 Some("html") => "text/html; charset=utf-8",
183:                 Some("js") | Some("mjs") => "text/javascript",
184:                 Some("wasm") => "application/wasm",
185:                 Some("css") => "text/css",
186:                 Some("json") => "application/json",
187:                 Some("png") => "image/png",
188:                 _ => "application/octet-stream",
189:             };
190:             let header = format!(
191:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
192:                 mime,
193:                 body.len()
194:             );
195:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + body.len());
196:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
197:             response.extend_from_slice(&body);
198:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
199:         }
200:         Err(_) => {
201:             let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\nFile not found.");
202:         }
203:     }
204: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Canvas-2D blit driver for the CPU splatting renderer.
 2: //!
 3: //! All rendering logic lives in the platform-free
 4: //! `adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer`; this wrapper's only job is
 5: //! to copy the finished RGBA framebuffer into the canvas via `ImageData` —
 6: //! no WebGL context is created at all.
 7: 
 8: use wasm_bindgen::{Clamped, JsCast, JsValue};
 9: use web_sys::{CanvasRenderingContext2d, HtmlCanvasElement, ImageData};
10: 
11: use crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer;
12: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
13: 
14: pub struct CpuCanvasRenderer {
15:     rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer,
16:     ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2d,
17:     settings: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings,
18: }
19: 
20: impl CpuCanvasRenderer {
21:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
22:         let ctx = canvas
23:             .get_context("2d")?
24:             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no 2d context available"))?
25:             .dyn_into::<CanvasRenderingContext2d>()?;
26:         let settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
27:         Ok(Self {
28:             rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer::new(canvas.width() as usize, canvas.height() as usize),
29:             ctx,
30:             settings,
31:         })
32:     }
33: 
34:     pub fn resize(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
35:         // Impose a low CPU backing resolution cap (480x270 max), keeping aspect ratio
36:         let max_w = 480.0;
37:         let max_h = 270.0;
38:         let scale = (max_w / width as f32).min(max_h / height as f32).min(1.0) * self.settings.internal_scale;
39:         let w = ((width as f32 * scale).round() as usize).max(1);
40:         let h = ((height as f32 * scale).round() as usize).max(1);
41: 
42:         self.rasterizer.resize(w, h);
43:     }
44: 
45:     pub fn telemetry_string(&self) -> String {
46:         let stats = self.rasterizer.telemetry();
47:         format!(
48:             "V:{} (D:{})/S:{}/P:{}K{}",
49:             stats.visited_nodes,
50:             stats.max_virtual_depth,
51:             stats.splat_count,
52:             stats.pixel_writes / 1000,
53:             if stats.budget_exhausted { "!" } else { "" }
54:         )
55:     }
56: }
57: 
58: impl RendererPort for CpuCanvasRenderer {
59:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
60:         self.rasterizer.upload_atlas(texels);
61:     }
62: 
63:     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
64:         Some(self.telemetry_string())
65:     }
66: 
67:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
68:         let old_scale = self.settings.internal_scale;
69:         self.settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
70:         self.settings.fov_tan = crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
71:         // The optimization switchboard is sampled once per frame here; the
72:         // platform-free rasterizer itself never reads globals.
73:         self.settings.toggles = crate::get_render_toggles();
74:         if self.settings.internal_scale != old_scale {
75:             if let Some(canvas) = self.ctx.canvas() {
76:                 self.resize(canvas.width(), canvas.height());
77:             }
78:         }
79:         self.rasterizer.settings = self.settings;
80:         self.rasterizer.draw(frame, chunks);
81:         let width = self.rasterizer.width() as u32;
82:         let height = self.rasterizer.height() as u32;
83:         let fb = self.rasterizer.framebuffer();
84:         
85:         if let Ok(image) = ImageData::new_with_u8_clamped_array_and_sh(
86:             Clamped(fb),
87:             width,
88:             height,
89:         ) {
90:             let _ = self.ctx.put_image_data(&image, 0.0, 0.0);
91:         }
92:     }
93: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/worker_source.rs
````rust
  1: //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
  2: //!
  3: //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
  4: //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
  5: //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, reality}` messages round-robin; workers run the full
  6: //! chunk pipeline (generation, BFS lighting, greedy mesh + face instances,
  7: //! SVO build/serialize, collision) and transfer one encoded byte buffer
  8: //! back (`adapters::chunk_codec`). No WebGL object ever leaves the main
  9: //! thread, and the frame loop never blocks on generation.
 10: //!
 11: //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
 12: //! by the echoed request; this driver only moves bytes.
 13: 
 14: use std::cell::RefCell;
 15: use std::rc::Rc;
 16: 
 17: use js_sys::{ArrayBuffer, Reflect, Uint8Array};
 18: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
 19: use web_sys::{MessageEvent, Worker, WorkerOptions, WorkerType};
 20: 
 21: use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::decode_chunk_payload;
 22: use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
 23: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkPayload, ChunkRequest, ChunkSourcePort, CompletedChunk};
 24: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 25: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 26: 
 27: pub struct WorkerChunkSource {
 28:     workers: Vec<Worker>,
 29:     next_worker: usize,
 30:     completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>>,
 31:     /// Keeps the onmessage closures alive for the workers' lifetime.
 32:     _handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>>,
 33:     /// Same-thread source for the synchronous [`ChunkSourcePort::load`]
 34:     /// contract (the engine never uses it while `is_async` is true).
 35:     fallback: LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl WorkerChunkSource {
 39:     /// Spawns the pool and hands every worker the URL query, so main thread
 40:     /// and workers derive the identical generator configuration.
 41:     pub fn new(query: &str, default_seed: u32) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 42:         let concurrency = web_sys::window()
 43:             .map(|w| w.navigator().hardware_concurrency())
 44:             .unwrap_or(2.0);
 45:         // Leave one core for the render thread; a Pi 4 (4 cores) gets 3.
 46:         let pool_size = ((concurrency as i32) - 1).clamp(1, 4) as usize;
 47: 
 48:         let completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
 49:         let mut workers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 50:         let mut handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 51:         for _ in 0..pool_size {
 52:             let options = WorkerOptions::new();
 53:             options.set_type(WorkerType::Module);
 54:             // Relative (not `/worker.js`): resolved against the document's
 55:             // URL, so this still finds the sibling file when the site is
 56:             // served from a subpath (e.g. a GitHub Pages project page at
 57:             // `<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) instead of the domain root.
 58:             let worker = Worker::new_with_options("worker.js", &options)?;
 59: 
 60:             let sink = completed.clone();
 61:             let handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>::new(move |event: MessageEvent| {
 62:                 if let Some(done) = parse_done_message(&event) {
 63:                     sink.borrow_mut().push(done);
 64:                 }
 65:             });
 66:             worker.set_onmessage(Some(handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
 67: 
 68:             let init = js_sys::Object::new();
 69:             Reflect::set(&init, &"type".into(), &"init".into())?;
 70:             Reflect::set(&init, &"query".into(), &query.into())?;
 71:             Reflect::set(&init, &"seed".into(), &(default_seed as f64).into())?;
 72:             worker.post_message(&init)?;
 73: 
 74:             workers.push(worker);
 75:             handlers.push(handler);
 76:         }
 77: 
 78:         let (seed, config) =
 79:             crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
 80:         Ok(Self {
 81:             workers,
 82:             next_worker: 0,
 83:             completed,
 84:             _handlers: handlers,
 85:             fallback: LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config),
 86:         })
 87:     }
 88: 
 89:     pub fn pool_size(&self) -> usize {
 90:         self.workers.len()
 91:     }
 92: }
 93: 
 94: impl ChunkSourcePort for WorkerChunkSource {
 95:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
 96:         self.fallback.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     fn load_with_reality(
100:         &self,
101:         origin_x: f32,
102:         origin_z: f32,
103:         level: u32,
104:         lod: u8,
105:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
106:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
107:         self.fallback
108:             .load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
109:     }
110: 
111:     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
112:         true
113:     }
114: 
115:     fn request(&mut self, request: ChunkRequest) {
116:         let message = js_sys::Object::new();
117:         let set = |k: &str, v: JsValue| {
118:             let _ = Reflect::set(&message, &k.into(), &v);
119:         };
120:         set("type", "gen".into());
121:         set("requestId", (request.request_id as f64).into());
122:         set("ox", (request.origin_x as f64).into());
123:         set("oz", (request.origin_z as f64).into());
124:         set("level", (request.level as f64).into());
125:         set("lod", (request.lod as f64).into());
126:         let reality_words = request.reality.to_words();
127:         let reality = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(reality_words.as_slice());
128:         set("reality", reality.into());
129:         let worker = &self.workers[self.next_worker % self.workers.len()];
130:         self.next_worker = self.next_worker.wrapping_add(1);
131:         let _ = worker.post_message(&message);
132:     }
133: 
134:     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
135:         std::mem::take(&mut *self.completed.borrow_mut())
136:     }
137: }
138: 
139: /// Decodes one `{type:"done", ...}` worker reply. Any malformed message is
140: /// dropped; the engine re-requests the chunk on a later tick because its
141: /// pending entry is only cleared by a matching completion or eviction.
142: fn parse_done_message(event: &MessageEvent) -> Option<CompletedChunk> {
143:     let data = event.data();
144:     let field = |name: &str| Reflect::get(&data, &name.into()).ok();
145:     if field("type")?.as_string()? != "done" {
146:         return None;
147:     }
148:     let request = ChunkRequest {
149:         request_id: field("requestId")?.as_f64()? as u32,
150:         origin_x: field("ox")?.as_f64()? as f32,
151:         origin_z: field("oz")?.as_f64()? as f32,
152:         level: field("level")?.as_f64()? as u32,
153:         lod: field("lod")?.as_f64()? as u8,
154:         reality: {
155:             let encoded = field("reality")?;
156:             let words = js_sys::Uint32Array::new(&encoded).to_vec();
157:             RealitySnapshot::from_words(&words).ok()?
158:         },
159:     };
160:     let buffer: ArrayBuffer = field("buf")?.dyn_into().ok()?;
161:     let bytes = Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec();
162:     let payload = decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)?;
163:     Some(CompletedChunk { request, payload })
164: }
````

````rust
 3: /// Interface Adapter to convert MergedQuads to JSON format for the web presentation layer.
 4: pub struct JsonPresenter;
 5: 
 6: impl JsonPresenter {
 7:     pub fn render_voxels(quads: &[MergedQuad]) -> String {
 8:         let mut json = String::with_capacity(quads.len() * 100);
 9:         json.push('[');
10: 
11:         for (i, quad) in quads.iter().enumerate() {
12:             let dir_str = match quad.dir {
13:                 FaceDirection::Up => "\"up\"",
14:                 FaceDirection::Down => "\"down\"",
15:                 FaceDirection::North => "\"north\"",
16:                 FaceDirection::South => "\"south\"",
17:                 FaceDirection::East => "\"east\"",
18:                 FaceDirection::West => "\"west\"",
19:             };
20: 
21:             let type_str = match quad.v_type {
22:                 VoxelType::Wall => "\"wall\"",
23:                 VoxelType::Floor => "\"floor\"",
24:                 VoxelType::Ceiling => "\"ceiling\"",
25:                 VoxelType::Light => "\"light\"",
26:                 VoxelType::RedWall => "\"redwall\"",
27:                 VoxelType::Grass => "\"grass\"",
28:                 VoxelType::Water => "\"water\"",
29:                 VoxelType::Tree => "\"tree\"",
30:                 VoxelType::RedLight => "\"redlight\"",
31:                 VoxelType::PaleWall => "\"palewall\"",
32:                 VoxelType::DamagedWall => "\"damagedwall\"",
33:                 VoxelType::DryCarpet => "\"drycarpet\"",
34:                 VoxelType::DeepCarpet => "\"deepcarpet\"",
35:                 VoxelType::StickyCarpet => "\"stickycarpet\"",
36:                 VoxelType::Fluid => "\"fluid\"",
37:                 VoxelType::Glimmer => "\"glimmer\"",
38:             };
39: 
40:             let obj = format!(
41:                 "{{\"x\":{},\"y\":{},\"z\":{},\"w\":{},\"h\":{},\"dir\":{},\"type\":{},\"color\":{}}}",
42:                 quad.x, quad.y, quad.z, quad.w, quad.h, dir_str, type_str, quad.color
43:             );
44: 
45:             json.push_str(&obj);
46:             if i < quads.len() - 1 {
47:                 json.push(',');
48:             }
49:         }
50: 
51:         json.push(']');
52:         json
53:     }
54: }
````

````rust
 69: /// Occupancy lookup used by the surface extractor. Coordinates are relative
 70: /// to the meshed chunk; implementations may resolve a one-voxel halo from
 71: /// adjacent chunks or a deterministically generated border. Missing lateral
 72: /// neighbors must be conservative (solid), never treated as air.
 73: pub trait VoxelNeighborhood {
 74:     fn voxel(&self, x: i32, y: i32, z: i32) -> u8;
 75: }
 76: 
 77: struct GridNeighborhood<'a> {
 78:     grid: &'a VoxelGrid,
 79:     origin: [usize; 3],
 80:     conservative_lateral_border: bool,
 81: }
 82: 
 83: impl VoxelNeighborhood for GridNeighborhood<'_> {
 84:     fn voxel(&self, x: i32, y: i32, z: i32) -> u8 {
 85:         let gx = self.origin[0] as i32 + x;
 86:         let gy = self.origin[1] as i32 + y;
 87:         let gz = self.origin[2] as i32 + z;
 88:         if gy < 0 || gy >= self.grid.height() as i32 {
 89:             return VOXEL_AIR;
 90:         }
 91:         if gx < 0 || gx >= self.grid.width() as i32 || gz < 0 || gz >= self.grid.depth() as i32 {
 92:             return if self.conservative_lateral_border {
 93:                 VOXEL_WALL
 94:             } else {
 95:                 VOXEL_AIR
 96:             };
 97:         }
 98:         self.grid.get(gx as usize, gy as usize, gz as usize)
 99:     }
100: }
101: 
102: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
103: struct FaceKey {
104:     v_type: VoxelType,
105:     color: u32,
106:     light: u8,
107:     ao: u8,
108: }

110: pub struct VoxelMapper {
111:     pub voxel_scale: f32,

114: impl VoxelMapper {
115:     pub fn new(voxel_scale: f32) -> Self {
116:         Self { voxel_scale }

119:     /// Maps the entire grid into merged exposed quads. This compatibility
120:     /// helper treats out-of-grid X/Z as air; streamed rendering should use
121:     /// [`Self::map_voxel_grid_with_padding`] instead.
122:     pub fn map_voxel_grid(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
123:         let neighborhood = GridNeighborhood {
124:             grid,
125:             origin: [0, 0, 0],
126:             conservative_lateral_border: false,
127:         };
128:         self.map_voxel_region(
129:             grid,
130:             [0, 0, 0],
131:             [grid.width(), grid.height(), grid.depth()],
132:             &neighborhood,
133:         )
134:     }
135: 
136:     /// Greedily meshes the interior of a grid carrying a one-voxel X/Z halo.
137:     /// Faces across a chunk edge are emitted only when the halo says the
138:     /// adjacent voxel is air, eliminating duplicate boundary faces and the
139:     /// pop that comes from assuming an unavailable neighbor is air.
140:     pub fn map_voxel_grid_with_padding(
141:         &self,
142:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
143:         lateral_padding: usize,
144:     ) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
145:         assert!(lateral_padding > 0, "surface meshing requires a voxel halo");
146:         assert!(grid.width() > lateral_padding * 2 && grid.depth() > lateral_padding * 2);
147:         let neighborhood = GridNeighborhood {
148:             grid,
149:             origin: [lateral_padding, 0, lateral_padding],
150:             conservative_lateral_border: true,
151:         };
152:         self.map_voxel_region(
153:             grid,
154:             [lateral_padding, 0, lateral_padding],
155:             [
156:                 grid.width() - lateral_padding * 2,
157:                 grid.height(),
158:                 grid.depth() - lateral_padding * 2,
159:             ],
160:             &neighborhood,
161:         )
162:     }
163: 
164:     /// Surface extraction against a supplied occupancy neighborhood. The
165:     /// dense `grid` supplies material/light/AO attributes for the interior;
166:     /// `neighborhood` decides whether each candidate face is exposed.
167:     pub fn map_voxel_region(
168:         &self,
169:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
170:         interior_origin: [usize; 3],
171:         dimensions: [usize; 3],
172:         neighborhood: &dyn VoxelNeighborhood,
173:     ) -> Vec<MergedQuad> {
174:         let mut quads = Vec::new();
175:         let scale = self.voxel_scale;
176:         let [w_dim, h_dim, d_dim] = dimensions;
177: 
178:         let attrs = |x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, v: u8, dir: FaceDirection| {
179:             self.face_key(
180:                 grid,
181:                 interior_origin[0] + x,
182:                 interior_origin[1] + y,
183:                 interior_origin[2] + z,
184:                 v,
185:                 dir,
186:             )
187:         };
188:         let mut append = |x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, w: f32, h: f32, dir, key: FaceKey| {
189:             quads.push(MergedQuad {
190:                 x,
191:                 y,
192:                 z,
193:                 w,
194:                 h,
195:                 dir,
196:                 v_type: key.v_type,
197:                 color: key.color,
198:                 light: key.light,
199:                 ao: key.ao,
200:             });
201:         };
202: 
203:         // +Y / -Y faces: 2D slices in X/Z.
204:         for y in 0..h_dim {
205:             for (dir, dy) in [(FaceDirection::Up, 1), (FaceDirection::Down, -1)] {
206:                 let get_face = |x: usize, z: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
207:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
208:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
209:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32 + dy, z as i32) == VOXEL_AIR)
210:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
211:                 };
212:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(w_dim, d_dim, &get_face) {
213:                     append(
214:                         u as f32 * scale,
215:                         y as f32 * scale,
216:                         v as f32 * scale,
217:                         qw as f32 * scale,
218:                         qh as f32 * scale,
219:                         dir,
220:                         key,
221:                     );
222:                 }
223:             }
224:         }
225: 
226:         // -Z / +Z faces: 2D slices in X/Y.
227:         for z in 0..d_dim {
228:             for (dir, dz) in [(FaceDirection::North, -1), (FaceDirection::South, 1)] {
229:                 let get_face = |x: usize, y: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
230:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
231:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
232:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32 + dz) == VOXEL_AIR)
233:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
234:                 };
235:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(w_dim, h_dim, &get_face) {
236:                     append(
237:                         u as f32 * scale,
238:                         v as f32 * scale,
239:                         z as f32 * scale,
240:                         qw as f32 * scale,
241:                         qh as f32 * scale,
242:                         dir,
243:                         key,
244:                     );
245:                 }
246:             }
247:         }
248: 
249:         // +X / -X faces: 2D slices in Z/Y.
250:         for x in 0..w_dim {
251:             for (dir, dx) in [(FaceDirection::East, 1), (FaceDirection::West, -1)] {
252:                 let get_face = |z: usize, y: usize| -> Option<FaceKey> {
253:                     let v = neighborhood.voxel(x as i32, y as i32, z as i32);
254:                     (v != VOXEL_AIR
255:                         && neighborhood.voxel(x as i32 + dx, y as i32, z as i32) == VOXEL_AIR)
256:                         .then(|| attrs(x, y, z, v, dir))
257:                 };
258:                 for (u, v, qw, qh, key) in self.greedy_mesh_2d(d_dim, h_dim, &get_face) {
259:                     append(
260:                         x as f32 * scale,
261:                         v as f32 * scale,
262:                         u as f32 * scale,
263:                         qw as f32 * scale,
264:                         qh as f32 * scale,
265:                         dir,
266:                         key,
267:                     );
268:                 }
269:             }
270:         }
271: 
272:         quads
273:     }
274: 
275:     fn face_key(
276:         &self,
277:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
278:         x: usize,
279:         y: usize,
280:         z: usize,
281:         voxel: u8,
282:         dir: FaceDirection,
283:     ) -> FaceKey {
284:         let ao = u8::from(grid.get_face_occlusion(x, y, z) & dir.occlusion_bit() != 0);
285:         FaceKey {
286:             v_type: Self::voxel_type(voxel),
287:             color: Self::material_color(voxel),
288:             light: grid.get_light(x, y, z),
289:             ao,
290:         }
291:     }
292: 
293:     fn voxel_type(voxel: u8) -> VoxelType {
294:         match voxel {
295:             VOXEL_WALL => VoxelType::Wall,
296:             VOXEL_FLOOR => VoxelType::Floor,
297:             VOXEL_CEILING => VoxelType::Ceiling,
298:             VOXEL_LIGHT => VoxelType::Light,
299:             VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => VoxelType::RedLight,
300:             VOXEL_RED_WALL => VoxelType::RedWall,
301:             VOXEL_GRASS => VoxelType::Grass,
302:             VOXEL_WATER => VoxelType::Water,
303:             VOXEL_TREE => VoxelType::Tree,
304:             VOXEL_PALE_WALL => VoxelType::PaleWall,
305:             VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL => VoxelType::DamagedWall,
306:             VOXEL_DRY_CARPET => VoxelType::DryCarpet,
307:             VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET => VoxelType::DeepCarpet,
308:             VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET => VoxelType::StickyCarpet,
309:             VOXEL_FLUID => VoxelType::Fluid,
310:             VOXEL_GLIMMER => VoxelType::Glimmer,
311:             _ => VoxelType::Wall,
312:         }
313:     }
314: 
315:     fn material_color(voxel: u8) -> u32 {
316:         // Single authority: the palette table beside the material ids.
317:         MATERIAL_COLORS
318:             .get(voxel as usize)
319:             .copied()
320:             .unwrap_or(0x000000)
321:     }
322: 
323:     /// Helper that performs 2D greedy meshing on a slice.
324:     fn greedy_mesh_2d(
325:         &self,
326:         w_slice: usize,
327:         h_slice: usize,
328:         get_face: &dyn Fn(usize, usize) -> Option<FaceKey>,
329:     ) -> Vec<(usize, usize, usize, usize, FaceKey)> {
330:         let mut visited = vec![vec![false; h_slice]; w_slice];
331:         let mut quads = Vec::new();
332: 
333:         for v in 0..h_slice {
334:             for u in 0..w_slice {
335:                 if visited[u][v] {
336:                     continue;
337:                 }
338: 
339:                 if let Some(key) = get_face(u, v) {
340:                     // Find max width along u
341:                     let mut quad_w = 1;
342:                     while u + quad_w < w_slice {
343:                         if visited[u + quad_w][v] {
344:                             break;
345:                         }
346:                         if let Some(next) = get_face(u + quad_w, v) {
347:                             if next == key {
348:                                 quad_w += 1;
349:                                 continue;
350:                             }
351:                         }
352:                         break;
353:                     }
354: 
355:                     // Find max height along v
356:                     let mut quad_h = 1;
357:                     'expand_h: while v + quad_h < h_slice {
358:                         for du in 0..quad_w {
359:                             if visited[u + du][v + quad_h] {
360:                                 break 'expand_h;
361:                             }
362:                             if let Some(next) = get_face(u + du, v + quad_h) {
363:                                 if next != key {
364:                                     break 'expand_h;
365:                                 }
366:                             } else {
367:                                 break 'expand_h;
368:                             }
369:                         }
370:                         quad_h += 1;
371:                     }
372: 
373:                     // Mark matched area as visited
374:                     for dv in 0..quad_h {
375:                         for du in 0..quad_w {
376:                             visited[u + du][v + dv] = true;
377:                         }
378:                     }
379: 
380:                     quads.push((u, v, quad_w, quad_h, key));
381:                 }
382:             }
383:         }
384:         quads
385:     }
386: }
387: 
388: #[cfg(test)]
389: mod tests {
390:     use super::*;
391: 
392:     #[test]
393:     fn test_voxel_mapping() {
394:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(2, 2, 2);
395:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
396: 
397:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(1.0);
398:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid(&grid);
399: 
400:         // Single isolated wall block should have 6 faces merged as 6 quads of size 1x1
401:         assert_eq!(quads.len(), 6);
402:         for q in quads {
403:             assert_eq!(q.w, 1.0);
404:             assert_eq!(q.h, 1.0);
405:         }
406:     }

408:     #[test]
409:     fn test_greedy_merging() {
410:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 1, 1);
411:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
412:         grid.set(1, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
413:         grid.set(2, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
414:         grid.set(3, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
415: 
416:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(1.0);
417:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid(&grid);
418: 
419:         // The Up faces of these 4 aligned blocks should merge into a single 4x1 quad!
420:         let up_quads: Vec<&MergedQuad> = quads
421:             .iter()
422:             .filter(|q| q.dir == FaceDirection::Up)
423:             .collect();
424:         assert_eq!(up_quads.len(), 1);
425:         assert_eq!(up_quads[0].w, 4.0);
426:         assert_eq!(up_quads[0].h, 1.0);

428: 
429:     #[test]
430:     fn padded_mesher_does_not_emit_face_against_solid_halo() {
431:         // X/Z padding is one cell. The rightmost interior voxel touches a
432:         // solid halo voxel, so its +X face must not be generated.
433:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 1, 3);
434:         grid.set(2, 0, 1, VOXEL_WALL); // interior x = 1
435:         grid.set(3, 0, 1, VOXEL_WALL); // +X halo
436: 
437:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(1.0);
438:         let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid_with_padding(&grid, 1);
439:         assert!(
440:             !quads.iter().any(|q| q.dir == FaceDirection::East),
441:             "solid neighbor halo must suppress the boundary face"
442:         );
443:     }

448:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
449:         grid.set(1, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
450:         grid.set_light(0, 0, 0, 5);
451:         grid.set_light(1, 0, 0, 6);
452: 
453:         let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(1.0);
454:         let up: Vec<_> = mapper
455:             .map_voxel_grid(&grid)
456:             .into_iter()
457:             .filter(|q| q.dir == FaceDirection::Up)
````

````rust
  1: /// Represents a node inside the Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO).
  2: /// Implements a linearized, GPU-friendly design stored in a flat arena array.
  3: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  4: pub enum SvoNode {
  5:     /// Leaf node storing actual voxel attributes
  6:     Leaf {
  7:         voxel_type: u8,
  8:         color: u32,
  9:         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
 10:         face_occlusion: u8,
 11:     },
 12:     /// Internal parent node directing traversal to 8 children
 13:     Internal {
 14:         /// Base index in the arena vector where the 8 children nodes are stored contiguously.
 15:         child_base_index: u32,
 16:         /// Bitmask where bit `i` represents if child `i` is non-empty (1) or empty air (0).
 17:         child_mask: u8,
 18:     },
 19: }
 20: 
 21: /// The Sparse Voxel Octree aggregate root entity.
 22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
 23: pub struct SparseVoxelOctree {
 24:     pub root: usize,
 25:     pub nodes: Vec<SvoNode>,
 26:     pub depth: u32,
 27:     pub world_size: f32,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: impl SparseVoxelOctree {
 31:     /// Creates a new empty Sparse Voxel Octree.
 32:     pub fn new(depth: u32, world_size: f32) -> Self {
 33:         let root_node = SvoNode::Leaf {
 34:             voxel_type: 0,
 35:             color: 0,
 36:             light_rgb: [0; 3],
 37:             face_occlusion: 0,
 38:         };
 39:         Self {
 40:             root: 0,
 41:             nodes: vec![root_node],
 42:             depth,
 43:             world_size,
 44:         }
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     /// Checks if the SVO is entirely empty (air).
 48:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 49:         match self.nodes[self.root] {
 50:             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => voxel_type == 0,
 51:             SvoNode::Internal { child_mask, .. } => child_mask == 0,
 52:         }
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /// Queries the SVO for voxel attributes at integer coordinates `(x, y, z)`.
 56:     pub fn get(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
 57:         let max_coord = 1 << self.depth;
 58:         if x >= max_coord || y >= max_coord || z >= max_coord {
 59:             return None;
 60:         }
 61:         self.get_recursive(self.root, x, y, z, self.depth)
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     fn get_recursive(
 65:         &self,
 66:         node_idx: usize,
 67:         x: u32,
 68:         y: u32,
 69:         z: u32,
 70:         depth: u32,
 71:     ) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
 72:         if node_idx >= self.nodes.len() {
 73:             return None;
 74:         }
 75: 
 76:         match self.nodes[node_idx] {
 77:             SvoNode::Leaf {
 78:                 voxel_type,
 79:                 color,
 80:                 light_rgb,
 81:                 face_occlusion,
 82:             } => Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion)),
 83:             SvoNode::Internal {
 84:                 child_base_index,
 85:                 child_mask,
 86:             } => {
 87:                 if depth == 0 {
 88:                     return None;
 89:                 }
 90: 
 91:                 let bit = depth - 1;
 92:                 let octant_x = (x >> bit) & 1;
 93:                 let octant_y = (y >> bit) & 1;
 94:                 let octant_z = (z >> bit) & 1;
 95:                 let octant_idx = (octant_z << 2) | (octant_y << 1) | octant_x;
 96: 
 97:                 // Check if the octant is active in the child mask
 98:                 if (child_mask & (1 << octant_idx)) == 0 {
 99:                     return Some((0, 0, [0; 3], 0)); // Empty air
100:                 }
101: 
102:                 let child_node_idx = child_base_index as usize + octant_idx as usize;
103:                 let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
104:                 self.get_recursive(child_node_idx, x & mask, y & mask, z & mask, depth - 1)
105:             }
106:         }
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Sets voxel attributes at coordinate `(x, y, z)`. Splits nodes and collapses uniform subtrees recursively.
110:     pub fn set(
111:         &mut self,
112:         x: u32,
113:         y: u32,
114:         z: u32,
115:         voxel_type: u8,
116:         color: u32,
117:         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
118:         face_occlusion: u8,
119:     ) {
120:         let max_coord = 1 << self.depth;
121:         if x >= max_coord || y >= max_coord || z >= max_coord {
122:             return;
123:         }
124:         self.set_recursive(
125:             self.root,
126:             x,
127:             y,
128:             z,
129:             self.depth,
130:             voxel_type,
131:             color,
132:             light_rgb,
133:             face_occlusion,
134:         );
135:     }
136: 
137:     fn set_recursive(
138:         &mut self,
139:         node_idx: usize,
140:         x: u32,
141:         y: u32,
142:         z: u32,
143:         depth: u32,
144:         v_type: u8,
145:         col: u32,
146:         ll: [u8; 3],
147:         fo: u8,
148:     ) {
149:         match self.nodes[node_idx] {
150:             SvoNode::Leaf {
151:                 voxel_type,
152:                 color,
153:                 light_rgb,
154:                 face_occlusion,
155:             } => {
156:                 if voxel_type == v_type && color == col && light_rgb == ll && face_occlusion == fo {
157:                     return;
158:                 }
159: 
160:                 if depth == 0 {
161:                     self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Leaf {
162:                         voxel_type: v_type,
163:                         color: col,
164:                         light_rgb: ll,
165:                         face_occlusion: fo,
166:                     };
167:                     return;
168:                 }
169: 
170:                 // Split leaf node
171:                 let child_base_index = self.nodes.len() as u32;
172:                 let child_mask = if voxel_type == 0 { 0 } else { 0xFF };
173: 
174:                 for _ in 0..8 {
175:                     self.nodes.push(SvoNode::Leaf {
176:                         voxel_type,
177:                         color,
178:                         light_rgb,
179:                         face_occlusion,
180:                     });
181:                 }
182: 
183:                 self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Internal {
184:                     child_base_index,
185:                     child_mask,
186:                 };
187: 
188:                 self.set_recursive(node_idx, x, y, z, depth, v_type, col, ll, fo);
189:             }
190:             SvoNode::Internal {
191:                 child_base_index,
192:                 mut child_mask,
193:             } => {
194:                 let bit = depth - 1;
195:                 let octant_x = (x >> bit) & 1;
196:                 let octant_y = (y >> bit) & 1;
197:                 let octant_z = (z >> bit) & 1;
198:                 let octant_idx = (octant_z << 2) | (octant_y << 1) | octant_x;
199: 
200:                 let child_node_idx = child_base_index as usize + octant_idx as usize;
201: 
202:                 if v_type != 0 {
203:                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
204:                 }
205: 
206:                 self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Internal {
207:                     child_base_index,
208:                     child_mask,
209:                 };
210: 
211:                 let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
212:                 self.set_recursive(
213:                     child_node_idx,
214:                     x & mask,
215:                     y & mask,
216:                     z & mask,
217:                     depth - 1,
218:                     v_type,
219:                     col,
220:                     ll,
221:                     fo,
222:                 );
223: 
224:                 // Try to collapse
225:                 self.collapse_if_uniform(node_idx);
226:             }
227:         }
228:     }
229: 
230:     fn collapse_if_uniform(&mut self, node_idx: usize) {
231:         if let SvoNode::Internal {
232:             child_base_index, ..
233:         } = self.nodes[node_idx]
234:         {
235:             let first_child_idx = child_base_index as usize;
236:             let mut uniform = true;
237:             let mut first_val = None;
238: 
239:             for i in 0..8 {
240:                 match self.nodes[first_child_idx + i] {
241:                     SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
242:                         uniform = false;
243:                         break;
244:                     }
245:                     SvoNode::Leaf {
246:                         voxel_type,
247:                         color,
248:                         light_rgb,
249:                         face_occlusion,
250:                     } => {
251:                         if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
252:                             if vt != voxel_type
253:                                 || col != color
254:                                 || ll != light_rgb
255:                                 || fo != face_occlusion
256:                             {
257:                                 uniform = false;
258:                                 break;
259:                             }
260:                         } else {
261:                             first_val = Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion));
262:                         }
263:                     }
264:                 }
265:             }
266: 
267:             if uniform {
268:                 if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
269:                     self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Leaf {
270:                         voxel_type: vt,
271:                         color: col,
272:                         light_rgb: ll,
273:                         face_occlusion: fo,
274:                     };
275:                 }
276:             }
277:         }
278:     }
279: }
````
