  1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  2:     VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VoxelGrid,
  3: };
  4: use std::collections::VecDeque;
  5: 
  6: /// Warm fluorescent tube color for standard lights (0-15 per channel).
  7: const LIGHT_WARM: [u8; 3] = [15, 14, 11];
  8: /// Deep red exit/alarm light color.
  9: const LIGHT_RED: [u8; 3] = [15, 3, 2];
 10: /// Cool, very dim emergency glimmer (blackout recovery skeleton). Its short
 11: /// BFS falloff is what keeps deep blackout genuinely dark between cues.
 12: const LIGHT_GLIMMER: [u8; 3] = [3, 5, 7];
 13: 
 14: /// Calculates colored 3D voxel lighting across the dense VoxelGrid using a
 15: /// BFS flood-fill, Rethinking-Voxels style: three independent light channels
 16: /// (RGB, 0-15 each) propagate simultaneously, so a red exit light and a warm
 17: /// ceiling tube blend smoothly where their falloffs overlap instead of
 18: /// snapping at a binary boundary.
 19: /// Time complexity stays O(n) in the number of voxels.
 20: pub fn calculate_voxel_lighting(grid: &mut VoxelGrid) {
 21:     let w = grid.width();
 22:     let h = grid.height();
 23:     let d = grid.depth();
 24: 
 25:     let falloff: u8 = 1;
 26: 
 27:     let mut queue: VecDeque<(usize, usize, usize)> = VecDeque::new();
 28: 
 29:     // Pass 1: seed all light sources with their emission color.
 30:     for z in 0..d {
 31:         for y in 0..h {
 32:             for x in 0..w {
 33:                 let v = grid.get(x, y, z);
 34:                 if v == VOXEL_LIGHT || v == VOXEL_RED_LIGHT || v == VOXEL_GLIMMER {
 35:                     let rgb = match v {
 36:                         VOXEL_RED_LIGHT => LIGHT_RED,
 37:                         VOXEL_GLIMMER => LIGHT_GLIMMER,
 38:                         _ => LIGHT_WARM,
 39:                     };
 40:                     grid.set_light_rgb(x, y, z, rgb);
 41:                     queue.push_back((x, y, z));
 42:                 }
 43:             }
 44:         }
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     // Pass 2: BFS flood-fill, all three channels at once.
 48:     while let Some((cx, cy, cz)) = queue.pop_front() {
 49:         let current = grid.get_light_rgb(cx, cy, cz);
 50:         if current.iter().all(|&c| c <= falloff) {
 51:             continue;
 52:         }
 53: 
 54:         let neighbors: [(isize, isize, isize); 6] = [
 55:             (cx as isize + 1, cy as isize, cz as isize),
 56:             (cx as isize - 1, cy as isize, cz as isize),
 57:             (cx as isize, cy as isize + 1, cz as isize),
 58:             (cx as isize, cy as isize - 1, cz as isize),
 59:             (cx as isize, cy as isize, cz as isize + 1),
 60:             (cx as isize, cy as isize, cz as isize - 1),
 61:         ];
 62: 
 63:         for &(nx, ny, nz) in &neighbors {
 64:             if nx >= 0
 65:                 && nx < w as isize
 66:                 && ny >= 0
 67:                 && ny < h as isize
 68:                 && nz >= 0
 69:                 && nz < d as isize
 70:             {
 71:                 let (nx, ny, nz) = (nx as usize, ny as usize, nz as usize);
 72: 
 73:                 // Downward propagation has 0 falloff, creating vertical
 74:                 // light columns.
 75:                 let is_downward = ny < cy;
 76:                 let actual_falloff = if is_downward { 0 } else { falloff };
 77:                 let next = current.map(|c| c.saturating_sub(actual_falloff));
 78: 
 79:                 if next == [0; 3] {
 80:                     continue;
 81:                 }
 82: 
 83:                 let n_light = grid.get_light_rgb(nx, ny, nz);
 84:                 // Component-wise max: overlapping colored lights blend.
 85:                 let merged = [
 86:                     n_light[0].max(next[0]),
 87:                     n_light[1].max(next[1]),
 88:                     n_light[2].max(next[2]),
 89:                 ];
 90: 
 91:                 if merged != n_light {
 92:                     grid.set_light_rgb(nx, ny, nz, merged);
 93:                     // Only continue propagating through air.
 94:                     if grid.get(nx, ny, nz) == VOXEL_AIR {
 95:                         queue.push_back((nx, ny, nz));
 96:                     }
 97:                 }
 98:             }
 99:         }
100:     }
101: }
102: 
103: #[cfg(test)]
104: mod tests {
105:     use super::*;
106: 
107:     #[test]
108:     fn test_light_propagation() {
109:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(3, 3, 3);
110: 
111:         // Setup:
112:         // A single light in the middle
113:         grid.set(1, 1, 1, VOXEL_LIGHT);
114:         // A wall blocking light
115:         grid.set(2, 1, 1, crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL);
116: 
117:         calculate_voxel_lighting(&mut grid);
118: 
119:         assert_eq!(grid.get_light(1, 1, 1), 15);
120:         assert_eq!(grid.get_light(1, 2, 1), 14); // Above
121:         assert_eq!(grid.get_light(2, 1, 1), 14); // Wall itself lights up
122:         assert_eq!(grid.get_light(3, 1, 1), 0); // Behind the wall is out of bounds, so it returns 0 anyway
123:     }
124: 
125:     #[test]
126:     fn warm_light_is_tinted_not_white() {
127:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(3, 3, 3);
128:         grid.set(1, 1, 1, VOXEL_LIGHT);
129:         calculate_voxel_lighting(&mut grid);
130: 
131:         let [r, g, b] = grid.get_light_rgb(1, 1, 1);
132:         assert_eq!([r, g, b], LIGHT_WARM);
133:         // Propagation preserves relative warmth.
134:         let [nr, _, nb] = grid.get_light_rgb(0, 1, 1);
135:         assert!(nr > nb, "red channel must stay above blue: {nr} vs {nb}");
136:     }
137: 
138:     #[test]
139:     fn overlapping_colored_lights_blend_component_wise() {
140:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(5, 1, 1);
141:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_LIGHT);
142:         grid.set(4, 0, 0, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT);
143:         calculate_voxel_lighting(&mut grid);
144: 
145:         // The midpoint sees red strongly from the red light (distance 2:
146:         // 15-2=13) and green/blue mostly from the warm light.
147:         let [r, g, b] = grid.get_light_rgb(2, 0, 0);
148:         assert_eq!(r, 13, "red channel from the nearer-in-red source");
149:         assert_eq!(g, 12, "green channel from the warm source (14-2)");
150:         assert_eq!(b, 9, "blue channel from the warm source (11-2)");
151:         assert!(grid.get_light(2, 0, 0) == 13, "scalar is the max channel");
152:     }
153: }

  1: //! Converts the core greedy-quad output into the browser renderer's compact
  2: //! indexed mesh payload. Geometry stays chunk-local and fixed-point so WebGL
  3: //! uploads are small and camera precision does not degrade far from origin.
  4: 
  5: use vackrooms::adapters::voxel_mapper::{FaceDirection, MergedQuad, VoxelMapper, VoxelType};
  6: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  7:     VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR,
  8:     VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_PALE_WALL, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
  9:     VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
 10: };
 11: 
 12: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 13: use crate::application::ports::{POSITION_FIXED_SCALE, PackedVertex, SurfaceMeshPayload};
 14: 
 15: /// Builds a seam-safe surface payload from a grid that includes a one-voxel
 16: /// X/Z halo. The mapper consults that halo before emitting boundary faces.
 17: pub fn build_surface_mesh(
 18:     halo_grid: &VoxelGrid,
 19:     voxel_scale: f32,
 20:     lod: u8,
 21:     lateral_padding: usize,
 22: ) -> SurfaceMeshPayload {
 23:     let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(voxel_scale);
 24:     let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid_with_padding(halo_grid, lateral_padding);
 25:     let width = halo_grid.width() - lateral_padding * 2;
 26:     let depth = halo_grid.depth() - lateral_padding * 2;
 27:     let bounds = Aabb::new(
 28:         [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 29:         [
 30:             width as f32 * voxel_scale,
 31:             halo_grid.height() as f32 * voxel_scale,
 32:             depth as f32 * voxel_scale,
 33:         ],
 34:     );
 35:     let mut lights = Vec::new();
 36:     for rl in &halo_grid.runtime_lights {
 37:         lights.push(crate::application::ports::LightSource {
 38:             id: ((rl.world_pos[0].to_bits() as u64) << 32) | rl.world_pos[2].to_bits() as u64,
 39:             position: rl.world_pos,
 40:             half_size: rl.half_size,
 41:             color: rl.rgb,
 42:             radius: rl.range,
 43:             intensity: rl.intensity,
 44:             flicker_mode: 0,
 45:             enabled: rl.enabled,
 46:         });
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     let mut mesh = SurfaceMeshPayload {
 50:         vertices: Vec::with_capacity(quads.len() * 4),
 51:         indices: Vec::with_capacity(quads.len() * 6),
 52:         bounds,
 53:         lod,
 54:         light_volume: Vec::with_capacity(width * halo_grid.height() * depth * 3),
 55:         light_volume_size: [width as u32, halo_grid.height() as u32, depth as u32],
 56:         lights,
 57:         faces: crate::adapters::face_instances::build_face_instances(&quads, voxel_scale),
 58:         voxel_scale,
 59:     };
 60:     for z in 0..depth {
 61:         for y in 0..halo_grid.height() {
 62:             for x in 0..width {
 63:                 let [r, g, b] = halo_grid.get_light_rgb(x + lateral_padding, y, z + lateral_padding);
 64:                 // The grid light is 0-15, WebGL expects 0-255 for gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE RGB textures.
 65:                 mesh.light_volume.push(r * 17);
 66:                 mesh.light_volume.push(g * 17);
 67:                 mesh.light_volume.push(b * 17);
 68:             }
 69:         }
 70:     }
 71:     for quad in &quads {
 72:         append_quad(&mut mesh, quad, voxel_scale);
 73:     }
 74:     mesh
 75: }
 76: 
 77: fn append_quad(mesh: &mut SurfaceMeshPayload, quad: &MergedQuad, voxel_scale: f32) {
 78:     let x0 = quad.x;
 79:     let x1 = quad.x + quad.w;
 80:     let y0 = quad.y;
 81:     let y1 = quad.y + quad.h;
 82:     let z0 = quad.z;
 83:     let z1_horizontal = quad.z + quad.h;
 84:     let z1_x_face = quad.z + quad.w;
 85: 
 86:     // `w` and `h` span different local axes per face. Move the positive
 87:     // faces to the far voxel plane so the indexed mesh is a closed shell.
 88:     let points = match quad.dir {
 89:         FaceDirection::Up => {
 90:             let y = quad.y + voxel_scale;
 91:             [
 92:                 [x0, y, z0],
 93:                 [x0, y, z1_horizontal],
 94:                 [x1, y, z1_horizontal],
 95:                 [x1, y, z0],
 96:             ]
 97:         }
 98:         FaceDirection::Down => [
 99:             [x0, y0, z0],
100:             [x1, y0, z0],
101:             [x1, y0, z1_horizontal],
102:             [x0, y0, z1_horizontal],
103:         ],
104:         FaceDirection::North => [
105:             [x0, y0, quad.z],
106:             [x0, y1, quad.z],
107:             [x1, y1, quad.z],
108:             [x1, y0, quad.z],
109:         ],
110:         FaceDirection::South => {
111:             let z = quad.z + voxel_scale;
112:             [[x0, y0, z], [x1, y0, z], [x1, y1, z], [x0, y1, z]]
113:         }
114:         FaceDirection::East => {
115:             let x = quad.x + voxel_scale;
116:             [
117:                 [x, y0, z0],
118:                 [x, y1, z0],
119:                 [x, y1, z1_x_face],
120:                 [x, y0, z1_x_face],
121:             ]
122:         }
123:         FaceDirection::West => [
124:             [quad.x, y0, z0],
125:             [quad.x, y0, z1_x_face],
126:             [quad.x, y1, z1_x_face],
127:             [quad.x, y1, z0],
128:         ],
129:     };
130: 
131:     let base = mesh.vertices.len() as u32;
132:     let normal_axis = normal_axis(quad.dir);
133:     let material = material_id(quad.v_type);
134:     for position in points {
135:         mesh.vertices.push(PackedVertex {
136:             position: position.map(pack_position),
137:             normal_axis,
138:             material,
139:             static_indirect: quad.light,
140:             ao: quad.ao,
141:         });
142:     }
143:     mesh.indices
144:         .extend_from_slice(&[base, base + 1, base + 2, base, base + 2, base + 3]);
145: }
146: 
147: fn pack_position(value: f32) -> u16 {
148:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE)
149:         .round()
150:         .clamp(0.0, u16::MAX as f32) as u16
151: }
152: 
153: fn normal_axis(dir: FaceDirection) -> u8 {
154:     match dir {
155:         FaceDirection::Up => 0,
156:         FaceDirection::Down => 1,
157:         FaceDirection::North => 2,
158:         FaceDirection::South => 3,
159:         FaceDirection::East => 4,
160:         FaceDirection::West => 5,
161:     }
162: }
163: 
164: pub(crate) fn material_id(v_type: VoxelType) -> u8 {
165:     match v_type {
166:         VoxelType::Wall => VOXEL_WALL,
167:         VoxelType::Floor => VOXEL_FLOOR,
168:         VoxelType::Ceiling => VOXEL_CEILING,
169:         VoxelType::Light => VOXEL_LIGHT,
170:         VoxelType::RedWall => VOXEL_RED_WALL,
171:         VoxelType::Grass => VOXEL_GRASS,
172:         VoxelType::Water => VOXEL_WATER,
173:         VoxelType::Tree => VOXEL_TREE,
174:         VoxelType::RedLight => VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
175:         VoxelType::PaleWall => VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
176:         VoxelType::DamagedWall => VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
177:         VoxelType::DryCarpet => VOXEL_DRY_CARPET,
178:         VoxelType::DeepCarpet => VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET,
179:         VoxelType::StickyCarpet => VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET,
180:         VoxelType::Fluid => VOXEL_FLUID,
181:         VoxelType::Glimmer => VOXEL_GLIMMER,

  1: //! First-person player controller: mouse look, WASD movement with friction,
  2: //! and axis-separated sliding collision against the [`CollisionWorld`].
  3: //!
  4: //! The tuning constants are carried over 1:1 from the original JS client so
  5: //! the wasm port feels identical.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::collision::CollisionWorld;
  8: 
  9: /// Acceleration applied while a movement key is held (units/s^2 toward the
 10: /// wish direction). Terminal speed = ACCELERATION / FRICTION = 2.5 u/s (increased from 0.5 u/s).
 11: const ACCELERATION: f32 = 20.0;
 12: /// Exponential velocity damping factor (1/s).
 13: const FRICTION: f32 = 8.0;
 14: /// Radians of yaw/pitch per pixel of mouse movement.
 15: const MOUSE_SENSITIVITY: f32 = 0.002;
 16: /// Pitch is clamped just short of straight up/down to avoid gimbal flip.
 17: const PITCH_LIMIT: f32 = std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2 - 0.05;
 18: 
 19: /// Which movement keys are currently held.
 20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
 21: pub struct MoveIntent {
 22:     pub forward: bool,
 23:     pub backward: bool,
 24:     pub left: bool,
 25:     pub right: bool,
 26:     pub turn_left: bool,
 27:     pub turn_right: bool,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// Player state. Position is the *eye* position in world space.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 32: pub struct Player {
 33:     pub position: [f32; 3],
 34:     pub yaw: f32,
 35:     pub pitch: f32,
 36:     /// Velocity in camera-local space: x = strafe, z = forward.
 37:     vel_strafe: f32,
 38:     vel_forward: f32,
 39: }
 40: 
 41: impl Player {
 42:     pub fn new(position: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 43:         Self {
 44:             position,
 45:             yaw: 0.0,
 46:             pitch: 0.0,
 47:             vel_strafe: 0.0,
 48:             vel_forward: 0.0,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     /// Moves the player to an authored recovery point and clears momentum.
 53:     /// Pit relocation uses this instead of assigning `position` directly so
 54:     /// the velocity that carried the player over the edge cannot immediately
 55:     /// push them back into the same hazard.
 56:     pub fn relocate(&mut self, position: [f32; 3]) {
 57:         self.position = position;
 58:         self.vel_strafe = 0.0;
 59:         self.vel_forward = 0.0;
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     /// Applies a mouse movement delta (in pixels) to yaw/pitch.
 63:     pub fn apply_look(&mut self, dx: f32, dy: f32) {
 64:         self.yaw -= dx * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY;
 65:         self.pitch = (self.pitch - dy * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY).clamp(-PITCH_LIMIT, PITCH_LIMIT);
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     /// World-space unit forward vector projected on the ground plane.
 69:     pub fn forward(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 70:         [-self.yaw.sin(), 0.0, -self.yaw.cos()]
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     /// World-space unit right vector on the ground plane.
 74:     pub fn right(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 75:         [self.yaw.cos(), 0.0, -self.yaw.sin()]
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     /// Integrates one physics step and resolves collision by sliding:
 79:     /// the X and Z axes are moved and tested independently, so hitting a
 80:     /// wall diagonally slides the player along it instead of stopping dead.
 81:     pub fn step(&mut self, dt: f32, intent: &MoveIntent, world: &CollisionWorld) {
 82:         // Friction: exponential-style decay, matching `v -= v * 8 * dt`.
 83:         self.vel_strafe -= self.vel_strafe * FRICTION * dt;
 84:         self.vel_forward -= self.vel_forward * FRICTION * dt;
 85: 
 86:         // Turn via keyboard (Doom controls)
 87:         let turn_speed = 3.0; // radians per second
 88:         if intent.turn_left {
 89:             self.yaw += turn_speed * dt;
 90:         }
 91:         if intent.turn_right {
 92:             self.yaw -= turn_speed * dt;
 93:         }
 94: 
 95:         let mut wish_forward = (intent.forward as i32 - intent.backward as i32) as f32;
 96:         let mut wish_strafe = (intent.right as i32 - intent.left as i32) as f32;
 97:         let len = (wish_forward * wish_forward + wish_strafe * wish_strafe).sqrt();
 98:         if len > 0.0 {
 99:             wish_forward /= len;
100:             wish_strafe /= len;
101:         }
102: 
103:         self.vel_forward += wish_forward * ACCELERATION * dt;
104:         self.vel_strafe += wish_strafe * ACCELERATION * dt;
105: 
106:         let fwd = self.forward();
107:         let rgt = self.right();
108:         let step_x = (fwd[0] * self.vel_forward + rgt[0] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
109:         let step_z = (fwd[2] * self.vel_forward + rgt[2] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
110: 
111:         let old = self.position;
112: 
113:         self.position[0] = old[0] + step_x;
114:         if world.collides(self.position) {
115:             self.position[0] = old[0];
116:         }
117: 
118:         self.position[2] = old[2] + step_z;
119:         if world.collides(self.position) {
120:             self.position[2] = old[2];
121:         }
122:     }
123: }
124:

## File: README.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine in Rust, structured with documented Clean
  4: Architecture and compiled to WebAssembly. Procedural "backrooms" world
  5: generation, BFS lighting, sparse voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk
  6: streaming and sliding player collision all run inside one wasm
  7: module — built to hold up on low-spec hardware. Rendering is pluggable:
  8: a greedy-meshed WebGL2 rasterizer by default, with an instanced face-splat
  9: path, a retained SVO raymarcher, and a CPU-only software fallback all
 10: selectable at runtime (see [Renderer backends](#renderer-backends)).
 11: 
 12: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design (layer map, ports,
 13: data flow, texel encodings, streaming and rendering pipeline).
 14: 
 15: ## How it works
 16: 
 17: Each chunk goes through the same pipeline, on the main thread or in a
 18: generation worker:
 19: 
 20: 1. **Procedural generation** (`src/use_cases/generate_chunk.rs` +
 21:    `*_level.rs`) — a `LevelGenerator` fills a `VoxelGrid` deterministically
 22:    from `(chunk position, seed, config)`. Level 0 is the office backrooms;
 23:    level 34 is an open grassland. Both tile seamlessly because geometry is
 24:    derived from world-space coordinates, never chunk-local ones.
 25: 2. **BFS lighting** — light sources placed by the generator flood-fill
 26:    through open voxels to produce per-voxel RGB light levels.
 27: 3. **SVO build + serialize** — the lit grid is packed into a sparse voxel
 28:    octree and serialized into the GPU texel encoding the renderer expects
 29:    (`src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`).
 30: 4. **Streaming** (`wasm_frontend/src/application/streaming.rs`) — chunks
 31:    around the player are requested, LOD'd by distance, and evicted as the
 32:    player moves; a coarse-first pass keeps distant chunks cheap.
 33: 5. **Collision** — player movement is axis-separated (X and Z tested and
 34:    moved independently against a `CollisionWorld`), so hitting a wall
 35:    diagonally slides along it instead of stopping dead.
 36: 6. **Render** — one of four interchangeable `RendererPort` implementations
 37:    draws the resident chunks (see below).
 38: 
 39: A standing gameplay quirk: leaning into a wall for a few seconds has a
 40: chance to "noclip" the player between level 0 (backrooms) and level 34
 41: (grassland) — see `update_noclip` in
 42: `wasm_frontend/src/application/engine.rs`.
 43: 
 44: ### Renderer backends
 45: 
 46: Chosen with `?renderer=` (see [Usage](#usage)):
 47: 
 48: | Value | Backend | Notes |
 49: |---|---|---|
 50: | *(default)* | `SurfaceRenderer` | Indexed greedy meshes, WebGL2 fixed-function depth. The SVO is kept for collision/debug only — no fragment shader walks it. |
 51: | `splat` | `SplatRenderer` | Instanced face-splat "microvoxel" path: one instance per visible surface rectangle, lit once in the vertex shader. |
 52: | `raymarch` | `WebGl2Renderer` | The retained hybrid SVO raymarcher: per-fragment octree walk against an RGBA32UI node-atlas texture. |
 53: | `cpu` | `CpuCanvasRenderer` | Software rasterizer blitted via `ImageData`; no WebGL context at all. |
 54: 
 55: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` fall back automatically (to CPU, or to
 56: surfaces) if WebGL2 or the requested backend is unavailable.
 57: 
 58: ## Build & run
 59: 
 60: Prerequisites: Rust (with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target) and
 61: [`wasm-pack`](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/).
 62: The page imports wasm-bindgen's native ES-module output directly; there is no
 63: webpack build stage in this repository.
 64: 
 65: ```sh
 66: # 1. Build the wasm front end into static/pkg/
 67: wasm-pack build wasm_frontend --target web --release --no-typescript --out-dir ../static/pkg
 68: 
 69: # 2. Run the dev server
 70: cargo run
 71: 
 72: # 3. Open http://localhost:3000
 73: ```
 74: 
 75: ## Usage
 76: 
 77: Click to capture the mouse; WASD to move, ESC to release.
 78: 
 79: - `http://localhost:3000/` — wasm engine (low-spec profile: 3×3 chunk
 80:   streaming, 0.2 u voxels, adaptive resolution)
 81: - `http://localhost:3000/?spec=high` — high-spec profile (5×5 chunks,
 82:   0.1 u voxels)
 83: - `http://localhost:3000/legacy` — the preserved original Three.js/JS client,
 84:   which fetches chunks from the server's `/maze` and `/octree` endpoints
 85:   instead of generating them in the browser
 86: 
 87: Worlds are shareable by URL — every query parameter below is optional and
 88: combinable:
 89: 
 90: | Parameter | Values | Effect |
 91: |---|---|---|
 92: | `spec` | `high` | Switches to the high-spec profile (finer voxels, wider streaming radius). Default is low-spec. |
 93: | `seed` | number or text | World seed. Non-numeric text is hashed (FNV-1a) so words work too. |
 94: | `pillars` | `0`–`4` | Structural column density multiplier (`0` = none). Default `1`. |
 95: | `walls` | `0`–`4` | Office wall density multiplier (`0` = open plan). Default `1`. |
 96: | `atria` | `0`–`4` | How much of the world vaults into tall atria. Default `1`. |
 97: | `lights` | `0`–`4` | Ceiling light panel density. Default `1`. |
 98: | `renderer` | `splat`, `raymarch`, `cpu` | Picks a non-default renderer backend (see above). |
 99: | `workers` | `0` | Disables the Web Worker generation pool and generates chunks synchronously on the main thread. |
100: | `level` | `0`, `34` | Debug: boots straight into a level (34 = the grassland) instead of waiting on a noclip roll. |
101: | `force_anomaly` | `pillars`, `blackout`, `pits`, `archway`, `redroom` | Debug: guarantees one anomaly of that family near spawn, bypassing organic frequency and the spawn keep-out. |
102: | `rt_hiz` | `0`, `1` | CPU hierarchical-Z rejection. |
103: | `rt_f2b` | `0`, `1` | CPU/raymarch near-to-far traversal. |
104: | `rt_mips` | `0`, `1` | CPU projected-size MIP/LOD collapse. |
105: | `rt_beam_occlusion` | `0`, `1` | CPU cone-light occlusion rays. |
106: | `rt_shadows` | `0`, `1` | GPU hero-light shadow pass. |
107: | `rt_cells` | `0`, `1` | GPU splat cell-range culling. |
108: | `rt_budget` | `0`, `1` | GPU splat far-chunk face budget. |
109: | `rt_cull` | `0`, `1` | CPU and raster-GPU chunk visibility culling. |
110: | `rt_dither` | `0`, `1` | GPU dither/grain effects. |
111: | `rt_timer` | `0`, `1` | Asynchronous GPU timing queries. |
112: 
113: The top-right HUD names the section you are in (level, zone, region), and
114: **F3** (or Settings → Debug) toggles the anomaly debug overlay: reality
115: epochs, resident traversal gates and pit hazards, and streaming counters.
116: 
117: The in-page settings menu (gear icon) also exposes mouse sensitivity, invert
118: Y, render scale, FOV, control scheme, and every renderer optimization switch.
119: Live preferences are saved to `localStorage`; Apply & Reload writes disabled
120: optimizations into the URL so a regression setup can be shared exactly.
121: 
122: ## GitHub Pages
123: 
124: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds `wasm_frontend` in release mode and
125: deploys `static/` on every push to `master` (or via manual dispatch). The
126: main engine (`/`, low- and high-spec profiles) generates chunks entirely in
127: the browser, so it needs nothing but static files and runs unmodified from a
128: Pages project URL (`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) — the worker pool
129: resolves `worker.js` relative to the page, not from the domain root.
130: 
131: The `/legacy` client and the `/maze`/`/octree` endpoints depend on
132: `src/main.rs`'s native HTTP server and cannot run on Pages; only the wasm
133: engine is served there.
134: 
135: One-time setup: in the repo's Settings → Pages, set Source to "GitHub
136: Actions".
137: 
138: ## Tests
139: 
140: ```sh
141: cargo test --workspace
142: npm run test:visual
143: ```
144: 
145: The application layers are browser-free by construction, so player physics,
146: collision, streaming, atlas assembly and input mapping are all covered by
147: native unit tests. The visual command first rebuilds `static/pkg` with
148: `wasm-pack`, then boots every renderer in Chromium and runs the approved
149: surface screenshot regression; it cannot pass against a stale WASM bundle.
150: 
151: ## Workspace layout
152: 
153: | Path | What it is |
154: |---|---|
155: | `src/` | `vackrooms` core: entities, use cases, adapters + native dev server |
156: | `wasm_frontend/` | Browser client: application / adapters / drivers (wasm-only) |
157: | `static/` | Thin HTML shell, wasm bundle output (`pkg/`), legacy client |
158: | `wasm_raycaster/` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (reference only) |
159: 
160: ## Modifying the engine
161: 
162: Ports (traits) sit at the boundary of each layer; implement the trait rather
163: than reaching into a concrete type:
164: 
165: - **New procedural level** — implement `LevelGenerator`
166:   (`src/use_cases/level_generator.rs`) alongside `backrooms_level.rs` /
167:   `grassland_level.rs`, register a level id, and give it a native unit test
168:   (generation must be deterministic and seamless at chunk borders — see the
169:   contract documented on the trait).
170: - **New renderer backend** — implement `RendererPort`
171:   (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`) under `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/`
172:   and wire a `?renderer=` value into `create_renderer` in
173:   `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/browser.rs`.
174: - **New chunk source** (e.g. a different streaming/caching strategy) —
175:   implement `ChunkSourcePort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`); see
176:   `LocalChunkSource` and `WorkerChunkSource` for the synchronous and
177:   worker-pool implementations.
178: - **Player/physics tuning** — `wasm_frontend/src/application/player.rs` and
179:   `engine.rs`; both are plain Rust, unit-tested natively without a browser.
180: 
181: After changing anything under `src/` or `wasm_frontend/src/`, run
182: `cargo test --workspace` (native, browser-free) before rebuilding the wasm
183: bundle with the command in [Build & run](#build--run). See
184: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layer map and data flow.
````

## File: src/domain/entities/architecture.rs
````rust
  1: //! Pure architectural domain types for procedurally *planned* levels.
  2: //!
  3: //! These describe a region-scale building plan — who designed it
  4: //! ([`ArchitectGenome`]), what each space is for ([`SpaceProgram`]), how
  5: //! circulation feeds spaces ([`CirculationSpine`]), and how spaces are
  6: //! assembled ([`AssemblyInstance`]) — before anything is voxelized. The
  7: //! planner (`use_cases::region_plan`) fills these in; the level generator
  8: //! samples them per voxel column. Nothing here knows about voxels, chunks,
  9: //! rendering, or WASM.
 10: //!
 11: //! All types are small, plain data. Determinism comes from how they are
 12: //! *derived* (seed + region coordinate), not from anything stored here.
 13: 
 14: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyInstance;
 15: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 16: 
 17: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 18: // Architect genomes: a "design culture" as a seed-derived parameter set.
 19: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 20: 
 21: /// How a designer routes people through a region.
 22: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 23: pub enum CirculationStyle {
 24:     /// One straight main corridor wall-to-wall.
 25:     StraightSpine,
 26:     /// A main corridor that bends at interior waypoints.
 27:     MeanderingSpine,
 28:     /// A primary spine with two short, disconnected-looking branches.
 29:     PairedBranches,
 30:     /// A spine plus stub branches that dead-end (unease by design).
 31:     TreeWithCulDeSacs,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// How a designer holds the ceiling up.
 35: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 36: pub enum StructuralSystem {
 37:     /// Columns on a square grid.
 38:     RegularGrid,
 39:     /// Wider bays in one axis, expressed as ceiling beams.
 40:     DeepSpansWithBeams,
 41:     /// Alternate column rows shifted half a bay.
 42:     OffsetGrid,
 43:     /// Columns only around cores and the perimeter.
 44:     CoreAndShell,
 45: }
 46: 
 47: /// Preferred room shapes.
 48: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
 49: pub struct ProportionRules {
 50:     /// Smallest room side a designer will draw, world units.
 51:     pub min_side: f32,
 52:     /// Largest room side, world units.
 53:     pub max_side: f32,
 54:     /// 0 = square rooms, 1 = strongly elongated rooms.
 55:     pub elongation: f32,
 56: }
 57: 
 58: /// How rooms open onto circulation.
 59: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 60: pub enum ThresholdLanguage {
 61:     /// Standard door-width opening under a solid lintel.
 62:     DoorWithLintel,
 63:     /// Full-height opening, no lintel.
 64:     OpenPortal,
 65:     /// Double-width opening under a lintel (suites, conference).
 66:     WidePortal,
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Ceiling articulation.
 70: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 71: pub enum CeilingLanguage {
 72:     /// Flat acoustic tile everywhere.
 73:     FlatTiles,
 74:     /// Beam grid with recessed panels.
 75:     Coffered,
 76:     /// Lowered continuous soffit (mechanical-heavy designers).
 77:     ExposedSoffit,
 78: }
 79: 
 80: /// Where the lights go.
 81: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 82: pub enum LightingLanguage {
 83:     /// Fluorescent modules on the ceiling grid.
 84:     GridPanels,
 85:     /// Continuous strips that follow circulation.
 86:     StripsAlongCirculation,
 87:     /// Sparse single fixtures (renovated or neglected areas).
 88:     SparsePendants,
 89: }
 90: 
 91: /// What later occupants did to the original plan.
 92: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 93: pub enum RenovationStyle {
 94:     /// Plan left as designed.
 95:     Untouched,
 96:     /// One assembly re-partitioned in a second designer's language.
 97:     PartialRefit,
 98:     /// Renovation structure overlaid on the original (contradictory columns).
 99:     LayeredRefits,
100: }
101: 
102: /// A design culture: every plan decision in a region is parameterized by one
103: /// of these. Derived deterministically from `(seed, region coordinate)`.
104: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
105: pub struct ArchitectGenome {
106:     pub circulation: CirculationStyle,
107:     pub structural_system: StructuralSystem,
108:     pub room_proportions: ProportionRules,
109:     pub threshold_language: ThresholdLanguage,
110:     pub ceiling_language: CeilingLanguage,
111:     pub lighting_language: LightingLanguage,
112:     /// 0 = bare shells, 1 = densely partitioned interiors.
113:     pub furnishing_density: f32,
114:     pub renovation_history: RenovationStyle,
115:     /// 0 = happily asymmetric, 1 = mirrors and centers everything.
116:     pub tolerance_for_symmetry: f32,
117: }
118: 
119: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
120: // Program: what a space is *for*.
121: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
122: 
123: /// First-class space semantics (the old room stamps, promoted to meaning).
124: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
125: pub enum SpaceProgram {
126:     Arrival,
127:     Reception,
128:     MainCorridor,
129:     SecondaryHall,
130:     OpenOffice,
131:     PrivateOffice,
132:     ConferenceRoom,
133:     WaitingArea,
134:     BreakRoom,
135:     Storage,
136:     ServerRoom,
137:     RestroomCore,
138:     Stair,
139:     Mechanical,
140:     Atrium,
141:     /// Planned, built, never occupied: lit shell or unlit void.
142:     AbandonedExpansion,
143: }
144: 
145: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146: // Geometry helpers (deliberately minimal — rectilinear plans only).
147: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148: 
149: /// A simple closed 2D polygon in world space. The planner only emits convex
150: /// rectilinear footprints, so containment is tested with the even-odd rule
151: /// and no general polygon library is needed.
152: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
153: pub struct Polygon2 {
154:     /// (x, z) vertices in world space, wound consistently.
155:     pub vertices: Vec<(f32, f32)>,
156: }
157: 
158: impl Polygon2 {
159:     /// Axis-aligned rectangle from min corner and size.
160:     pub fn rect(x: f32, z: f32, w: f32, d: f32) -> Self {
161:         Self {
162:             vertices: vec![(x, z), (x + w, z), (x + w, z + d), (x, z + d)],
163:         }
164:     }
165: 
166:     /// Even-odd containment test.
167:     pub fn contains(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> bool {
168:         let v = &self.vertices;
169:         let mut inside = false;
170:         let mut j = v.len() - 1;
171:         for i in 0..v.len() {
172:             let (xi, zi) = v[i];
173:             let (xj, zj) = v[j];
174:             if ((zi > z) != (zj > z)) && (x < (xj - xi) * (z - zi) / (zj - zi) + xi) {
175:                 inside = !inside;
176:             }
177:             j = i;
178:         }
179:         inside
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Axis-aligned bounds: (min_x, min_z, max_x, max_z).
183:     pub fn bounds(&self) -> (f32, f32, f32, f32) {
184:         let mut b = (f32::MAX, f32::MAX, f32::MIN, f32::MIN);
185:         for &(x, z) in &self.vertices {
186:             b.0 = b.0.min(x);
187:             b.1 = b.1.min(z);
188:             b.2 = b.2.max(x);
189:             b.3 = b.3.max(z);
190:         }
191:         b
192:     }
193: }
194: 
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: // Assemblies: planned spaces with structure, ceilings and fixtures.
197: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
198: 
199: /// A doorway/portal on an assembly boundary, opening onto circulation.
200: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
201: pub struct Opening {
202:     /// Center of the opening in world space (on the footprint boundary).
203:     pub center: Position,
204:     /// Clear width, world units (>= ~1.0 per walkability contract).
205:     pub width: f32,
206:     /// True if the opening runs through a wall parallel to the X axis
207:     /// (i.e. you walk through it along Z).
208:     pub through_x_wall: bool,
209:     /// Lintel underside height in units; `None` = full-height portal.
210:     pub lintel_units: Option<f32>,
211: }
212: 
213: /// A named subspace inside an assembly (a private office in a suite, a stall
214: /// block in a restroom core). v1 keeps these as tagged rectangles.
215: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
216: pub struct Space {
217:     pub program: SpaceProgram,
218:     pub footprint: Polygon2,
219: }
220: 
221: /// A concrete structural layout for one assembly.
222: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
223: pub struct StructuralSystemInstance {
224:     pub system: StructuralSystem,
225:     /// Column spacing along X / Z, world units.
226:     pub bay_x: f32,
227:     pub bay_z: f32,
228:     /// World-space phase of the grid (so neighboring assemblies don't align).
229:     pub phase: (f32, f32),
230:     /// Column side, world units.
231:     pub column_side: f32,
232: }
233: 
234: /// A ceiling treatment over a sub-area of an assembly.
235: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
236: pub struct CeilingZone {
237:     pub area: Polygon2,
238:     pub language: CeilingLanguage,
239:     /// Finished ceiling height, world units.
240:     pub height_units: f32,
241: }
242: 
243: /// One light fixture, tied to a ceiling module (not a free grid point).
244: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
245: pub struct Fixture {
246:     pub at: Position,
247:     /// Fixture half-extent along X / Z (a 2x0.6 strip, a 0.6x0.6 panel...).
248:     pub half_x: f32,
249:     pub half_z: f32,
250:     pub lit: bool,
251: }
252: 
253: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
254: pub enum LightKind {
255:     CeilingPanel,
256:     Strip,
257:     Emergency,
258: }
259: 
260: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
261: pub struct RuntimeLight {
262:     pub world_pos: [f32; 3],
263:     pub half_size: [f32; 2],
264:     pub rgb: [f32; 3],
265:     pub range: f32,
266:     pub intensity: f32,
267:     pub enabled: bool,
268:     pub kind: LightKind,
269: }
270: 
271: /// A void reserved for building services (risers, plenums). v1: reserved and
272: /// rendered as sealed solids; kept in the model so later passes can route
273: /// through them.
274: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
275: pub struct ServiceVoid {
276:     pub area: Polygon2,
277: }
278: 
279: /// Backrooms-specific distortions applied to one assembly.
280: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
281: pub struct CorruptionProfile {
282:     /// Duplicated from another assembly with this world-space offset error.
283:     pub misalignment: (f32, f32),
284:     /// Built but never occupied: no fixtures lit, no furnishing.
285:     pub abandoned: bool,
286:     /// A second genome's structural grid overlaid on the original.
287:     pub renovation_overlay: bool,
288:     /// Every fixture in this room burns red. The *room* is the anomaly —
289:     /// its geometry stays ordinary; only the light exposes it. Red never
290:     /// appears as a wall material anywhere in Level 0.
291:     pub red_room: bool,
292: }
293: 
294: /// A planned, placed space: program + footprint + everything needed to
295: /// voxelize it believably.
296: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
297: pub struct AssemblyInstance {
298:     pub id: u32,
299:     pub program: SpaceProgram,
300:     pub footprint: Polygon2,
301:     pub entrances: Vec<Opening>,
302:     pub spaces: Vec<Space>,
303:     pub structure: StructuralSystemInstance,
304:     pub ceiling_zones: Vec<CeilingZone>,
305:     pub fixtures: Vec<Fixture>,
306:     pub service_voids: Vec<ServiceVoid>,
307:     pub corruption: CorruptionProfile,
308: }
309: 
310: /// A corridor: a wide polyline with priority over everything it crosses.
311: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
312: pub struct CirculationSpine {
313:     pub id: u32,
314:     /// `MainCorridor` or `SecondaryHall`.
315:     pub spine_kind: SpaceProgram,
316:     /// Axis-aligned polyline waypoints in world space.
317:     pub path: Vec<Position>,
318:     /// Clear width, world units.
319:     pub width: f32,
320: }
321: 
322: impl CirculationSpine {
323:     /// Distance from (x, z) to the spine centerline (axis-aligned segments).
324:     pub fn distance(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> f32 {
325:         self.nearest(x, z).0
326:     }
327: 
328:     /// Nearest point on the centerline: `(distance, along, is_horizontal)`.
329:     /// `along` is the world coordinate *along* the nearest segment's axis, so
330:     /// modules (light strips, wall gaps) repeat in world space and stay
331:     /// continuous across chunk and region borders.
332:     pub fn nearest(&self, x: f32, z: f32) -> (f32, f32, bool) {
333:         let mut best = (f32::MAX, 0.0, true);
334:         for seg in self.path.windows(2) {
335:             let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
336:             let (dx, dz) = (b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z);
337:             let len2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
338:             let t = if len2 > 0.0 {
339:                 (((x - a.x) * dx + (z - a.z) * dz) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
340:             } else {
341:                 0.0
342:             };
343:             let (px, pz) = (a.x + t * dx, a.z + t * dz);
344:             let d2 = (x - px) * (x - px) + (z - pz) * (z - pz);
345:             if d2 < best.0 {
346:                 let horizontal = dx.abs() >= dz.abs();
347:                 best = (d2, if horizontal { px } else { pz }, horizontal);
348:             }
349:         }
350:         (best.0.sqrt(), best.1, best.2)
351:     }
352: }
353: 
354: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
355: // The region plan.
356: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
357: 
358: /// Everything planned for one square region of the world. Regions tile a
359: /// fixed world-space lattice; a chunk generator asks for the plan of every
360: /// region its chunk overlaps and samples them per column.
361: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
362: pub struct RegionPlan {
363:     /// Lower-left corner in world space.
364:     pub origin_world: Position,
365:     /// Side length, world units.
366:     pub size_world: f32,
367:     /// Dominant designer first, then renovator, then optional intruder.
368:     pub architects: Vec<ArchitectGenome>,
369:     pub assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
370:     pub corridors: Vec<CirculationSpine>,
371:     /// Region-overlapping anomaly instances. Macro instances deliberately
372:     /// repeat in every intersected region with the same stable identity;
373:     /// consumers deduplicate them by [`AnomalyInstance::id`].
374:     pub anomalies: Vec<AnomalyInstance>,
375: }

377: #[cfg(test)]
378: mod tests {
379:     use super::*;
380: 
381:     #[test]
382:     fn rect_polygon_contains_interior_not_exterior() {
383:         let p = Polygon2::rect(10.0, 20.0, 5.0, 8.0);
384:         assert!(p.contains(12.0, 24.0));
385:         assert!(!p.contains(9.9, 24.0));
386:         assert!(!p.contains(12.0, 28.5));
387:         assert_eq!(p.bounds(), (10.0, 20.0, 15.0, 28.0));
388:     }
389: 
390:     #[test]
391:     fn spine_distance_measures_to_nearest_segment() {
392:         let spine = CirculationSpine {
393:             id: 0,
394:             spine_kind: SpaceProgram::MainCorridor,
395:             path: vec![
396:                 Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
397:                 Position::new(10.0, 0.0),
398:                 Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
399:             ],
400:             width: 2.0,
401:         };
402:         assert!((spine.distance(5.0, 3.0) - 3.0).abs() < 1e-5);
403:         assert!((spine.distance(13.0, 10.0) - 3.0).abs() < 1e-5);
404:         assert!((spine.distance(10.0, 5.0) - 0.0).abs() < 1e-5);
405:     }
406: }
