 57: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 58: #[allow(dead_code)] // `t`/`voxel_type` exist for the Debug dump on failure
 59: struct Hit {
 60:     chunk: usize,
 61:     t: f32,
 62:     /// Leaf box in chunk-local space.
 63:     box_min: [f32; 3],
 64:     box_max: [f32; 3],
 65:     voxel_type: u32,
 66: }
 67: 
 68: /// 1:1 Rust port of the GLSL `raymarchSVO` (same constants, same epsilons).
 69: fn raymarch_svo(
 70:     atlas: &[u32],
 71:     ro: [f32; 3],
 72:     rd: [f32; 3],
 73:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
 74:     t_entry: f32,
 75:     world_size: f32,
 76: ) -> Option<(f32, [f32; 3], [f32; 3], u32)> {
 77:     let mut t = t_entry;
 78:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
 79: 
 80:     let mut stack: Vec<(usize, [f32; 3], [f32; 3])> = Vec::new();
 81:     let mut current_node = chunk_root_idx;
 82:     let mut cmin = [0.0f32; 3];
 83:     let mut cmax = [world_size; 3];
 84: 
 85:     for _ in 0..160 {
 86:         let tx = current_node * 4;
 87:         let (is_leaf, a, b) = (atlas[tx] == 1, atlas[tx + 1], atlas[tx + 2]);
 88: 
 89:         if is_leaf {
 90:             if a != 0 {
 91:                 return Some((t, cmin, cmax, a));
 92:             }
 93:             // Empty-space skip to this leaf's exit plane.
 94:             let exit = |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
 95:             let tx = exit(cmin[0], cmax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
 96:             let ty = exit(cmin[1], cmax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
 97:             let tz = exit(cmin[2], cmax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
 98:             let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
 99:             t = t_exit;
100:             p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
101:             // Snap every tied axis past its exit plane (a ray exactly
102:             // through a corner advances diagonally; leaving an axis ON its
103:             // plane stalls the march instead).
104:             if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
105:                 p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { cmax[0] } else { cmin[0] })
106:                     + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
107:             }
108:             if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
109:                 p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { cmax[1] } else { cmin[1] })
110:                     + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
111:             }
112:             if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
113:                 p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { cmax[2] } else { cmin[2] })
114:                     + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
115:             }
116:             // Multi-level pop, mirroring the shader: the skip may cross
117:             // boundaries shared by several ancestor boxes at once.
118:             while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
119:                 let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
120:                 current_node = f.0;
121:                 cmin = f.1;
122:                 cmax = f.2;
123:             }
124:         } else {
125:             let center = [
126:                 (cmin[0] + cmax[0]) * 0.5,
127:                 (cmin[1] + cmax[1]) * 0.5,
128:                 (cmin[2] + cmax[2]) * 0.5,
129:             ];
130:             let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
131:             let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
132:             let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
133:             let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
134: 
135:             if b & (1 << child_idx) != 0 {
136:                 if stack.len() < 8 {
137:                     stack.push((current_node, cmin, cmax));
138:                 }
139:                 if ox == 1 {
140:                     cmin[0] = center[0]
141:                 } else {
142:                     cmax[0] = center[0]
143:                 }
144:                 if oy == 1 {
145:                     cmin[1] = center[1]
146:                 } else {
147:                     cmax[1] = center[1]
148:                 }
149:                 if oz == 1 {
150:                     cmin[2] = center[2]
151:                 } else {
152:                     cmax[2] = center[2]
153:                 }
154:                 current_node = a as usize + child_idx;
155:             } else {
156:                 let omin = [
157:                     if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cmin[0] },
158:                     if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cmin[1] },
159:                     if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cmin[2] },
160:                 ];
161:                 let omax = [
162:                     if ox == 1 { cmax[0] } else { center[0] },
163:                     if oy == 1 { cmax[1] } else { center[1] },
164:                     if oz == 1 { cmax[2] } else { center[2] },
165:                 ];
166:                 let exit =
167:                     |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
168:                 let tx = exit(omin[0], omax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
169:                 let ty = exit(omin[1], omax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
170:                 let tz = exit(omin[2], omax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
171:                 let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
172:                 t = t_exit;
173:                 p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
174:                 if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
175:                     p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { omax[0] } else { omin[0] })
176:                         + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
177:                 }
178:                 if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
179:                     p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { omax[1] } else { omin[1] })
180:                         + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
181:                 }
182:                 if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
183:                     p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { omax[2] } else { omin[2] })
184:                         + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
185:                 }
186:                 while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
187:                     let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
188:                     current_node = f.0;
189:                     cmin = f.1;
190:                     cmax = f.2;
191:                 }
192:             }
193:         }
194:     }
195:     None
196: }
197: 
198: fn outside(p: [f32; 3], min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
199:     p[0] < min[0]
200:         || p[0] > max[0]
201:         || p[1] < min[1]
202:         || p[1] > max[1]
203:         || p[2] < min[2]
204:         || p[2] > max[2]
205: }
206: 
207: /// Mirrors the shader's `main()`: slab-test all chunks, sort by entry, march
208: /// nearest first, return the first hit.
209: fn march_scene(
210:     atlas: &[u32],
211:     draws: &[wasm_frontend::application::ports::ChunkDraw],
212:     ro: [f32; 3],
213:     rd: [f32; 3],
214: ) -> Option<Hit> {
215:     let safe = |v: f32| {
216:         if v.abs() < 1e-4 {
217:             1e-4f32.copysign(v)
218:         } else {
219:             v
220:         }
221:     };
222:     // The shader passes safe_rd (not raw rd) into raymarchSVO too.
223:     let rd = [safe(rd[0]), safe(rd[1]), safe(rd[2])];
224:     let inv = [1.0 / rd[0], 1.0 / rd[1], 1.0 / rd[2]];
225: 
226:     let mut hits: Vec<(usize, f32)> = Vec::new();
227:     for (i, d) in draws.iter().enumerate() {
228:         let lro = [
229:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
230:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
231:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
232:         ];
233:         let mut t_entry = f32::MIN;
234:         let mut t_exit = f32::MAX;
235:         for a in 0..3 {
236:             let t1 = (0.0 - lro[a]) * inv[a];
237:             let t2 = (d.world_size - lro[a]) * inv[a];
238:             t_entry = t_entry.max(t1.min(t2));
239:             t_exit = t_exit.min(t1.max(t2));
240:         }
241:         if t_entry < t_exit && t_exit > 0.0 {
242:             hits.push((i, t_entry.max(0.0)));
243:         }
244:     }
245:     hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1));
246: 
247:     for (i, t_min) in hits {
248:         let d = &draws[i];
249:         let lro = [
250:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
251:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
252:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
253:         ];
254:         if let Some((t, bmin, bmax, vt)) =
255:             raymarch_svo(atlas, lro, rd, d.root_index as usize, t_min, d.world_size)
256:         {
257:             return Some(Hit {
258:                 chunk: i,
259:                 t,
260:                 box_min: bmin,
261:                 box_max: bmax,
262:                 voxel_type: vt,
263:             });
264:         }
265:     }
266:     None
267: }
268: 
269: /// Every hit the reference ray-marcher reports must be a genuinely solid
270: /// region of the source octree — otherwise the renderer shows phantom boxes.
271: #[test]
272: fn multi_chunk_raymarch_reports_no_phantom_geometry() {
273:     let seed = 42;
274:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
275:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
276:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
277: 
278:     // 3x3 resident set around spawn, same as the engine with radius 1.
279:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
280:     // Level 0 now has vaulted regions up to 5.4 u, so a steep ray starting
281:     // near the edge of the spawn chunk can travel farther laterally before
282:     // reaching its ceiling. Keep enough loaded world around the sweep to
283:     // test traversal, not an artificial streaming boundary.
284:     for dz in -2..=2 {
285:         for dx in -2..=2 {
286:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
287:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
288:                 (ox, oz),
289:                 0,
290:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
291:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
292:             ));
293:         }
294:     }
295:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
296: 
297:     // Ground truth: rebuild each chunk's SVO exactly like LocalChunkSource.
298:     let svos: Vec<_> = chunks
299:         .iter()
300:         .map(|c| {
301:             let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
302:             let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(c.origin.0, c.origin.1), seed, config);
303:             BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, config.svo_depth(), config.svo_world_size())
304:         })
305:         .collect();
306: 
307:     let ro = [5.0f32, 1.7, 5.0]; // spawn eye position
308:     let mut phantoms = Vec::new();
309:     let mut hit_count = 0usize;
310: 
311:     // Dense direction sweep: 64 yaw steps x 17 pitch steps.
312:     for yi in 0..64 {
313:         for pi in -8..=8i32 {
314:             let yaw = yi as f32 / 64.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
315:             let pitch = pi as f32 / 8.0 * 1.2;
316:             let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
317:             let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
318:             let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
319: 
320:             let Some(hit) = march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd) else {
321:                 continue;
322:             };
323:             hit_count += 1;
324: 
325:             // The leaf box center, in voxel coordinates of the owning chunk.
326:             let scale = config.voxel_scale;
327:             let c = [
328:                 (hit.box_min[0] + hit.box_max[0]) * 0.5,
329:                 (hit.box_min[1] + hit.box_max[1]) * 0.5,
330:                 (hit.box_min[2] + hit.box_max[2]) * 0.5,
331:             ];
332:             let (vx, vy, vz) = (
333:                 (c[0] / scale) as u32,
334:                 (c[1] / scale) as u32,
335:                 (c[2] / scale) as u32,
336:             );
337:             let truth = svos[hit.chunk].get(vx, vy, vz);
338:             let solid = truth.map(|(vt, _, _, _)| vt != 0).unwrap_or(false);
339:             if !solid {
340:                 phantoms.push((yaw, pitch, hit));
341:             }
342:         }
343:     }
344: 
345:     assert!(
346:         hit_count > 200,
347:         "sanity: the sweep must actually hit walls, got {hit_count}"
348:     );
349:     assert!(
350:         phantoms.is_empty(),
351:         "{} phantom hits out of {}; first 5: {:#?}",
352:         phantoms.len(),
353:         hit_count,
354:         &phantoms[..phantoms.len().min(5)]
355:     );
356: }
357: 
358: /// The world is a closed slab (floor everywhere at y=0, ceiling at the top),
359: /// so every ray with meaningful up/down pitch MUST hit something. A miss is
360: /// a traversal crack — the "black bars in walls" artifact caused by popping
361: /// only one stack level when a skip crosses several octree levels at once.
362: #[test]
363: fn pitched_rays_never_escape_through_cracks() {
364:     let seed = 42;
365:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
366:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
367: 
368:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
369:     for dz in -1..=1 {
370:         for dx in -1..=1 {
371:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
372:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
373:                 (ox, oz),
374:                 0,
375:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
376:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
377:             ));
378:         }
379:     }
380:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
381: 
382:     let mut misses = 0usize;
383:     let mut total = 0usize;
384:     for px in 0..8 {
385:         for pz in 0..8 {
386:             let ro = [1.0137 + px as f32 * 1.11, 1.7, 0.9713 + pz as f32 * 1.19];
387:             for yi in 0..128 {
388:                 for pi in [-40i32, -25, 25, 40] {
389:                     let yaw = (yi as f32 + 0.173) / 128.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
390:                     let pitch = pi as f32 / 60.0 * 1.2;
391:                     let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
392:                     let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
393:                     let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
394:                     total += 1;
395:                     if march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd).is_none() {
396:                         misses += 1;
397:                     }
398:                 }
399:             }
400:         }
401:     }
402:     assert_eq!(
403:         misses, 0,
404:         "{misses} of {total} pitched rays escaped through cracks"
405:     );
406: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/Cargo.toml
````toml
 1: # wasm_frontend — the browser front end of the voxel engine.
 2: #
 3: # Clean Architecture placement:
 4: #   application/  Use-case layer for the interactive client (player physics,
 5: #                 chunk streaming policy, frame orchestration). Pure Rust,
 6: #                 unit-tested natively. Defines the ports (RendererPort,
 7: #                 ChunkSourcePort) that outer layers implement.
 8: #   adapters/     Interface adapters: input mapping, SVO atlas assembly, and
 9: #                 the local chunk source that drives the `vackrooms` core
10: #                 use cases (generation -> SVO -> GPU serialization).
11: #   drivers/      Frameworks & Drivers: WebGL2 renderer, browser event/rAF
12: #                 plumbing, HUD. Only this layer touches web-sys, and it is
13: #                 compiled exclusively for wasm32.
14: [package]
15: name = "wasm_frontend"
16: version = "0.1.0"
17: edition = "2024"
18: 
19: [lib]
20: crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
21: 
22: [dependencies]
23: # Inner-ring engine core: entities (VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree),
24: # use cases (GenerateChunk, BuildOctree, lighting) and the GPU serializer.
25: vackrooms = { path = ".." }
26: 
27: # Browser bindings are wasm-only so `cargo test` on the host runs the pure
28: # application/adapters layers without pulling in web-sys.
29: [target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
30: wasm-bindgen = "0.2"
31: js-sys = "0.3"
32: console_error_panic_hook = "0.1"
33: web-sys = { version = "0.3", features = [
34:     "Window",
35:     "Location",
36:     "Document",
37:     "Element",
38:     "HtmlElement",
39:     "HtmlCanvasElement",
40:     "CssStyleDeclaration",
41:     "Event",
42:     "EventTarget",
43:     "KeyboardEvent",
44:     "MouseEvent",
45:     "TouchEvent",
46:     "TouchList",
47:     "Touch",
48:     "Navigator",
49:     "Performance",
50:     "CanvasRenderingContext2d",
51:     "ImageData",
52:     "WebGl2RenderingContext",
53:     "WebGlProgram",
54:     "WebGlQuery",
55:     "WebGlShader",
56:     "WebGlTexture",
57:     "WebGlBuffer",
58:     "WebGlVertexArrayObject",
59:     "WebGlUniformLocation",
60:     "WebGlFramebuffer",
61:     "Worker",
62:     "WorkerOptions",
63:     "WorkerType",
64:     "MessageEvent",
65:     "console",
66: ] }
````

  1: /// Represents a dense 3D grid of voxels.
  2: /// This is the foundation for our "smaller voxels" requirement.
  3: pub struct VoxelGrid {
  4:     width: usize,
  5:     height: usize,
  6:     depth: usize,
  7:     data: Vec<u8>,
  8:     /// Scalar light level 0-15 (the max of the RGB channels), kept for
  9:     /// presenters and bakes that only need brightness.
 10:     light_data: Vec<u8>,
 11:     /// Colored flood-fill light, 0-15 per channel.
 12:     light_rgb: Vec<[u8; 3]>,
 13:     pub runtime_lights: Vec<crate::domain::entities::architecture::RuntimeLight>,
 14:     /// Semantic threshold planes emitted by the same architectural pass as
 15:     /// geometry. The application consumes them to advance deterministic
 16:     /// anomaly epochs; render/collision never invent a separate reality.
 17:     pub traversal_gates: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGate>,
 18:     /// Real floor openings that relocate the player when entered.
 19:     pub pit_hazards: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::PitHazard>,
 20:     face_occlusion: Vec<u8>,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: pub const VOXEL_AIR: u8 = 0;
 24: pub const VOXEL_WALL: u8 = 1;
 25: pub const VOXEL_FLOOR: u8 = 2;
 26: pub const VOXEL_CEILING: u8 = 3;
 27: pub const VOXEL_LIGHT: u8 = 4;
 28: pub const VOXEL_RED_WALL: u8 = 5;
 29: /// Walkable ground cover (grassland level). Visual-only, like FLOOR.
 30: pub const VOXEL_GRASS: u8 = 6;
 31: /// Walkable shallow water (grassland lakes). Visual-only, like FLOOR.
 32: pub const VOXEL_WATER: u8 = 7;
 33: /// Tree trunk (grassland). Solid: blocks the player like WALL.
 34: pub const VOXEL_TREE: u8 = 8;
 35: pub const VOXEL_RED_LIGHT: u8 = 9;
 36: /// Pale bone-tinted arch-room wall. Solid like WALL.
 37: pub const VOXEL_PALE_WALL: u8 = 10;
 38: /// Rough, damaged blackout-expanse wall. Solid like WALL.
 39: pub const VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL: u8 = 11;
 40: /// Shallow, dry, desaturated pillar-expanse carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 41: pub const VOXEL_DRY_CARPET: u8 = 12;
 42: /// Deep, wet arch-room carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 43: pub const VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET: u8 = 13;
 44: /// Thick, sticky, discolored red-room carpet. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 45: pub const VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET: u8 = 14;
 46: /// Recessed basin holding dark ankle-deep fluid. Walkable, like FLOOR.
 47: pub const VOXEL_FLUID: u8 = 15;
 48: /// Tiny cool emergency glimmer fixture (blackout recovery skeleton).
 49: /// Emissive like LIGHT, far dimmer and colder.
 50: pub const VOXEL_GLIMMER: u8 = 16;
 51: 
 52: /// Number of voxel material ids (the palette table length).
 53: pub const VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT: usize = 17;
 54: 
 55: /// The one authoritative material palette, `0xRRGGBB` per voxel id. Every
 56: /// consumer — octree bake, greedy-mesh debug colors, CPU splatter, and the
 57: /// generated GLSL tables — derives from this table so a new material can
 58: /// never render differently across paths.
 59: pub const MATERIAL_COLORS: [u32; VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT] = [
 60:     0x000000, // 0 air (never drawn)
 61:     0xDDCC66, // 1 yellow wallpaper wall
 62:     0x998811, // 2 office carpet floor
 63:     0xCCCCCC, // 3 dropped ceiling
 64:     0xFFF8D6, // 4 fluorescent panel
 65:     0x880000, // 5 crimson / peeled red wall
 66:     0x4F9A3D, // 6 grass
 67:     0x3A6FB8, // 7 water
 68:     0x6B4A2F, // 8 tree / dark pillar
 69:     0xFF4433, // 9 red light
 70:     0xD8D2C0, // 10 pale arch wall
 71:     0x8A7F5C, // 11 rough damaged wall
 72:     0xC2B76B, // 12 dry shallow carpet
 73:     0x6B5E22, // 13 deep wet carpet
 74:     0x7A4A26, // 14 sticky red-room carpet
 75:     0x2E2A22, // 15 dark pooled fluid
 76:     0x9FC4E8, // 16 cool emergency glimmer
 77: ];
 78: 
 79: /// Palette lookup as normalized linear-ish RGB for shader tables.
 80: pub fn material_color_f32(voxel: u8) -> [f32; 3] {
 81:     let c = MATERIAL_COLORS
 82:         .get(voxel as usize)
 83:         .copied()
 84:         .unwrap_or(0x000000);
 85:     [
 86:         ((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
 87:         ((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
 88:         (c & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
 89:     ]
 90: }
 91: 
 92: /// Materials that block the player and produce collision boxes. Everything
 93: /// else is walkable or decorative.
 94: pub const SOLID_MATERIALS: [u8; 5] = [
 95:     VOXEL_WALL,
 96:     VOXEL_TREE,
 97:     VOXEL_RED_WALL,
 98:     VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
 99:     VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
100: ];
101: 
102: /// Materials that emit light in the baked flood fill and render emissive.
103: pub const EMISSIVE_MATERIALS: [u8; 3] = [VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_GLIMMER];
104: 
105: impl VoxelGrid {
106:     pub fn new(width: usize, height: usize, depth: usize) -> Self {
107:         let size = width * height * depth;
108:         Self {
109:             width,
110:             height,
111:             depth,
112:             data: vec![VOXEL_AIR; size],
113:             light_data: vec![0; size],
114:             light_rgb: vec![[0; 3]; size],
115:             runtime_lights: Vec::new(),
116:             traversal_gates: Vec::new(),
117:             pit_hazards: Vec::new(),
118:             face_occlusion: vec![0; size],
119:         }
120:     }
121: 
122:     pub fn width(&self) -> usize {
123:         self.width
124:     }
125:     pub fn height(&self) -> usize {
126:         self.height
127:     }
128:     pub fn depth(&self) -> usize {
129:         self.depth
130:     }
131: 
132:     fn index(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> Option<usize> {
133:         if x < self.width && y < self.height && z < self.depth {
134:             Some(y * (self.width * self.depth) + z * self.width + x)
135:         } else {
136:             None
137:         }
138:     }
139: 
140:     pub fn set(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, voxel_type: u8) {
141:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
142:             self.data[idx] = voxel_type;
143:         }
144:     }
145: 
146:     pub fn get(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
147:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
148:             self.data[idx]
149:         } else {
150:             VOXEL_AIR
151:         }
152:     }
153: 
154:     /// Sets a neutral (white) light level: all three channels get `level`.
155:     pub fn set_light(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, level: u8) {
156:         self.set_light_rgb(x, y, z, [level; 3]);
157:     }
158: 
159:     pub fn get_light(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
160:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
161:             self.light_data[idx]
162:         } else {
163:             0
164:         }
165:     }
166: 
167:     /// Sets colored light (0-15 per channel); the scalar level becomes the
168:     /// max of the channels.
169:     pub fn set_light_rgb(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, rgb: [u8; 3]) {
170:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
171:             self.light_rgb[idx] = rgb;
172:             self.light_data[idx] = rgb[0].max(rgb[1]).max(rgb[2]);
173:         }
174:     }
175: 
176:     pub fn get_light_rgb(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> [u8; 3] {
177:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
178:             self.light_rgb[idx]
179:         } else {
180:             [0; 3]
181:         }
182:     }
183: 
184:     pub fn set_face_occlusion(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize, mask: u8) {
185:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
186:             self.face_occlusion[idx] = mask;
187:         }
188:     }
189: 
190:     pub fn get_face_occlusion(&self, x: usize, y: usize, z: usize) -> u8 {
191:         if let Some(idx) = self.index(x, y, z) {
192:             self.face_occlusion[idx]
193:         } else {
194:             0
195:         }
196:     }
197: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/local_chunk_source.rs
````rust
  1: //! In-wasm chunk source: implements the application's [`ChunkSourcePort`] by
  2: //! driving the core engine use cases directly. There is no server round-trip;
  3: //! the entire pipeline — procedural generation, BFS lighting, SVO build, GPU
  4: //! serialization, collision extraction — runs inside the wasm module.
  5: //!
  6: //! Pipeline per chunk:
  7: //!   GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase  (VoxelGrid, lighting included)
  8: //!     -> BuildOctreeUseCase           (SparseVoxelOctree)
  9: //!     -> OctreeGpuSerializer          (row-padded RGBA32UI texel stream)
 10: //!     -> collision walk               (solid leaves -> world-space AABBs)
 11: 
 12: use vackrooms::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
 13: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
 15: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
 16: use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
 17: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 18: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 19: use vackrooms::use_cases::ports::{NULL_TELEMETRY, NoiseProvider, TelemetryPort};
 20: 
 21: use crate::adapters::surface_mesh::build_surface_mesh;
 22: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 23: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkPayload, ChunkSourcePort};
 24: 
 25: /// Voxel types that block the player. FLOOR/CEILING/LIGHT/GRASS/WATER and
 26: /// the carpet/fluid classes are visual-only: including them would make the
 27: /// player collide with the floor they stand on. Shared with the core so a
 28: /// new wall class can never render solid but collide hollow.
 29: const SOLID_TYPES: [u8; 5] = vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::SOLID_MATERIALS;
 30: 
 31: pub struct LocalChunkSource<N: NoiseProvider> {
 32:     noise: N,
 33:     telemetry: &'static dyn TelemetryPort,
 34:     seed: u32,
 35:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl<N: NoiseProvider> LocalChunkSource<N> {
 39:     pub fn new(noise: N, seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> Self {
 40:         Self {
 41:             noise,
 42:             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
 43:             seed,
 44:             config,
 45:         }
 46:     }
 47: 
 48:     pub fn with_telemetry(
 49:         noise: N,
 50:         seed: u32,
 51:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 52:         telemetry: &'static dyn TelemetryPort,
 53:     ) -> Self {
 54:         Self {
 55:             noise,
 56:             telemetry,
 57:             seed,
 58:             config,
 59:         }
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     fn generate_payload(
 63:         &self,
 64:         origin_x: f32,
 65:         origin_z: f32,
 66:         level: u32,
 67:         lod: u8,
 68:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 69:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
 70:         let config = self.config.with_level(level).at_lod(lod);
 71:         let generator =
 72:             GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&self.noise, self.telemetry);
 73: 
 74:         // Generate one extra voxel around the X/Z perimeter, then crop the
 75:         // authoritative interior for SVO/collision. The greedy mesher reads
 76:         // the halo while deciding boundary faces, so it never invents a face
 77:         // merely because the adjacent streamed chunk has not uploaded yet.
 78:         let halo_config = GeneratorConfig {
 79:             chunk_size: config.chunk_size + config.voxel_scale * 2.0,
 80:             ..config
 81:         };
 82:         let halo_grid = generator.execute_with_reality(
 83:             Position::new(origin_x - config.voxel_scale, origin_z - config.voxel_scale),
 84:             self.seed,
 85:             halo_config,
 86:             reality,
 87:         );
 88:         let grid = crop_lateral_halo(&halo_grid, 1);
 89:         let surface = build_surface_mesh(&halo_grid, config.voxel_scale, lod, 1);
 90: 
 91:         let svo =
 92:             BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, config.svo_depth(), config.svo_world_size());
 93: 
 94:         let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 95:         let collision = extract_collision_boxes(&svo, origin_x, origin_z, config.voxel_scale);
 96: 
 97:         ChunkPayload {
 98:             root: svo.root as u32,
 99:             nodes: gpu.texel_data,
100:             world_size: config.svo_world_size(),
101:             surface,
102:             collision,
103:             traversal_gates: halo_grid.traversal_gates.clone(),
104:             pit_hazards: halo_grid.pit_hazards.clone(),
105:         }
106:     }
107: }
108: 
109: impl<N: NoiseProvider> ChunkSourcePort for LocalChunkSource<N> {
110:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
111:         self.generate_payload(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, &RealitySnapshot::default())
112:     }
113: 
114:     fn load_with_reality(
115:         &self,
116:         origin_x: f32,
117:         origin_z: f32,
118:         level: u32,
119:         lod: u8,
120:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
121:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
122:         self.generate_payload(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
123:     }
124: }
125: 
126: /// Copies the actual chunk interior out of a generated X/Z halo while
127: /// retaining voxel type, colored baked lighting, and directional AO.
128: fn crop_lateral_halo(halo: &VoxelGrid, padding: usize) -> VoxelGrid {
129:     assert!(halo.width() > padding * 2 && halo.depth() > padding * 2);
130:     let mut inner = VoxelGrid::new(
131:         halo.width() - padding * 2,
132:         halo.height(),
133:         halo.depth() - padding * 2,
134:     );
135:     for z in 0..inner.depth() {
136:         for y in 0..inner.height() {
137:             for x in 0..inner.width() {
138:                 let hx = x + padding;
139:                 let hz = z + padding;
140:                 inner.set(x, y, z, halo.get(hx, y, hz));
141:                 inner.set_light_rgb(x, y, z, halo.get_light_rgb(hx, y, hz));
142:                 inner.set_face_occlusion(x, y, z, halo.get_face_occlusion(hx, y, hz));
143:             }
144:         }
145:     }
146:     inner
147: }
148: 
149: /// Walks the SVO and emits one world-space AABB per solid leaf region.
150: /// Uniform subtrees collapsed by the SVO become single large boxes for free,
151: /// which keeps the collision set small.
152: pub fn extract_collision_boxes(
153:     svo: &SparseVoxelOctree,
154:     origin_x: f32,
155:     origin_z: f32,
156:     voxel_scale: f32,
157: ) -> Vec<Aabb> {
158:     let mut boxes = Vec::new();
159:     let size = 1u32 << svo.depth;
160:     walk(
161:         svo,
162:         svo.root,
163:         0,
164:         0,
165:         0,
166:         size,
167:         origin_x,
168:         origin_z,
169:         voxel_scale,
170:         &mut boxes,
171:     );
172:     boxes
173: }
174: 
175: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
176: fn walk(
177:     svo: &SparseVoxelOctree,
178:     node_idx: usize,
179:     x: u32,
180:     y: u32,
181:     z: u32,
182:     size: u32,
183:     origin_x: f32,
184:     origin_z: f32,
185:     voxel_scale: f32,
186:     out: &mut Vec<Aabb>,
187: ) {
188:     match svo.nodes[node_idx] {
189:         SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
190:             if SOLID_TYPES.contains(&voxel_type) {
191:                 let min = [
192:                     origin_x + x as f32 * voxel_scale,
193:                     y as f32 * voxel_scale,
194:                     origin_z + z as f32 * voxel_scale,
195:                 ];
196:                 let extent = size as f32 * voxel_scale;
197:                 out.push(Aabb::new(
198:                     min,
199:                     [min[0] + extent, min[1] + extent, min[2] + extent],
200:                 ));
201:             }
202:         }
203:         SvoNode::Internal {
204:             child_base_index,
205:             child_mask,
206:         } => {
207:             let half = size / 2;
208:             for child in 0..8u32 {
209:                 if child_mask & (1 << child) != 0 {
210:                     walk(
211:                         svo,
212:                         child_base_index as usize + child as usize,
213:                         x + (child & 1) * half,
214:                         y + ((child >> 1) & 1) * half,
215:                         z + ((child >> 2) & 1) * half,
216:                         half,
217:                         origin_x,
218:                         origin_z,
219:                         voxel_scale,
220:                         out,
221:                     );
222:                 }
223:             }
224:         }
225:     }
226: }
227: 
228: #[cfg(test)]
229: mod tests {

231:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid};
232:     use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
233: 
234:     #[test]
235:     fn wall_leaf_becomes_world_space_box_and_floor_does_not() {
236:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
237:         grid.set(1, 0, 2, VOXEL_WALL);
238:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_FLOOR);
239:         let svo = BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, 2, 2.0);
240: 
241:         let boxes = extract_collision_boxes(&svo, 10.0, 20.0, 0.5);
242:         assert_eq!(boxes.len(), 1);
243:         let b = &boxes[0];
244:         assert_eq!(b.min, [10.5, 0.0, 21.0]);
245:         assert_eq!(b.max, [11.0, 0.5, 21.5]);
246:     }
247:

250:         let source =

252:         let payload = source.load(10.0, 10.0, 0, 0);
253:         // Row padding: node stream is a whole number of 1024-texel rows.
254:         assert_eq!(payload.nodes.len() % (1024 * 4), 0);
255:         assert!(payload.world_size > 0.0);
256:         assert!(
257:             !payload.collision.is_empty(),

262:     #[test]

266:         let fine = source.load(10.0, 10.0, 0, 0);

268:         assert_eq!(

277:         );
278:         assert!(
279:             !coarse.collision.is_empty(),

281:         );
282:     }

## File: ARCHITECTURE.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms — Architecture
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine built on **Clean Architecture**, targeting
  4: low-spec hardware. The whole engine — procedural generation, lighting, sparse
  5: voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, player physics, and
  6: rendering — compiles to a single WebAssembly module. The browser
  7: runs it; a zero-dependency native HTTP server merely serves the files (or, on
  8: GitHub Pages, static files alone — the wasm engine generates chunks entirely
  9: client-side and needs no server).
 10: 
 11: ## Rendering family
 12: 
 13: `RendererPort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`) has four
 14: implementations, selected at runtime by `create_renderer`
 15: (`wasm_frontend/src/drivers/browser.rs`) from the `?renderer=` query param:
 16: 
 17: | `?renderer=` | Driver | Approach |
 18: |---|---|---|
 19: | *(default)* | `surface_webgl::SurfaceRenderer` | Indexed greedy meshes, WebGL2 fixed-function depth. The SVO is retained per chunk for collision/debug only — no fragment shader walks it. |
 20: | `splat` | `splat_webgl::SplatRenderer` | Instanced face-splat "microvoxel" path: one GPU instance per visible surface rectangle, lit once in the vertex shader; the retained mesh is drawn only into the shadow map. |
 21: | `raymarch` | `webgl::WebGl2Renderer` | The hybrid SVO raymarcher described below — a per-fragment octree walk. |
 22: | `cpu` | `cpu_canvas::CpuCanvasRenderer` | Software rasterizer (`adapters::cpu_splatter`) blitted via `ImageData`; no WebGL context at all. |
 23: 
 24: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` fall back (to CPU, or to surfaces)
 25: if WebGL2 or the requested backend fails to initialize.
 26: 
 27: Renderer code is organized by lifetime and responsibility rather than by one
 28: backend-sized class:
 29: 
 30: | Module | Responsibility |
 31: |---|---|
 32: | `drivers/surface_webgl/{mod,resources,draw}.rs` | surface composition, chunk GPU resources, staged frame pipeline |
 33: | `drivers/splat_webgl/{mod,resources,draw}.rs` | splat composition, instance/shadow resources, staged frame pipeline |
 34: | `drivers/webgl/{mod,atlas,draw}.rs` | raymarch composition, SVO texture lifecycle, fullscreen submission |
 35: | `adapters/cpu_splatter/` | atlas decode, camera, cone light, ray queries, shading, raster traversal, tests |
 36: | `drivers/gl/` | context/program setup, matrices, light selection, shadow targets, timers, visibility |
 37: | `drivers/shaders/` | one literate Rust module per GLSL program plus shared chunks |
 38: 
 39: Optional shortcuts are plain data in `application::render_settings::RenderToggles`.
 40: Each driver snapshots that switchboard once per frame; inner algorithms never
 41: read browser globals. The same switches are available live in Settings →
 42: Optimize and as shareable `?rt_<name>=0|1` query parameters.
 43: 
 44: Of the three classical voxel pipeline families (mesh/rasterized,
 45: SVO ray casting, hybrid), the `raymarch` backend implements a
 46: **hybrid SVO raymarcher**:
 47: 
 48: 1. **Chunk-level coarse pass** — each resident chunk's AABB is slab-tested
 49:    per fragment and the hits are insertion-sorted by entry distance, so rays
 50:    march the nearest chunk first and exit on the first solid hit.
 51: 2. **Fragment SVO traversal** — stack-based descent through the octree with
 52:    **empty-space skipping**: an air leaf or masked-out octant is exited in a
 53:    single step via its AABB exit plane, never voxel-by-voxel.
 54: 3. **Shading** — packed 24-bit leaf color × BFS-propagated light level,
 55:    face normal from the hit box, exponential distance fog.
 56: 
 57: Low-spec strategy: no depth buffer, no MSAA, nearest-filtered integer
 58: textures, and an **adaptive internal-resolution governor** (0.5×–1.0× backing
 59: store, hysteresis + cooldown) instead of temporal checkerboarding — simpler,
 60: and it degrades smoothly on weak GPUs.
 61: 
 62: ## The dependency rule
 63: 
 64: Source dependencies point inward only. No inner layer names a browser, GPU,
 65: socket, or clock.
 66: 
 67: ```
 68: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 69: │ FRAMEWORKS & DRIVERS                                               │
 70: │   wasm_frontend/drivers   WebGL2, DOM events, rAF, HUD, console    │
 71: │   src/main.rs             native HTTP server (std::net only)      │
 72: │   src/frameworks_drivers  SimpleNoiseProvider, StdTelemetry        │
 73: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
 74: │  │ INTERFACE ADAPTERS                                           │  │
 75: │  │   src/adapters            OctreeGpuSerializer, VoxelMapper,  │  │
 76: │  │                           JsonPresenter                      │  │
 77: │  │   src/interface_adapters  WebRendererAdapter (presenters)    │  │
 78: │  │   wasm_frontend/adapters  InputCollector, LocalChunkSource   │  │
 79: │  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
 80: │  │  │ USE CASES (application business rules)                 │  │  │
 81: │  │  │   src/use_cases           GenerateChunk + ports        │  │  │
 82: │  │  │   src/domain/use_cases    BuildOctree, lighting, maze  │  │  │
 83: │  │  │   wasm_frontend/application  Engine (frame loop),      │  │  │
 84: │  │  │      Player, CollisionWorld, StreamingPolicy, atlas    │  │  │
 85: │  │  │      + ports (RendererPort, ChunkSourcePort)           │  │  │
 86: │  │  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │  │
 87: │  │  │  │ ENTITIES (enterprise business rules)             │  │  │  │
 88: │  │  │  │   VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree, Position, Grid   │  │  │  │
 89: │  │  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │  │
 90: │  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
 91: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 92: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: ### Crates
 96: 
 97: | Crate | Role | Targets |
 98: |---|---|---|
 99: | `vackrooms` (root) | Entities + use cases + adapters; native dev-server binary | native **and** wasm32 |
100: | `wasm_frontend` | Browser client: application/adapters (portable) + drivers (wasm-only) | wasm32 (pure layers test natively) |
101: | `wasm_raycaster` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment | kept for reference |
102: 
103: The split inside `wasm_frontend` is enforced mechanically: `web-sys`,
104: `js-sys` and `wasm-bindgen` are `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")']`
105: dependencies, and `drivers/` is `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`. A native
106: `cargo test` therefore cannot even *see* browser types — the compiler is the
107: architecture cop.
108: 
109: ### Ports (dependency inversion boundaries)
110: 
111: | Port | Defined in (inner) | Implemented by (outer) |
112: |---|---|---|
113: | `NoiseProvider` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `SimpleNoiseProvider` |
114: | `TelemetryPort` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `StdTelemetry` (native stdout), `ConsoleTelemetry` (browser console), `NullTelemetry` (tests) |
115: | `RendererPort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `SurfaceRenderer` (default), `SplatRenderer`, `WebGl2Renderer` (raymarch), `CpuCanvasRenderer`, recording fakes (tests) |
116: | `ChunkSourcePort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `LocalChunkSource` (synchronous, in-wasm generation), `WorkerChunkSource` (pooled Web Worker generation, default); an HTTP-fetching implementation would slot in without touching the engine |
117: 
118: ## Data flow: from noise to pixel
119: 
120: The SVO atlas path below feeds the `raymarch` backend directly; the default
121: `SurfaceRenderer` and `SplatRenderer` consume the same lit `VoxelGrid` but
122: greedy-mesh or face-splat it instead of walking the octree per fragment (the
123: SVO they receive is used for collision only).
124: 
125: ```
126: SimpleNoiseProvider (driver)
127:       │ NoiseProvider port
128:       ▼
129: GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase ──► VoxelGrid (dense u8 grid + light grid)
130:       │                                   │
131:       │                          calculate_voxel_lighting (BFS flood fill)
132:       ▼                                   ▼
133: BuildOctreeUseCase ──────────────► SparseVoxelOctree
134:       │                              (arena Vec<SvoNode>, uniform-collapsed)
135:       ▼
136: OctreeGpuSerializer ─────────────► RGBA32UI texel stream, rows of 1024,
137:       │                              row-padded per chunk
138:       ▼
139: application::atlas::build_atlas ─► merged atlas + per-chunk rebased roots
140:       │ RendererPort port
141:       ▼
142: WebGl2Renderer ──────────────────► RGBA32UI texture + uniform chunk table
143:       ▼
144: fragment shader (drivers/shaders/raymarch.rs) — fullscreen quad, sorted chunk AABBs,
145: stack-based SVO march, empty-space skipping ──► pixels
146: ```
147: 
148: Collision geometry is derived **from the same SVO** (solid WALL/RED_WALL
149: leaves → world-space AABBs in `local_chunk_source::extract_collision_boxes`),
150: so physics and visuals can never drift apart. Uniform subtrees collapsed by
151: the SVO become single large collision boxes for free.
152: 
153: ### SVO node texel encoding (RGBA32UI, one node per texel)
154: 
155: | Channel | Internal node (`R == 0`) | Leaf node (`R == 1`) |
156: |---|---|---|
157: | R | 0 | 1 |
158: | G | `child_base_index` (children contiguous at +0..+7) | `voxel_type` |
159: | B | `child_mask` (bit *i* set = child *i* non-empty) | 24-bit `0xRRGGBB` color |
160: | A | 0 | light level 0–15 |
161: 
162: The same layout is documented at its source of truth,
163: `src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`, and decoded in
164: `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/raymarch.rs` (`decodeNode`).
165: 
166: ## Level 0: architecture first
167: 
168: Level 0 no longer decorates a random maze — it *plans* buildings and then
169: voxelizes them (`use_cases/region_plan.rs` + `use_cases/backrooms_level.rs`):
170: 
171: 1. **Region plans.** The world tiles into fixed 80 u regions. A pure function
172:    of `(seed, region)` derives 1–3 `ArchitectGenome`s (circulation style,
173:    structural system, proportions, threshold/ceiling/lighting languages,
174:    renovation history), routes one dominant 4.8–7.2 u primary spine between
175:    shared edge portals (so it chains across regions forever), then adds at
176:    most two 3.6–5.0 u interior branches. It attaches incomplete, 12–24 u
177:    `AssemblyInstance` masses beside that circulation rather than tiling the
178:    region with rooms. Thresholds are selected per assembly: narrow lintelled
179:    doors are rare; most fronts use a broad or unframed portal.
180: 2. **Corruption.** A final pass makes the sane plan Backrooms: suites repeat
181:    with misaligned copies, one assembly becomes an unlit
182:    `AbandonedExpansion` shell, renovations overlay contradictory column
183:    grids.
184: 3. **Voxelization.** `BackroomsLevel` samples the plan per voxel column with
185:    priority *corridor → assembly → fabric*: corridors carve open under
186:    3.4–4.2 u (primary) or 3.0–3.6 u (secondary) ceilings; assemblies retain
187:    long perimeter runs and sparse partitions; everything between is a sparse
188:    18 u wall fabric that dissolves into open space. A broad ceiling field
189:    holds the visual baseline at 3.2–3.6 u, with 3.8–4.4 u expanses, 4.5–5.4 u
190:    vaults, and rare 2.5–2.8 u compression zones. This keeps cheap office
191:    finishes at an implausible scale instead of producing a low office maze.
192: 
193: All plan geometry snaps to a 0.4 u lattice (one coarse voxel) so every LOD
194: of a chunk voxelizes the same architecture. Debug hook:
195: `cargo run --example dump_plan` prints region plans as ASCII;
196: `debug_region_ascii` renders any plan.
197: 
198: ### Infinite generation and anomalies
199: 
200: The generation code is organized by the language of Level 0, rather than by
201: delivery mechanism:
202: 
203: ```
204: InfiniteRegionWindow ──► RegionPlan(s) ──► architectural ColumnPlan
205:                                                 │
206: anomalies/{planning,geometry} ──────────────────┤
207: red_rooms/{planning,geometry,recursive_level} ──┘
208:                                                 │
209:                                       ColumnField (1-column halo)
210:                                                 │
211:                                       voxelize_columns ──► VoxelGrid
212: ```
213: 
214: - `domain/entities/anomaly/` contains only domain language: rectilinear
215:   geometry, immutable anomaly instances, traversal semantics, and canonical
216:   reality snapshots. The public `anomaly` namespace remains stable.
217: - `use_cases/anomalies/` plans and samples macro anomaly families.
218:   `use_cases/red_rooms/` owns the assembly-derived encounter and its recursive
219:   Level 0 address. The old `anomaly_plan` module is only a compatibility
220:   facade.
221: - `InfiniteRegionWindow` is the finite query cache for an infinite region
222:   lattice. A missing plan is an error instead of silently falling back to an
223:   unrelated region.
224: - A committed Red Room derives its branch seed and region-aligned translation
225:   with integer hashes over the full 64-bit anomaly id. Planning and sampling
226:   use that same address, so worker order, chunk boundaries, and floating-point
227:   id precision cannot select different worlds.
228: - `ColumnField` and `voxelize_columns` are resolution-dependent output stages.
229:   World planning never reads the requested output extent; generating one 20 u
230:   area or four 10 u areas produces the same voxels at matching coordinates.
231: 
232: Reality is part of chunk identity. Entering a Red Room changes the active
233: infinite Level 0 address, so all resident chunks are atomically scheduled for
234: replacement; partially repainting only the vestibule would splice two worlds
235: at a streaming boundary.
236: 
237: ## Chunk streaming
238: 
239: Chunk generation runs on a pool of Web Workers (`WorkerChunkSource`,
240: `static/worker.js` — each a second instance of the same wasm module), sized
241: to `hardware_concurrency - 1` (clamped 1–4), so crossing a streaming
242: boundary never stalls the frame loop; `?workers=0` forces the older
243: synchronous in-thread `LocalChunkSource`, which is also the automatic
244: fallback if the worker pool fails to spin up. Either way, the resident set
245: itself is **time-sliced** and **progressive**: `StreamingPolicy` produces the
246: desired resident set (nearest-first) each frame, and the `Engine` spends a
247: per-tick cost budget on it in two phases:
248: 
249: 1. **Availability** — every missing chunk first loads at a *coarse LOD*
250:    (voxels 2× the size, ~1/8 the generation/lighting/SVO cost, ~1 budget
251:    unit), so the whole footprint renders after roughly one tick instead of
252:    trickling in chunk by chunk.
253: 2. **Refinement** — leftover budget reloads the nearest coarse chunk *within
254:    `fine_distance`* at full resolution, replacing it in place (same atlas
255:    slot, partial row upload). Chunks beyond `fine_distance` stay coarse: at
256:    that range a coarse voxel projects to about the same pixels as a fine one
257:    — a screen-space-error LOD. Refinement is monotonic while resident, so
258:    the LOD choice never flaps.
259: 
260: Every LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`GeneratorConfig::at_lod`
261: halves the SVO depth as it doubles `voxel_scale`), and cell borders/door
262: positions derive from world space, so a coarse chunk is a faithful low-res
263: proxy of its fine version and payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
264: The atlas texture and collision world are rebuilt only on a resident-set
265: change — steady-state frames upload nothing (asserted by
266: `steady_state_does_not_reupload_atlas`).
267: 
268: Profiles (selected by URL, `?spec=high`):
269: 
270: | | chunk size | radius | voxels (fine/coarse) | SVO depth | fine ring |
271: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
272: | low (default) | 10 u | 1 (3×3) | 0.2 / 0.4 u | 6 / 5 | 15 u (all 9) |
273: | high | 20 u | 2 (5×5) | 0.1 / 0.2 u | 8 / 7 | 25 u (~9 of 25) |
274: 
275: The shader's chunk table is fixed at 25 entries — exactly the 5×5 high-spec
276: worst case (`application::atlas::MAX_CHUNKS`).
277: 
278: ## Player simulation
279: 
280: `application::player` ports the original client's tuning 1:1: exponential
281: friction (8 s⁻¹), acceleration 4 u/s² (terminal 0.5 u/s), mouse sensitivity
282: 0.002 rad/px, pitch clamped short of ±90°. Collision is **axis-separated
283: sliding**: X and Z are moved and tested independently against the
284: `CollisionWorld`, so hitting a wall diagonally slides along it. `dt` is
285: clamped to 100 ms so a background-tab hitch cannot teleport the player
286: through a wall.
287: 
288: ## Testing strategy
289: 
290: Ports make the interesting logic natively testable — no browser, no GPU:
291: 
292: - `cargo test --workspace` runs 116 tests: entities, generation, lighting,
293:   octree build/serialize, plus the front end's player physics, sliding
294:   collision, streaming policy/eviction, atlas rebasing, input mapping, and
295:   the resolution governor.
296: - Renderer/chunk-source **test doubles** verify the engine's contract with
297:   its ports (upload counts, draw-table sizes) rather than pixels.
298: - The drivers layer is deliberately thin: translation only, no decisions.
299: 
300: ## Native dev server
301: 
302: `src/main.rs` is a zero-dependency HTTP server used for local development:
303: static files with correct MIME types (`application/wasm` is mandatory for
304: streaming instantiation), plus the legacy JSON/binary chunk endpoints
305: (`/maze`, `/octree`) that the preserved Three.js client (`/legacy`) still
306: consumes. The wasm client needs no data endpoints at all.
307: 
308: ## Roadmap (documented non-goals of this iteration)
309: 
310: - Temporal reprojection / checkerboarding to complement adaptive resolution.
311: - Per-chunk AABB *rasterization* (BackSide boxes + `gl_FragDepth` writeback)
312:   to replace the fullscreen quad once chunk counts grow beyond 25 (`raymarch`
313:   backend only).
314: - LOD: shallower SVO mip levels for distant chunks.
````

736:         // World tuning sliders live display

738:             $(`setting-${knob}`).addEventListener('input', (e) => {

745:         const tabContents = document.querySelectorAll('.tab-content');

747:         tabButtons.forEach(btn => {

780:         $('apply-settings-btn').addEventListener('click', () => {
781:             const params = new URLSearchParams();

787:             }

790:             if (renderer !== 'surface') params.set('renderer', renderer);
791:             const forcedAnomaly = $('setting-force-anomaly').value;
792:             if (forcedAnomaly) params.set('force_anomaly', forcedAnomaly);

794:             // Persist CPU configurations on link
795:             if (Number(prefs.cpuScale) !== 1.0) params.set('cpuScale', prefs.cpuScale);
796:             if (Number(prefs.cpuSplat) !== 12.0) params.set('cpuSplatPx', prefs.cpuSplat);
797:             if (Number(prefs.cpuDist) !== 96.0) params.set('cpuRange', prefs.cpuDist);
798:             if (prefs.cpuShadows !== 'off') params.set('cpuShadows', prefs.cpuShadows);

802:                 // `false`, otherwise the link is not an exact reproduction.
803:                 params.set(`rt_${name}`, enabled ? '1' : '0');
804:             }
805: 
806:             window.location.search = params.toString();
807:         });
808: 
809:         // ---- Boot -----------------------------------------------------------
810:         init().then(() => {
811:             $('settings-btn').style.display = 'block';
812:             applyLivePrefs();
813:         }).catch((err) => {
814:             $('status-msg').textContent = 'Failed to start engine: ' + err;
815:         });
816:     </script>
817: </body>
818: </html>
